secondary.title: A pathogenic AMPAR mutation disrupts hippocampal synapse maturation and homeostasis.
secondary.abstract: AMPA receptors (AMPARs) mediate fast excitatory synaptic transmission and are critical for activity-dependent synapse maturation and circuit development. De novo missense mutations in AMPAR subunits are linked to neurodevelopmental disorders (NDDs), yet how these variants disrupt neuronal function remains unclear. Here, we examine a recurrent pathogenic mutation in the GluA1 subunit (GRIA1 p.A636T) that alters AMPAR function and is associated with autism spectrum disorder (ASD) and intellectual disability (ID). Using GluA1A636T knock-in mice of either sex, we identify impairments in hippocampal-dependent learning and working memory. Quantitative proteomics combined with bulk RNA-seq revealed age-dependent molecular remodeling in mutant hippocampus. Synaptic protein alterations were present in juvenile and adult mice, whereas a pronounced upregulation of mitochondrial and glial-associated proteins emerged more strongly in adulthood. Transcriptomic analyses showed partial concordance and highlighted divergence between RNA and protein regulation. Consistent with these molecular changes, there were increases in markers of oxidative stress in juvenile and adult mutant animals, whereas altered mitochondria morphology emerged selectively in adult mutants. Electrophysiological recordings demonstrated reduced basal excitatory transmission, persistence of silent synapses in adulthood and exaggerated activity-dependent synaptic potentiation, which were associated with reduced spine size consistent with impaired synapse maturation. Together, these findings indicate that a pathogenic AMPAR mutation disrupts developmental synapse maturation with secondary metabolic adaptations emerging over time.Significance Statement Mutations in genes encoding AMPA-type glutamate receptors are increasingly linked to neurodevelopmental disorders, including autism and intellectual disability. However, how these mutations disrupt brain function and development remains poorly understood. Using a mouse model carrying a recurrent disease-associated mutation in the GluA1 AMPA receptor subunit, we show that the presence of this mutant subunit protein impairs the normal maturation of excitatory synapses in the hippocampus. Mutant mice retain immature "silent" synapses into adulthood, exhibit abnormal synaptic plasticity, reduced spine size, and deficits in learning and memory. Molecular analyses reveal age-dependent remodeling of synaptic and mitochondrial proteins, suggesting that metabolic changes arise secondary to disrupted synapse development. These findings clarify how pathogenic AMPA receptor variants alter brain function over time.

secondary.title: Unraveling the Genotype-Phenotype Landscape of Kleefstra Syndrome Through EHMT1 Variant Analysis.
secondary.abstract: BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Kleefstra syndrome type 1 (KLEFS1) is a rare neurodevelopmental disorder caused by pathogenic variants in EHMT1, which play a key role in epigenetic regulation. Core features include global developmental delay (GDD), intellectual disability (ID), facial dysmorphism, congenital heart defects (CHDs), and neuropsychiatric manifestations. METHODS: This retrospective study included patients with KLEFS1 evaluated at Seoul National University Hospital between January 2022 and April 2025. Genetic diagnoses were made using chromosomal microarray or whole-exome or whole-genome sequencing, and clinical data were extracted from medical records. To enhance statistical power, we conducted a joint analysis with established cohorts of at least 30 clinically characterized patients. RESULTS: Among the 15 patients with KLEFS1, 14 (93.3%) exhibited GDD or ID, with frequent comorbidities such as CHDs (8/12, 66.7%), orthopaedic manifestations (6/12, 50.0%), epilepsy (6/15, 40.0%), and sleep problems (4/11, 36.4%). Brain MRI revealed abnormalities in 10 of the 12 patients (83.3%), including pituitary anomalies in 2 (16.7%). By combining our data with recently published multicenter international cohorts, we assessed genotype-phenotype correlations by comparing the clinical features of 202 patients with different variant subtypes. Patients with multigene deletions had a significantly higher prevalence of CHDs (53.5% vs 25.8%, p value = 2 × 10-4), cortical visual impairment (12.5% vs 1.7%, p value = 0.004), microcephaly (37.1% vs 17.8%, p value = 0.009), corpus callosum abnormalities (17.9% vs 5.9%, p value = 0.02), and hearing impairment (39.7% vs 25.6%, p value = 0.04) than those with single-nucleotide variants (SNVs) or short insertions/deletions (indels), in addition to the previously identified features including epilepsy, constipation, and short stature. We also observed that a recurrent EHMT1 variant (p.Arg948Trp), identified in multiple unrelated patients, was linked to significant phenotypic heterogeneity, including late-onset neurocognitive regression. DISCUSSION: Our study showed that patients with multigene deletions are significantly more likely to exhibit multiorgan involvement, including CHDs, cortical visual impairments, microcephaly, corpus callosum abnormalities, and hearing impairments, compared with those with SNVs or indels, emphasizing the importance of genotype-informed management. We report pituitary gland abnormalities in KLEFS1, expanding the phenotypic and neuroimaging spectrum of KLEFS1. The patient showing regression in their 30s necessitates long-term, comprehensive studies to support care.

secondary.title: Along-tract statistical mapping of white matter abnormalities in children with SeLECTS.
secondary.abstract: BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: Emerging evidence suggests that self-limited epilepsy with centrotemporal spikes (SeLECTS) may reflect atypical neurodevelopment. As WM maturation extends from the second trimester through adolescence, this study aimed to identify regions of delayed or aberrant white matter (WM) development in children with SeLECTS using along-tract statistical mapping for precise localization of microstructural alterations. MATERIALS AND METHODS: 38 children with SeLECTS and 31 healthy controls underwent diffusion-weighted MRI scan. Fractional anisotropy (FA), mean diffusivity (MD), and radial diffusivity (RD) were derived from the diffusion tensor model. Whole-brain tractography was performed using deterministic EuDX tracking and registered to a standardized bundle atlas in MNI space. Thirty WM tracts per subject were extracted. Linear mixed models within the BUAN tractometry framework were used to assess segment wise group differences, while partial correlations were performed to evaluate associations between diffusion metrics and cognitive performance. FDR correction was applied per bundle for all comparisons. RESULTS: After FDR correction, children with SeLECTS showed increased MD in the forceps minor, midbody of the corpus callosum, right corticospinal tract, right extreme capsule, and bilateral uncinate fasciculi. MD values in the affected WM segments showed negative correlations with performance and full-scale IQ, and the segments showing significant correlations overlapped with those showing significant group differences. CONCLUSIONS: SeLECTS is associated with MD-based microstructural alterations in superficial frontal, temporal, and parietal pathways, potentially indicating delayed white matter maturation.

secondary.title: Paternal methylphenidate exposure alters sperm miRNAs and induces intergenerational behavioral and transcriptional changes that are largely reversed by washout.
secondary.abstract: Attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) is a neurodevelopmental disorder characterized by inattention, hyperactivity, and impulsivity. Methylphenidate (MPH), a first-line medication, is often used long-term and not routinely discontinued in individuals planning to have children. Guided by the Paternal Origins of Health and Disease framework, in this study, we investigated intergenerational effects of paternal MPH exposure and reversibility of sperm epigenetic changes. Male BALB/c mice received MPH (15 mg/kg) or vehicle for 28 days and were mated with untreated females immediately after treatment (F0-T1) or after a 40-day washout period (F0-T2). Behavioral tests and brain gene expression analyses were conducted in the offspring (F1), and sperm small noncoding RNA (sncRNA) profiles were examined in F0 males. Male offspring in the F0-T1-MPH group showed increased open-arm entry into the elevated plus maze and reduced expression of Maoa, Maob, and Bdnf in the medial prefrontal cortex. These changes were absent in the offspring derived from the F0-T2-MPH group. Sperm sncRNA sequencing identified 5,684 differentially expressed fragments in F0-T1-MPH mice, including marked alterations in miRNA-derived fragments, such as miR-34c-5p and miR-30e-5p. The target genes of these altered miRNAs were enriched in ADHD-related pathways, including axon guidance and Rap1 signaling. After washout, the number of differentially expressed sncRNA fragments decreased to 665, whereas the number of altered miRNA-derived fragments decreased from 383 to 7. These findings suggest that paternal MPH exposure may influence offspring behavior and brain gene expression through sperm miRNA alterations and that these effects are largely reversible following drug withdrawal.

secondary.title: Modeling Progressive Brain Volume Losses in Chronic Moderate Severe Traumatic Brain Injury: Extensive, but Attenuating.
secondary.abstract: OBJECTIVE: Progressive brain atrophy has now been widely observed in the chronic stages of moderate-severe traumatic brain injury (msTBI), but there is only coarse information regarding its prevalence and magnitude, and whether rate of atrophy accelerates or attenuates across time. We examined these questions in a Canadian inception cohort from the Toronto Rehab TBI Recovery Study. METHODS: N = 123 patients with post-traumatic amnesia ranging from > 1 h to 10 weeks (70%, > 7 days) were administered up to three MRIs at approximately 5 months, 1 year, and 3 years post-injury. N = 32 healthy controls were scanned up to two times on average 14 months apart. Ventricle-to-brain ratio (VBR) was calculated and manual segmentation of the hippocampi (HPC), corpus callosum (CC), and substructures was employed. For each region, annualized rates of progressive atrophy were modeled from approximately 5 months to 1 year and 1 to 3 years post-TBI; proportions of patients with annualized volume losses of 2.5%-5%, 5%-10%, and > 10% were estimated. RESULTS: Mixed-effects longitudinal models estimated robust progressive atrophy in both time windows in all regions compared to controls, but with significant attenuation across windows. In the earlier window, > 10% annualized loss was estimated in 76.2% of patients for VBR, 53.2% for CC, and 25.0% for HPC bilaterally. In the later window, at least 5%-10% annualized loss was estimated in 63.3% of patients for VBR, 49.4% for CC, and 17.7% for right HPC; for left HPC, 6.3% of patients showed at least 2.5%-5% annualized decline. INTERPRETATION: Clinically concerning prevalence and degree of progressive volume losses were observed in the chronic stages of msTBI, with tapering of losses across time, and regional variations. Research is needed to understand and mitigate clinical impact of these declines.

secondary.title: Prenatal Maternal Phosphatidylcholine and Children's Behavior and Cognition through 4 Years of Age: Randomized Clinical Trial.
secondary.abstract: BACKGROUND: Increasing popularity of choline supplements may prompt patients to seek advice on safe, effective doses during prenatal visits. Rationale for prenatal phosphatidylcholine supplements stems from the fetal developmental role of α7-nicotinic cholinergic receptor gene CHRNA7, associated with Schizophrenia, Attention Deficit Disorder, and Autism Spectrum Disorder. Fetal brain developmental problems, including those linked to CHRNA7, convey risk for these mental illnesses. Choline derived from maternal phosphatidylcholine intake activates fetal α7-nicotinic receptors, which facilitate brain neurosynaptic development, observed after birth as robust inhibition of cerebral neurophysiological responses to repeated stimuli. A previous study found that maternal prenatal phosphatidylcholine compared to placebo significantly improved newborns' neurophysiology and thereby decreased the children's attention and social withdrawal problems at 40 months of age. OBJECTIVE: To assess whether maternal prenatal phosphatidylcholine compared to placebo in a larger randomized clinical trial supports fetal brain development to decrease childhood attention and social behavioral problems and increase cognitive performance. STUDY DESIGN: A clinical trial at University of Colorado Hospital Prenatal Clinics and affiliated community hospitals randomized 206 women to 9000 mg phosphatidylcholine (the form of choline occurring naturally in food) or placebo from 16 weeks' gestation through delivery. From 18 months to 4 years of age, 142 children were assessed by parents on the Child Behavior Check List 1.5-5-year version (CBCL1.5-5yr). The 2 primary outcomes were Withdrawn and Attention Problems. A secondary outcome was the Wechsler Preschool and Primary Scale of Intelligence-IV Full Scale Intelligence Quotient (Full Scale-IQ). Cerebral neurophysiological inhibition, assessed soon after birth, confirmed phosphatidylcholine's fetal developmental effects. RESULTS: Prenatal phosphatidylcholine supplements compared to placebo produced fewer children with multiple or pervasive Withdrawn problems and increased WPPSI-IV Full-Scale IQ (mean difference 7.78, 95% CI 1.88, 13.7; p = .010). Attention problems did not decrease significantly. In exploratory analyses, 11 children had CBCL1.5-5yr Autism Spectrum T-scores in the clinical referral range and language deficits typical of Autism Spectrum Disorder, 10 of 71 from women who had placebo and 1 of 71 who had phosphatidylcholine, Risk Ratio 10.0; 95% CI 1.31, 76.1; p = .026. Twelve children had Full-Scale IQ > 120 (>90 %ile), 10 of 54 from women who had phosphatidylcholine and 2 of 49 who had placebo, Risk Ratio 4.54; 95% CI 1.05, 19.7; p = .044. Positive effects were observed regardless of presence or absence of maternal mental disorders. Phosphatidylcholine produced no significant adverse effects or safety problems for women or children. Nausea, vomiting, dizziness, and hypertension were not increased. The children had normal physical parameters at birth and through childhood. Several limitations temper the study's findings: effects on Attention problems did not reach significance, parents rated social behavior, and one-third of women were lost between prenatal enrollment and 4-year assessments. CONCLUSION: Prenatal phosphatidylcholine supplements provide safe, effective support of fetal brain development. Comparison of doses from this and previous trials suggests 6300 mg phosphatidylcholine or 900 mg choline, beginning as early as possible in gestation. Outcomes for the children include fewer social withdrawal problems and increased cognitive test performance.

secondary.title: Predictive factors associated with interval changes in STN-DBS lead-tip position between immediate and delayed postoperative CT.
secondary.abstract: BACKGROUND: Brain shift during deep brain stimulation (DBS) surgery may contribute to changes in lead position. Although intracranial air volume is considered an important factor, other intraoperative factors may also influence lead displacement. This study evaluated interval changes in subthalamic nucleus (STN)-DBS lead-tip position between immediate and delayed postoperative computed tomography (CT) and investigated factors associated with these changes, including intracranial air volume and intraoperative head position. METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 42 DBS leads implanted bilaterally in the STN of 21 patients with Parkinson's disease. Lead-tip coordinates were assessed using Elements software (Brainlab) on CT obtained immediately after implantation and after resolution of intracranial air. Interval displacement was defined as the difference in lead-tip coordinates between the delayed and immediate postoperative CT scans. Intraoperative head position was quantified as "Angle A," measured from the horizontal reference line to the anterior commissure-posterior commissure line. Associations between potential explanatory factors and lead-tip displacement were assessed using linear mixed-effects models with patient included as a random intercept to account for within-patient correlation between bilateral leads. RESULTS: Lead-tip positions showed significant interval displacement in the lateral, anterior, and caudal directions. In univariable mixed-effects analysis, intracranial air volume was significantly associated with anterior displacement (β = 0.033, 95% CI 0.018-0.048, p < 0.001), whereas Angle A was not (β = -0.030, 95% CI - 0.067-0.007, p = 0.111). In a multivariable mixed-effects model including intracranial air volume and Angle A, intracranial air volume remained significantly associated with anterior displacement (β = 0.0289, 95% CI 0.0110-0.0469, p = 0.002), while a larger Angle A was associated with less anterior displacement (β = -0.0270, 95% CI - 0.0535 to - 0.0004, p = 0.047). CONCLUSIONS: Intracranial air volume was consistently associated with anterior STN-DBS lead-tip displacement between immediate and delayed postoperative CT. Intraoperative head position was also associated with anterior displacement after adjustment for intracranial air volume, although this finding was of borderline statistical significance and should be considered exploratory. These findings support efforts to minimize intracranial air entry during DBS implantation, while the potential influence of intraoperative head positioning requires further prospective investigation.

secondary.title: Directing Neuronal Differentiation via Calcium-Chirality Synergy in Supramolecular Nanofibers.
secondary.abstract: While chiral supramolecular nanofibrous networks (NFNs) show promise in regulating cell fate, precisely directing differentiation pathways remains challenging. This study systematically investigates the influence of various chiral supramolecular NFNs on neural cell differentiation. A series of chiral supramolecular NFNs was synthesized using L/D-amino acids and their derivatives as building blocks, including L/D-lysine (L/D-Lys), L/D-histidine (L/D-His), L/D-arginine (L/D-Arg), and L/D-glutamic acid derivatives (Fmoc-L/D-Glu). The regulatory effects of these NFNs on the NG108-15 were evaluated during the differentiation process. Our findings demonstrate that the chiral microenvironment established by D-Lys-gel significantly enhances NG108-15 differentiation and correlates with robust activation of the Ca2+ signaling pathway. To further elucidate the relationship between supramolecular chirality and metal ions, we synthesized chiral supramolecular NFNs from L/D-Lys-Ca2+-gel and L/D-Lys-Mg2+-gel. Notably, the supramolecular NFNs derived from D-Lys-Ca2+-gel exhibited superior capacity to promote neurite outgrowth and maturation compared to their L-enantiomer and Mg2+-incorporated counterparts. Proteomics analysis revealed that the chiral supramolecular NFNs obtained from D-Lys-Ca2+-gel enhance neuronal differentiation by upregulating key effectors involved in both axon guidance and calcium signaling pathways, particularly the Camkk2-Tiam1 cascade. This study provides valuable insights into the design of chiral biomaterials and proposes novel strategies for neural regeneration and tissue engineering.

secondary.title: Mapping the knowledge structure and emerging trends of blood-based biomarkers in autism spectrum disorder: A bibliometric analysis (2016-2026).
secondary.abstract: BACKGROUND: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is a clinically heterogeneous neurodevelopmental condition, and its diagnosis still relies mainly on behavioral assessment. Blood-based biomarkers may provide objective support for early detection, biological subgrouping, clinical monitoring, and individualized intervention. However, findings in this field remain dispersed across multiple biological pathways. This study aimed to map the knowledge structure and emerging trends of ASD blood-based biomarker research. METHODS: Publications on ASD blood-based biomarkers from 2016 to 2026 were retrieved from the Web of Science Core Collection. After duplicate removal and eligibility screening, 1785 English-language articles and reviews were included. CiteSpace, VOSviewer, and Microsoft Excel were used to examine publication trends, collaboration networks, influential journals and authors, co-cited references, keyword clusters, and citation bursts. RESULTS: Research output increased steadily, with the United States and China contributing the largest number of publications and the United States showing stronger international connectivity. Co-cited reference and keyword analyses identified oxidative stress, inflammatory cytokines, gut microbiota, metabolomics, mitochondrial respiration, and gastrointestinal symptoms as major knowledge clusters. Recent burst terms, including machine learning, Mendelian randomization, gut-brain axis, innate immunity, sex differences, and neurological disorders, indicate a shift toward causal inference, multi-omics integration, and data-driven biomarker prediction. CONCLUSIONS: ASD blood-based biomarker research has grown steadily over the past decade and is moving from descriptive clinical observations toward mechanistic, multi-omics, and computational approaches. Oxidative stress, mitochondrial dysfunction, gut-brain interactions, inflammatory responses, and machine learning-based prediction now represent major directions in this field. Future studies should focus on multicenter longitudinal cohorts, standardized analytical workflows, detailed clinical phenotyping, and independent validation to improve reproducibility and support clinical translation.

secondary.title: A geometric rs-fMRI connectome descriptor reveals individual stability without robust autism group differences.
secondary.abstract: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) has resisted reproducible case-control characterization in resting-state functional connectivity, leaving open whether reported group differences reflect genuine biology or methodological variability. We introduce a geometric framework that represents functional connectomes on the symmetric positive-definite Riemannian manifold and quantifies individual deviation as tangent-space dispersion, complemented by normative modeling of graph topology. Using the multi-site Autism Brain Imaging Data Exchange (ABIDE I) cohort (N=1035 subjects), we evaluate this descriptor under stringent robustness conditions and report three findings. First, individual connectome geometry is a stable, individually unique descriptor. The magnitude of a subject's deviation is highly reliable across split halves (intraclass correlation ICC[Formula: see text]) but is dominated by an acquisition-site scale, whereas its high-dimensional shape identifies subjects within-session with 98.9% accuracy once that scale is removed. Second, the case-control difference in dispersion is null and, by two one-sided equivalence tests against Cohen's d = 0.2, statistically equivalent to zero in all ABIDE I analysis cohorts (full cohort d = -0.007, N = 1035; strict cohort d = +0.038, N = 635); a nominal single-atlas effect (dispersion ratio 1.05, p = 0.046) does not survive multi-atlas reanalysis. Third, acquisition site explains 69% of dispersion variance while diagnosis explains 0.0001%; deviations form no discrete subtypes and do not predict symptom severity (minimum p=0.15 across tested graph-deviation predictors). Geometric dispersion is therefore a reproducible, individually unique connectome descriptor but not a case-control biomarker of ASD, which helps to explain the inconsistency of connectomic findings in autism.

secondary.title: Identification of EIF4A1 as a candidate molecular indicator of autism spectrum disorder using integrative bioinformatic and biological methods.
secondary.abstract: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is a heterogeneous neurodevelopmental condition with complex genetic and molecular mechanism. Identifying reliable molecular biomarkers remains a critical challenge. In this study, we integrated mRNA expression profiles from five post-mortem brain tissue GEO datasets to identify ASD-associated genes. Following batch effect correction, differentially expressed genes (DEGs) were analysed and Weighted Gene Co-expression Network Analysis (WGCNA) was performed to screen genes correlated with ASD. Then, five machine learning algorithms - Random Forest, LASSO, Boruta, CatBoost, and LightGBM - were applied to screen hub genes. Lastly, alterations of the hub gene(s) were investigated with a maternal immune activation (MIA) rat model using poly I:C by measuring mRNA expression of the hub genes in the rat nucleus accumbens (NAc) and caudate putamen (CPu). A total of 30 DEGs and 54 WGCNA module genes were identified, yielding 29 key candidates by intersecting these two gene sets. EIF4A1 (Eukaryotic Translation Initiation Factor 4A1) was the sole gene consistently ranked among the top five by all five machine learning algorithms. Analysis of the integrated dataset confirmed that EIF4A1 mRNA expression was significantly elevated in ASD subjects. Finally, using the MIA rat model of ASD, we found that EIF4A1 mRNA expression was significantly down-regulated in the NAc and CPu, and this deficit was rescued by treatment with the antipsychotics olanzapine or risperidone. In conclusion, the present study positions EIF4A1 as a promising candidate molecular indicator with potential implications for understanding disease mechanisms and developing targeted interventions of ASD.

secondary.title: Glabridin and glabrene from Glycyrrhiza glabra L. as natural Co-operative modulators of the human serotonin transporter: Evidence from docking, molecular simulations and machine-learning QSAR models.
secondary.abstract: Serotonin transporter (SERT), encoded by SLC6A4, is a key regulator of serotonergic neurotransmission and a primary target for selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors (SSRIs). Dysregulation of SERT is implicated in neuropsychiatric and neurodevelopmental disorders, including autism spectrum disorder (ASD). SSRIs, while widely used, have limitations such as adverse effects, drug-drug interactions, and interindividual variability, necessitating safer and mechanistically distinct SERT modulators. This study utilized an integrative in-silico approach to evaluate the SERT inhibitory potential of glabridin, glabrene, and liquiritigenin the phytoestrogens from Glycyrrhiza glabra (licorice), known for neuroprotective properties. Blind and site-specific molecular docking, molecular dynamics simulations, binding free energy calculations, ADMET profiling, and machine learning-based QSAR modeling were employed to characterize ligand-transporter interactions. The compounds glabridin and glabrene exhibited favorable binding affinity for the central S1 substrate-binding site of human SERT, with a comparable or superior binding free energy (-50.35 kcal/mol and -52.41 kcal/mol, respectively) to the reference SSRI paroxetine (-53.04 kcal/mol). The 100 ns MD simulations confirmed stable ligand occupancy and persistent interactions with key residues involved in extracellular gate regulation, stabilizing the SERT outward-open inhibitory conformation. ADMET predictions indicated favorable pharmacokinetic properties, including blood-brain barrier permeability and acceptable toxicity profiles of glabridin and glabrene. QSAR-derived IC50 estimates and combination modeling revealed nonantagonistic, mild positive cooperativity between glabridin and glabrene, supported by dual-ligand docking and MM-GBSA analyses, suggesting complementary orthosteric engagement. These findings position glabridin and glabrene as putative natural SERT modulators, providing a mechanistic basis for their potential use in serotonergic modulation therapeutics, warranting further experimental validation.

secondary.title: Glycerol Phenylbutyrate Treatment in a Pediatric Cohort of SLC6A1-Related Neurodevelopmental Disorder.
secondary.abstract: BACKGROUND: The SLC6A1 gene encodes the gamma-aminobutyric acid transporter 1 protein, which facilitates the reuptake of gamma-aminobutyric acid from the synaptic cleft in inhibitory synapses back into presynaptic neurons and glial cells. SLC6A1 haploinsufficiency leads to neurodevelopmental impairment including epilepsy, movement disorders, intellectual disability, and autism spectrum disorder. SLC6A1-related neurodevelopmental disorder (SLC6A1-NDD) is a rare condition with autosomal dominant inheritance for which there is no cure. Acting as a chemical chaperone, glycerol phenylbutyrate, used for urea cycle disorders, can cross the blood-brain barrier and increase GABA transporter 1 surface cell expression in animal and in vitro models. This research aimed to review the clinical characteristics of a cohort of pediatric patients with SLC6A1-related neurodevelopmental disorder (SLC6A1-NDD) in Spain and to assess the efficacy and safety of glycerol phenylbutyrate treatment. METHODS: We have conducted retrospective review of the clinical characteristics of SLC6A1-NDD pediatric patients from 13 hospitals in Spain and investigated the efficacy and safety of glycerol phenylbutyrate treatment. RESULTS: Fourteen patients were included in the cohort, out of which eleven were treated with glycerol phenylbutyrate. A significant reduction in the number of epileptic seizures was observed in 80% of patients with uncontrolled seizures at baseline and 40% became seizure-free. A clear improvement in video-electroencephalogram abnormalities was evident in 64%, while 27.2% experienced cognitive improvement and 36.3% showed significantly improved psychiatric manifestations. Seven of the eleven treated patients experienced some side effects from which three has discontinued the treatment. CONCLUSIONS: Glycerol phenylbutyrate treatment is relatively well tolerated, and although it is effective in reducing the frequency of seizures and improving video-electroencephalogram abnormalities, it is less effective in ameliorating cognitive and psychiatric manifestations.

secondary.title: Sex-dependent effects of imperatorin on autistic-like behaviors and BDNF signaling in rats prenatally exposed to valproic acid.
secondary.abstract: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is defined by cognitive impairments such as learning and memory decline, and social interaction and communication deficits. This study investigated the potential effects of Imperatorin (IMP), a furocoumarin and a phytochemical isolated from the leaves of Ferulago trifida on valproic acid (VPA)-induced behavioral and brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF) alterations in a rat model of ASD. Open field test (locomotion, anxiety), grooming test, marble burying test (OCD-like behavior), novel object recognition memory test, and real-time PCR (BDNF levels) were conducted to collect data. The results showed increased locomotion in ASD-like rats in both sexes with greater effect in females, while IMP restored it in males and decreased it in females. Anxiety was increased in ASD-like rats in both sexes with greater effect in females; IMP had no effect. Grooming was increased in ASD-like rats in both sexes with greater effect in females, while IMP restored it in males and decreased it in females. Marbles buried was increased in ASD-like rats in both sexes, while IMP decreased it in males. Memory was impaired in ASD-like rats in both sexes; IMP had no effect. BDNF was decreased in ASD-like rats in both sexes with greater effect in females, while IMP increased it in both sexes. In conclusion, our findings showed hyperlocomotion, anxiety-like behavior, OCD-like behavior, memory deficit, and BDNF downregulation as ASD-related features, with evidence of sex-specific patterns and partial therapeutic effects of IMP.

secondary.title: Metabolic and microstructural brain alterations associated with occupational blast exposure.
secondary.abstract: Repeated occupational exposure to low-level blast may pose a risk to the neurological health of service members. To date, no studies have specifically investigated the effects of such repetitive exposure using fluorodeoxyglucose positron emission tomography (FDG-PET). This study aims to characterize cerebral metabolic alterations associated with occupational blast exposure, accounting for confounding factors such as posttraumatic stress disorder (PTSD) symptoms and aging. Male service members with chronic mild TBI (mTBI) were categorized into high-risk (HR; n = 204) and low-risk (LR; n = 68) blast exposure groups based on their military occupational specialty. FDG-PET and diffusion tensor imaging (DTI) data were analyzed using region-of-interest (ROI) and voxelwise methods. Statistical models included age and PTSD symptom severity as covariates. Compared to the LR group, ROI analyses revealed higher FDG uptake in the left pallidum, caudate, and ventrolateral prefrontal cortex in the HR group. These elevations in metabolic activity may reflect compensatory mechanisms in response to neurophysiological disruption following blast exposure. Voxelwise analysis showed lower FDG uptake in the HR group within white matter, predominantly in the right hemisphere, including the corpus callosum, anterior thalamic radiation, inferior and superior longitudinal fasciculi. Corresponding DTI findings showed higher fractional anisotropy (p = 0.0025) and axial diffusivity (p = 0.024) in these regions. Furthermore, leftward metabolic lateralization was observed in the pallidum, with the HR group (Cohen's d = 1.36, 95% CI [1.14, 1.57]) exhibiting greater metabolic asymmetry than the LR group (Cohen's d = 1.16, 95% CI [0.79, 1.51]). Findings from this study reveal metabolic and microstructural alterations associated with occupational blast exposure in service members with mTBI.

secondary.title: Increased inflammatory cytokines in the temporal cortex in autism spectrum disorder.
secondary.abstract: Alterations in immune and neuroinflammatory processes are evident in neurodevelopmental disorders such as autism spectrum disorders (ASD). While prior studies using cerebrospinal fluid and plasma/serum have identified differences in cytokine levels in ASD when compared with controls, specific changes in postmortem human brain tissue remains poorly characterized. The superior temporal gyrus (STG) is involved in social communication and sensory processing, and is affected in ASD, making it a relevant region for investigating immune-related differences that has not been previously studied. Neuroimmune profiles were measured in STG tissue from 46 postmortem cases: ASD (n = 17), and neurotypical controls (n = 29). Fresh-frozen samples were collected using biopsy punches, and cytokines, chemokines, and growth factors were quantified using multiplexed bead immunoassays. In ASD cases, there were significantly increased levels of inflammatory cytokines in IL-1α, IL-8, IL-18, FLT-3L, FGF-2, G-CSF, M-CSF, MCP3, PDGF-AA and GROa compared to controls. In contrast, there was a significant decrease in RANTES, IFNα2 and IL-4 cytokine levels in ASD. Overall, ASD presented a distinctive STG cytokine profile with increased pro-inflammatory cytokine levels in the absence of an immune regulatory balance. These data highlights that unique neuroimmune pathways occur in neurodevelopmental disorders such as ASD offering insights into potential therapeutic targets.

secondary.title: Dual-target deep brain stimulation for severe pediatric autism: Sustained core symptom reduction in a 12-month case study.
secondary.abstract: OBJECTIVE: Core autism spectrum disorder (ASD) symptoms lack effective interventions. While single-target DBS helps comorbid conditions, it fails to improve social deficits. Here we aimed to explore the efficacy of bilateral dual-target DBS targeting the anterior limb of the internal capsule (ALIC) and nucleus accumbens (NAcc) in a pediatric severe ASD patient. METHODS: A 9-year-old girl diagnosed with ASD, presenting with severe symptoms and intellectual disability, underwent bilateral NAcc/ALIC DBS implantation. Standardized assessments, including Autism Treatment Evaluation Checklist (ATEC), Repetitive Behavior Scale-Revised (RBS-R), Autism Behavior Checklist (AuBC), and Childhood Autism Rating Scale-2 (CARS-2), were performed pre-operatively and at 3, 6, 9 and 12 months postoperatively. RESULTS: Clinical assessments revealed significant improvement in core ASD symptoms by the 3-month postoperative evaluation. Specifically, ATEC scores decreased by 65.9%, RBS-R by 85.7%, AuBC by 69.4% and CARS-2 by 17.5%. These benefits persisted for the 12 months follow-up period with the last assessment showing ATEC reduced by 81.3%, RBS-R by 96.4%, AuBC by 86.5%, and CARS-2 by 21.3%. No adverse events occurred. CONCLUSIONS: Bilateral dual-target ALIC-NAcc DBS was feasibility and safety, and resulted in sustained improvement in the core features of severe ASD. SIGNIFICANCE: The present results suggest DBS targeting ALIC and NAcc is a promising neurotherapeutic strategy for ASD.

secondary.title: Associations between chronic placental inflammation, fetal brain development and later autism traits.
secondary.abstract: Prenatal inflammation is a recognized risk factor for autism spectrum disorder (ASD), but the neural pathways linking in utero immune exposure to later outcomes remain unclear. We examined whether chronic placental inflammation (CPI), a sustained immune response within the placenta, is associated with fetal brain functional connectivity differences and later ASD traits. A cohort of 105 pregnant individuals (85.7% African American/Black, 1.0% Asian American, 4.8% Bi-racial, 4.8% White, 1.0% Other, 2.9% Missing) underwent fetal resting-state fMRI between 24 and 38 weeks' gestation. After delivery, placental tissues were evaluated by expert pathologists for CPI lesions. Fetuses exposed to CPI (n = 44) showed significant differences in resting-state functional connectivity (RSFC) compared to non-exposed fetuses (n = 61) across ten network pairs, with the greatest effects in prefrontal, cerebellar, visual, and motor regions. These connectivity differences were associated with behavioral outcomes: cerebellar-medial visual RSFC was the strongest prenatal predictor of ASD traits at age 3. An exploratory structural equation modeling indicated that CPI was associated with reduced cerebellum-medial visual RSFC, which was associated with higher ASD trait scores, though the indirect pathway did not reach statistical significance. This study provides the first human evidence that chronic placental inflammation is associated with large-scale fetal brain network differences that are also associated with autism traits, suggesting that prenatal immune activity may be relevant to neurodevelopmental trajectories.

secondary.title: Graph neural network-based modeling of functional brain connectivity in autism spectrum disorder using the ABIDE-I and II datasets.
secondary.abstract: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is a neurodevelopmental condition characterized by atypical large-scale brain network organization. Using the comprehensive Autism Brain Imaging Data Exchange (ABIDE-I and ABIDE-II; n = 2013 participants), this study systematically evaluated three representative graph neural network (GNN) architectures for ASD classification based on resting-state functional MRI. The Graph Convolutional Network (GCN), Graph Attention Network (GAT), and Self-Attention Graph Pooling (SAGPool) models were applied to graph representations of functional connectivity among 200 brain regions, following standardized preprocessing and ComBat harmonization. Across 100 repetitions of 10-fold stratified cross-validation, all three models achieved consistent and reproducible accuracy (∼61% balanced accuracy), establishing a robust performance benchmark for connectome-based ASD classification. Permutation-based feature importance analysis revealed convergent brain regions across models, including the bilateral thalamus, right superior temporal gyrus, right middle occipital gyrus, and bilateral precuneus, which are involved in sensory integration, social cognition, and default mode network functioning. These findings indicate that distinct GNN architectures converge on common neurobiological signatures of ASD, highlighting their potential for reliable brain network modeling and biomarker discovery in psychiatry research.

secondary.title: Therapeutic potential of edaravone and flurbiprofen in valproic acid-induced autism: Targeting oxidative stress and neuroinflammation.
secondary.abstract: BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) presents significant therapeutic challenges, with growing evidence implicating neuroinflammation and oxidative stress in its pathophysiology. This study aimed to investigate the protective effects of edaravone and flurbiprofen, administered alone and in combination, in a valproic acid (VPA)-induced autism model in male rats. MATERIALS AND METHODS: An autism model was established through prenatal VPA exposure. Social behavior, anxiety, and memory were assessed using a battery of standardized behavioral tests. Pro-inflammatory and oxidative stress markers were evaluated via ELISA, and hippocampal neuronal density was assessed by Nissl staining. RESULTS: All treatment groups (edaravone, flurbiprofen, and their combination) showed significant improvements in autism-related behaviors, including enhanced social interaction, reduced memory deficits, and decreased anxiety. The treatments lowered pro-inflammatory cytokines (IL-6, TNF-α) and MDA levels, while restoring the activity of antioxidant enzymes GPX and SOD. CONCLUSIONS: Edaravone and flurbiprofen effectively improved autism-like behaviors by targeting shared pathways of oxidative stress and neuroinflammation. However, the combination therapy offered no additive benefits over monotherapy. This finding suggests that monotherapy with either drug is sufficient to achieve maximal therapeutic effects, a point with significant implications for future treatment strategies in ASD. SIGNIFICANCE STATEMENT: This study advances neurodevelopmental neuroscience by demonstrating that independently targeting oxidative stress or neuroinflammation achieves maximal behavioral and hippocampal rescue in an autism model, revealing a convergent therapeutic ceiling that challenges combinatorial polypharmacy and refines our understanding of how overlapping pathological pathways govern neural circuit dysfunction and functional recovery.

secondary.title: The effect of sex on sleep neurophysiology in typical and altered neurodevelopment.
secondary.abstract: STUDY OBJECTIVES: Sleep electroencephalography (EEG) patterns exhibit complex variations influenced by multiple factors, including age and sex. While sex effects in sleep neurophysiology are well-described in adults, evidence in pediatric populations is limited, particularly in the context of neurodevelopmental disorders (NDDs). METHODS: Here, we analyzed a large pediatric clinical dataset to examine sex differences in whole-night sleep EEG among children without NDDs (N = 1523, 2.5-17.5 years) and those with autism spectrum disorder (ASD,N = 196), attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD,N = 523), and intellectual disabilities (IntDis,N = 167). We investigated sleep macro- and microarchitecture, including spectral power, density and morphology of spindles and slow oscillations, and their temporal coupling. RESULTS: Significant sex differences in the non-NDD sample were observed across features of sleep macroarchitecture, spectral power, sleep spindles, and slow oscillations, with the majority of findings replicated in an independent cohort. More specifically, non-NDD boys exhibited more fragmented sleep compared to girls, but this pattern was not observed among children with NDDs. In contrast, fast spindle density was lower in boys regardless of NDD diagnosis, which may contribute to males' increased susceptibility to developing NDDs. No sex differences were observed in EEG-based brain age predictions. Medical record analysis revealed limited sex differences in the prevalence of sleep disorders. We found strong evidence of altered sleep EEG characteristics in boys and girls with IntDis. Several sleep EEG metrics showed nominal group-by-sex interactions with ASD and ADHD girls displaying more pronounced alterations, pointing to a varying degree of sleep disturbance. CONCLUSIONS: Our findings demonstrate that many sleep EEG features exhibit significant sex differences during childhood, but these differences may be distinct in NDD populations. The sex-specific sleep alterations in NDDs highlight the potential importance of considering sex in pediatric sleep research.

primary.title: CHCHD2 mitigates age-associated proteostatic collapse by maintaining homeostasis of the mitochondria-lysosome axis.
primary.abstract: Mutations in coiled-coil-helix-coiled-coil-helix domain containing 2 (CHCHD2), including the Parkinson's disease (PD)-linked CHCHD2T61I mutation, are associated with Lewy body disorders (LBDs) by unknown mechanisms. Here, we demonstrate that CHCHD2T61I exacerbates age-related brain pathologies, including axonal degeneration and cognitive deficits, by disrupting the mitochondria-lysosome axis. Specifically, CHCHD2T61I binds and reduces cathepsin B (CTSB) and cathepsin L (CTSL) levels, inducing lysosomal membrane permeability and impairing α-synuclein fibril clearance. We also demonstrate that human CHCHD2 declines in the brain with age, while expression of wild-type CHCHD2 safeguards against age-related neuroinflammation, dopaminergic neuron loss, insoluble protein aggregation, and structural deterioration of mitochondria and lysosomes. These findings, supported by observed reductions in CTSB and CHCHD2 in human LBD brains, establish CHCHD2 as a key regulator of neuronal resilience to aging and proteostatic collapse via the mitochondria-lysosome axis. Preventing age-associated CHCHD2 decline offers a therapeutic strategy to preserve brain health throughout aging.

primary.title: Dysregulated cholesterol trafficking through ABCA1 drives neurodegeneration in Parkinson's disease.
primary.abstract: Although brain cholesterol dysregulation is implicated in Parkinson's disease (PD), targeting cholesterol synthesis has shown limited efficacy. Here we identify ATP-binding cassette transporter A1 (ABCA1) as a critical regulator of cholesterol homeostasis in PD. We show that ABCA1 expression is elevated in the substantia nigra of postmortem PD brains and in a PD mouse model, with regional analyses revealing preferential alterations in nigral and striatal circuits. Mechanistically, astrocytic ABCA1 drives excessive cholesterol efflux in mice, promoting neuronal cholesterol overload. In neurons, ABCA1 localizes to lysosomes, where it facilitates cholesterol import, leading to cholesterol accumulation, autophagy impairment and α-synuclein pathology. Genetic silencing of Abca1 in either astrocytes or dopaminergic neurons attenuates neurodegeneration and behavioral deficits in vivo. Furthermore, we identify magnesium citrate as an ABCA1 inhibitor and show that it reduces dopaminergic neuronal loss in a PD mouse model. Our findings identify an ABCA1-dependent cholesterol pathway underlying PD pathogenesis and support ABCA1 inhibition as a potential disease-modifying strategy.

primary.title: Endosome-associated Rab GTPases control distinct aspects of neural circuit assembly.
primary.abstract: Neural circuit assembly relies on the precise regulation of cell-surface receptors that mediate signaling and adhesion. Endocytosis controls receptor activity and availability by internalizing and routing proteins through early endosomes to one of two main pathways: recycling back to the cell-surface or delivery to lysosomes for degradation. Rab GTPases direct receptors into these distinct pathways, but their specific contributions to circuit formation remain opaque. Using clonal analyses with null alleles, we dissected the roles of Rab-mediated trafficking to early, late, and recycling endosomes across multiple stages of circuit assembly in vivo. Our approach revealed that Rab5 and Rab11 regulate extensive and largely distinct developmental events, highlighting the pivotal roles of early endosome sorting and recycling pathways in circuit assembly. As neurons mature, both the spatial distribution and abundance of specific endocytic compartments change to reflect evolving trafficking demands. Our findings underscore how distinct post-endocytic trafficking fates are necessary to build neural circuits.

primary.title: Autolysosomal enhancer GHF201 attenuates pathophysiology in a mucopolysaccharidosis type I mouse model.
primary.abstract: Mucopolysaccharidosis type I (MPS-I) is a hereditary lysosomal storage disorder caused by deficiency in the lysosomal enzyme α-L-iduronidase (IDUA) leading to pathogenic over-accumulation of glycosaminoglycans (GAGs), major constituent of connective tissue and mediators of cell signaling. We tested the therapeutic efficacy of the autolysosomal activator GHF201 in the Idua -/- mouse model of MPS-I. We show that GHF201 reduced GAGs and increased cathepsin activity in Idua -/- mouse embryonic fibroblasts (MEFs) and brain cells. In vivo GHF201 improved aberrant locomotion and behavior, reduced interstitial cathepsins in joints and liver, increased systemic catabolism, corrected bone dysplasia, increased autophagic flux, and ameliorated CNS neurodegeneration and neuroinflammation. GHF201 also reduced brain N-glycans, which are degraded in lysosomes. In conclusion, the lysosomal and autophagic activator GHF201 was demonstrated to improve various pathophysiological parameters in MPS-I-modeling Idua -/- female mice. Our results suggest that GHF201 can complement the inadequate Aldurazyme enzyme replacement therapy as an add-on therapy.

primary.title: Lysosomal multi-omics reveals altered sphingolipid catabolism associated with lysosomal dysfunction in the aging brain.
primary.abstract: Lipids dynamically reside in multiple intracellular locations, and their organellar distribution is important for function. During brain aging, lysosomal lipid changes have been noted, but lipid identity, interactions, and functional relevance have not been characterized. We used mass spectrometry to assess longitudinal changes in the lipidome and proteome of lysosomal fractions from the murine cortex, from 3 to 24 months, followed by multi-omics factor analysis (MOFA) to identify factors underlying lysosomal aging. Our data uncover an age-dependent increase in lysosomal abundance of lipid and protein myelin components and suggest altered sphingolipid catabolism favoring degradation of sphingomyelins over glycosphingolipids. We experimentally corroborate MOFA predictions to demonstrate that age-dependent accumulation of myelin-derived glycosphingolipids is associated with lysosomal enlargement and dysfunction and is most pronounced in microglia. Our findings suggest that age-related lysosomal lipidome changes resemble those observed in lysosomal storage diseases and underscore the importance of organelle-specific analyses for elucidating lipid function.

primary.title: Astrocytic cathepsin D promotes α-synuclein processing and Lewy neurite-like aggregate maturation.
primary.abstract: Parkinson's disease (PD) and related synucleinopathies are marked by the accumulation and propagation of α-synuclein (α-syn) aggregates, a process primarily studied in neurons. Whether astrocytes actively contribute to α-syn processing and intercellular transfer remains unclear. Here, using a physiologically relevant neuron-astrocyte co-culture system that recapitulates tripartite synapse architecture, we show that astrocytes process α-syn and influence the morphological maturation of neuronal aggregates. Astrocytes internalize α-syn pre-formed fibrils (PFFs) and generate C-terminally truncated α-syn species via a Cathepsin D (CtsD)-dependent process. PFF-loaded astrocytes transfer α-syn-containing material to neurons and promote the formation and maturation of pS129-α-syn-positive Lewy neurite (LN)-like aggregates. Notably, α-syn PFF exposure induces lysosomal membrane damage, a senescence-like reactive state, and CtsD upregulation in astrocytes. Although PFF-containing lysosomes undergo autophagic engulfment, they persist within astrocytes, and a subset is detected beyond the astrocytic membrane boundary. Together, our findings support a model in which astrocytic lysosomal remodeling of internalized α-syn contributes to the morphological maturation and intercellular propagation of neuronal α-syn pathology in this co-culture system.

primary.title: BAG3 coordinates astrocytic proteostasis of Alzheimer's disease-linked proteins via proteasome, autophagy, and retromer interactions.
primary.abstract: Bcl-2-associated athanogene 3 (BAG3) is a mediator of chaperone-assisted selective autophagy, and in the brain, is most highly expressed in astrocytes. However, its role in astrocytes remains poorly defined. Given the genetic and pathological links of BAG3 to proteostasis and neurodegenerative diseases, we investigated how BAG3 contributes to astrocyte function and Alzheimer's disease (AD). To define its function and relevance, we used single-nucleus RNA sequencing to confirm BAG3 enrichment in astrocytes and employed CRISPR/Cas9 editing of human induced pluripotent stem cells followed by proteomic and transcriptomic profiling, which revealed that BAG3 loss caused greater disruption in astrocytes than in neurons. BAG3-deficient astrocytes displayed reduced autophagy, lysosomal abundance and activity, and proteasome function. Coimmunoprecipitation identified BAG3 known binding partners (e.g., HSPB8, proteasome regulators), as well as an interactor in the retromer complex, VPS35. BAG3 deficiency resulted in altered retromer activity as measured by amyloid precursor protein (APP) localization in endosomes. In addition to validating these binding partners, integrative -omics analyses showed that BAG3 regulates AD-relevant proteins (GFAP, BIN1), as well as HSPB8. Functionally, BAG3 knockout astrocytes exhibited impaired amyloid-β proteostasis when cocultured with APP/PSEN1 mutant neurons, directly linking BAG3 to a disease-relevant astrocyte phenotype. Finally, analysis of postmortem human brain revealed that BAG3 expression marks a stress-responsive astrocyte subtype in aged individuals. Together, these findings demonstrate that BAG3 coordinates astrocyte proteostasis through interactions with regulators of autophagy, proteasome activity, and retromer function, positioning it as a potential therapeutic target and central node of astrocytic protein quality control in neurodegeneration.

primary.title: PTPRS mediates invasion of tetanus neurotoxin into the central nervous system.
primary.abstract: Tetanus neurotoxin (TeNT) invades the central nervous system (CNS) via retrograde transport through motoneurons. Whether a host factor is needed to mediate TeNT trafficking has remained unknown. Here, using pull-down and mass spectrometry analysis, and by developing a luciferase-based in vivo transport assay, we identify receptor protein tyrosine phosphatase sigma (PTPRS; PTPσ) as the retrograde transport receptor for TeNT. Global or motoneuron-specific PTPRS knockout (KO) abolishes TeNT entry into the CNS in mouse models. PTPRS-TeNT interactions occur in endosomes, prevent toxin translocation, and direct TeNT trafficking in neurons. Structural studies establish that the TeNT light chain and belt region bind to the immunoglobulin domain of PTPRS. Disrupting TeNT-PTPRS interactions blocks TeNT trafficking into the spinal cord; consistently, a PTPRS-binding-deficient TeNT mutant induces botulism-like flaccid paralysis. Thus, PTPRS is the host factor mediating TeNT trafficking into the CNS, revealing a targetable pathway for post-entry intervention and drug delivery into the CNS.

primary.title: Human microglia clear intraneuronal α-synuclein aggregates by GPNMB-mediated trogocytosis.
primary.abstract: Microglia are the primary immune cells of the brain, but their role in Parkinson's disease is not fully understood. Chronic microglial activation is toxic to neurons, but in the early stages of pathology, microglia also exert beneficial functions. We used induced pluripotent stem cell (iPSC)-derived coculture models to investigate how human microglia respond to α-synuclein aggregates that form de novo inside human dopaminergic neurons with α-synuclein gene triplication or are triggered by fibrils. We found that microglia cleared Ser129-phosphorylated α-synuclein aggregates through a contact-dependent mechanism. This process was fine-tuned by sensing (P2RY12) and inhibitory (CD22) signals and involved selective phagocytosis of neuronal subcompartments (trogocytosis), independently of TREM2 or phosphatidylserine. In the presence of intraneuronal α-synuclein aggregates, microglia exhibited morphological and transcriptional changes indicative of activation. Using single-cell sequencing, we identified a cluster of disease-associated microglia (DAM) responsible for this beneficial phenotype and the Parkinson's disease GWAS candidate glycoprotein nonmetastatic melanoma protein B (GPNMB) as a key effector of aggregate clearance by microglial lysosomes. GPNMB interacted with Ser129-phosphorylated α-synuclein in iPSC-derived microglia exposed to aggregate-laden dopaminergic neurons and was up-regulated in substantia nigra microglia of individuals with incidental Lewy bodies or Parkinson's disease. Microglia-specific GPNMB knockdown using CRISPRi reduced intraneuronal aggregate clearance. GPNMB-mediated trogocytosis was negatively regulated by an autocrine IL-10 signaling loop, whereas IL-10 receptor blockade enhanced the phagocytic response. Together, our study identifies a subtype of human microglia capable of removing intraneuronal aggregates and potential therapeutic targets.

primary.title: Batten disease protein CLN8 enables a non-canonical phospholipid synthesis pathway.
primary.abstract: According to text book knowledge, de novo glycerophospholipid (GPL) synthesis begins with the acylation of glycerol-3-phosphate to form phosphatidic acid, the precursor of all other GPLs. Here we describe an alternative GPL synthesis pathway that starts with the acyl-CoA-dependent acylation of glycerophosphoglycerol, resulting in the formation of lysophosphatidylglycerol. The acyltransferase reaction is catalysed by the Batten disease-associated protein ceroid lipofuscinosis neuronal 8 (CLN8). Tracer studies revealed that CLN8-derived lysophosphatidylglycerol is selectively converted into bis(monoacylglycero)phosphate (BMP), a GPL essential for lysosomal lipid homeostasis but not into phosphatidylglycerol or cardiolipin. CLN8-knockout cells and mice cannot utilize glycerophosphoglycerol for BMP synthesis, resulting in BMP deficiency and excess accumulation of phospholipids in lysosomes. The lipid synthesis pathway described herein is relevant for understanding lysosomal lipid metabolism and the pathogenesis of neurodegenerative diseases. BMP deficiency may contribute to or even underlie lysosomal cargo accumulation in certain forms of Batten disease and other lysosomal storage disorders.

primary.title: Early reduction of myelin-associated glycoprotein at myelin membranes in Huntington's disease.
primary.abstract: Huntington's disease (HD) is marked by progressive neuronal loss and atrophy of grey matter structures, particularly the caudate and putamen. Brain imaging studies reveal that the white matter starts to decay in the brain of individuals bearing the HD mutation many years before symptomatic onset. However, the mechanism by which the HD mutation causes white matter loss remains to be further defined. In this study, we examined white matter pathology and explored the underlying mechanism in the HDQ140 knock-in mouse model of HD. Western blot analysis of proteins localized at different layers of the myelin sheath showed that myelin-associated glycoprotein (MAG), which is localized at the innermost myelin layer, was decreased earlier than proteins localized at outer layers of the myelin. The loss of MAG occurred at fully myelinated axons and was progressive with age. In postmortem symptomatic human HD brains, the level of MAG as well as other myelin proteins was also decreased. In HD mouse brains, MAG labeling was reduced at fiber bundles but accumulated in perinuclear structures of cells that expressed breast carcinoma amplified sequence 1, a marker for new oligodendrocytes. While their abundance was normal, new oligodendrocytes in HD brains were impeded in acquiring the expression of MAG. Compared with those in wild-type mouse brains, oligodendrocytes in HD mouse brains had a reduced frequency of MAG-bearing small vesicles and an increased abundance and enlargement of MAG-containing perinuclear structures. Further studies suggest that the MAG-accumulating perinuclear structures were derived from the late endosomal lysosomal compartment. Our study suggests that white matter decay in HD brains involves an early progressive loss of MAG in myelin membranes.

primary.title: RYR:ATP6V0A1 complexes couple ER-lysosome contact sites to dynamic autophagy control.
primary.abstract: Ryanodine receptors (RYRs) are ER-resident Ca2+-release channels enriched in excitable cells, including neurons. RYR hyperactivity is implicated in early pathogenesis of disorders such as Alzheimer's disease (AD), which is associated with impaired autophagy. We recently uncovered a mechanism linking RYR activity to lysosome availability for autophagy. RYRs localize to ER-lysosome contact sites via direct binding to ATP6V0A1, a V-ATPase subunit that also suppresses RYR-mediated Ca2+ release. In human iPSC-derived cortical neurons, spontaneous RYR activity promotes lysosomal secretion, depleting the intracellular lysosomal pool and inhibiting autophagic flux. RYR inhibition promotes ERlysosome contacts, limits lysosomal secretion, and restores lysosome availability for autophagosome fusion and cargo degradation (including APP). Conversely, disrupting the RYR:ATP6V0A1 interaction using a RYR-derived protein fragment serving as a "decoy" for ATP6V0A1 evokes RYR hyperactivity and stimulates lysosomal secretion. In this Punctum, we discuss how this RYR2:ATP6V0A1 "contact-site hub" may be perturbed in disease and highlight open questions on how lysosomes decode RYR-derived Ca2+ signals.

secondary.title: β-Adducin Restrains PLA2G4A-Dependent Lysosomal Membrane Permeabilization and Neuronal Death in Ischemic Stroke.
secondary.abstract: Failure to preserve vulnerable neurons in the ischemic penumbra remains a barrier in ischemic stroke. Lysosomal membrane permeabilization (LMP) is increasingly recognized as a critical event in ischemic neuronal death, yet the endogenous mechanisms that preserve lysosomal integrity remain poorly defined. Here, we identify β-adducin (Add2) as an endogenous protector of lysosomal homeostasis in ischemic neurons. We found that β-adducin was markedly reduced in neurons after cerebral ischemia in both middle cerebral artery occlusion and oxygen-glucose deprivation/reoxygenation models. Neuron-specific knockdown of Add2 increased infarct volume, worsened neurological deficits, and enhanced neuronal apoptosis. Mechanistically, β-adducin interacted with cytosolic phospholipase A2 group IVA (PLA2G4A) and restricted its accumulation on lysosomes. Loss of β-adducin enhanced lysosomal localization of PLA2G4A, promoted LMP, increased cytosolic leakage of cathepsins, and exacerbated neuronal injury, whereas silencing PLA2G4A attenuated these effects. Upstream, ischemic stress reduced FTO expression, increased N6-methyladenosine (m6A) modification of Add2 mRNA, and accelerated Add2 transcript decay. Conversely, FTO overexpression restored β-adducin expression and alleviated ischemic neuronal injury. Together, these findings identify β-adducin as a key component of an endogenous lysosomal defense pathway in ischemic stroke and suggest that reduced FTO-mediated demethylation and consequent β-adducin loss contribute to PLA2G4A-associated lysosomal injury and neuronal death.

secondary.title: HSV-1 induces stable associations between the Golgi and endosomes within the cytoplasmic viral assembly compartment of neuronal cells.
secondary.abstract: Assembly of mature herpesvirus particles is associated with extensive rearrangement of cytoplasmic membranes. Herpes simplex virus type 1 (HSV-1) infection in neuronal cells induces the formation of a distinctive cytoplasmic viral assembly compartment (cVAC), in which rearranged host membranes and viral proteins are clustered at the perinuclear microtubule-organizing center (MTOC). Although both the trans-Golgi network (TGN) and endosomal compartments have been implicated as membrane sources for cytoplasmic envelopment, how secretory and endosomal pathways are reorganized and associated within the cVAC remains unclear. Here, we treated HSV-1-infected cells with nocodazole at a post-entry stage to disperse membrane components of the cVAC and identify microtubule-independent membrane organizations and associations using immunofluorescence imaging. We found that the Golgi apparatus was fragmented during infection but maintained cisternal stacking, as the Golgi markers GM130, GalT, and GRASP65 remained colocalized in both the absence and presence of nocodazole. We further demonstrated that Golgi mini-stacks retained their association with Rab6 during HSV-1 infection and formed microtubule-independent associations with early and recycling endosomes, resulting in the formation of Golgi-endosome super-mini-stacks. Viral capsid, glycoprotein, and tegument proteins were colocalized with Golgi-endosome super-mini-stacks in both the presence and absence of microtubules, suggesting that this membrane complex serves as a site of cytoplasmic envelopment regardless of clustering at the MTOC. Formation of these stable Golgi-endosome associations did not require viral capsids. Neither actin filaments nor acetylated microtubules colocalized with Golgi-endosome super-mini-stacks, suggesting that cytoskeletal elements are not required for this association.IMPORTANCEMany viruses remodel host cytoplasmic membranes to facilitate their assembly. Elucidating the molecular mechanisms underlying this remodeling may reveal novel antiviral targets while also providing insight into fundamental principles of intracellular membrane organization. Infection with an important human pathogen, herpes simplex virus type 1 (HSV-1), induces extensive membrane remodeling that leads to the formation of the cytoplasmic viral assembly compartment (cVAC) in neuronal cells, yet the underlying mechanisms remain poorly understood. Here, we demonstrate that HSV-1 induces stable associations between membranes within the cVAC. Our findings support a model in which HSV-1 generates a dynamic hybrid membrane compartment during infection, potentially reconciling conflicting views on the roles of distinct membrane sources in cytoplasmic assembly.

secondary.title: MD2-IN-1 restores microglial lysosomal function and attenuates amyloid pathology through TREM2-associated signaling in 5×FAD mice.
secondary.abstract: Triggering receptor expressed on myeloid cells 2 (TREM2) is a central regulator of microglial adaptation during Alzheimer's disease (AD), yet the development of small-molecule modulators associated with TREM2 signaling remains limited. Here, through a consensus pharmacophore-guided virtual screening strategy, MD2-IN-1 was identified as a candidate small molecule associated with TREM2 signaling. Biolayer interferometry and cellular thermal shift assays supported cellular target engagement related to TREM2 (KD = 13.85 μM). In Aβ-stimulated BV2 microglia, MD2-IN-1 increased SYK phosphorylation, promoted Aβ uptake, and shifted microglial responses toward a less proinflammatory phenotype. These effects were markedly attenuated following Trem2 knockdown, indicating the involvement of the TREM2-SYK signaling pathway. Mechanistically, MD2-IN-1 restored lysosomal acidification and increased the expression of the V-ATPase subunits ATP6v0c and ATP6v0a1, accompanied by increased intracellular Aβ degradation. In 5×FAD mice, chronic MD2-IN-1 administration improved cognitive performance without detectable behavioral abnormalities compared with WT animals. Multimodal PET imaging demonstrated reduced amyloid deposition and attenuated neuroinflammatory signals, which were further supported by histological analyses showing decreased plaque burden, reduced inflammatory microglial responses, and preserved neuronal integrity. In addition, MD2-IN-1 reduced P62 accumulation and restored ATP6v0c expression in vivo, whereas these effects were partially attenuated by pharmacological inhibition of TREM2. Collectively, these findings identify MD2-IN-1 as a small-molecule modulator associated with TREM2 signaling that restores microglial lysosomal degradative function and promotes Aβ clearance in AD models, providing pharmacological support for targeting adaptive microglial responses in AD.

secondary.title: Nanotechnology meets neurodegeneration: restoring lysosomal function with nanovectors.
secondary.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Neurodegenerative diseases (NDs) remain a growing burden worldwide. Characterized primarily by degeneration of neurons in the central nervous system (CNS), driven in part by pathological protein aggregates and by alterations of the autophagy-lysosomal pathway (ALP), current therapeutic strategies only mitigate the outcomes of NDs rather than their origin, highlighting the need for the development of new targeted therapies. AREAS COVERED: CNS-targeted nanoparticles (NPs) to tackle ALP have offered promising avenues by bypassing biological barriers, reducing pathological protein aggregates, restoring lysosomal pH and activity, upregulating autophagic flux, and contributing to neuroprotection. This report summarizes recent advances in the development of CNS‑targeted nanocarriers for autophagy as a treatment for ND. EXPERT OPINION: Restoring ALP function is a promising disease-modifying strategy for NDs, as it helps clear toxic protein aggregates. Nanotechnology offers an effective way to deliver such therapies to the brain by overcoming the blood-brain barrier, enabling targeted, multimodal, and potentially cell-specific interventions. However, key challenges remain, including late diagnosis, the need for precise cell targeting, and concerns about long-term safety and bioaccumulation. Despite these limitations, growing research interest is expected to accelerate the development and clinical translation of these approaches.

secondary.title: Berbamine hydrochloride as a brain-penetrant galectin-3 inhibitor in a model of Huntington's disease.
secondary.abstract: Galectin-3 (Gal3) acts as an intracellular sensor of lysosomal damage and a key driver of microglial activation and neuroinflammation in multiple neurodegenerative disorders. Despite its biological importance, no inhibitors have been identified that both modulate intracellular Gal3 activity and effectively cross the blood-brain barrier. Here, we established an innovative high-content imaging platform using microglia expressing Gal3-GFP, allowing direct visualization of Gal3 puncta formation upon lysosomal damage as a phenotypic readout for compound screening. Through screening of ∼24 000 small molecules, we identified berbamine hydrochloride as a potent inhibitor of Gal3 puncta formation with confirmed blood-brain barrier permeability. Mechanistically, berbamine hydrochloride disrupts Gal3 oligomerization and Gal3-TREM2 interaction via a unique allosteric mechanism distinct from the canonical glycan-binding domain. It attenuated lipopolysaccharide-induced inflammation in vitro and achieved sustained brain exposure in vivo. In the R6/2 mouse model of Huntington's disease, berbamine hydrochloride effectively improved motor functions, reduced mutant huntingtin protein aggregation and restored crucial dopaminergic and ciliary signalling pathways. Transcriptomic profiling further identified Gal3 as a central regulatory hub within Huntington's disease-associated networks that were corrected upon treatment. Computational docking and molecular dynamics simulations further supported an allosteric binding mode distinct from the canonical glycan-binding domain of Gal3. Together, these findings establish berbamine hydrochloride as the first blood-brain barrier-penetrant small molecule inhibitor targeting intracellular Gal3 with therapeutic benefit in Huntington's disease. Furthermore, the puncta-based screening strategy that we developed provides a robust platform for discovering intracellular modulators of Gal3 relevant to a wide range of neurological diseases.

secondary.title: Local ROS and inefficient autophagosome formation limit Optineurin-mediated mitophagy in neurons.
secondary.abstract: Mitophagy is a quality control mechanism that maintains neuronal health by removing damaged mitochondria. In neurons, mitophagy can be driven by Optineurin (OPTN), a selective autophagy receptor recruited in response to oxidative stress. However, mechanistic studies of mitophagy have relied mainly on non-neuronal cell lines and acute damage paradigms. It remains unknown whether these findings translate to neurons under physiological stress conditions. Here, we investigated the temporal dynamics of OPTN-dependent mitophagy under mild oxidative stress using live-cell imaging in primary rat hippocampal neurons. We found that autophagosomes failed to readily engulf OPTN-positive (OPTN+) mitochondria, revealing a previously unidentified rate-limiting step in neuronal OPTN-mediated mitophagy. Additionally, OPTN+ mitochondria colocalized with acidified lysosomes over timescales significantly longer than previously reported. These OPTN+ mitochondria displayed locally elevated reactive oxygen species (ROS). Scavenging mitochondrial ROS increased lysosomal colocalization with damaged mitochondria and accelerated mitophagy progression. Together, these findings indicate that redox signaling contributes to the slow timescale of OPTN-mediated mitophagy in neurons.

secondary.title: Plant-Derived Senolytic Ingredient, Camellia sinensis Root Extract, Ameliorates Skin Aging-Associated Phenotypes.
secondary.abstract: Senescent cells affect neighbouring cells via the senescence-associated secretory phenotype (SASP), which involves proinflammatory cytokines, chemokines and proteases. Camellia sinensis root extract (SENOMUNE) has shown therapeutic potential for skin aging-related disorders. However, whether it exerts senolytic effect remains to be explored. Thus, this study aimed to assess the senolytic properties of SENOMUNE in a stress-induced premature senescence model in normal human dermal fibroblasts (NHDFs) through cell viability assays, quantitative reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction, western blot and flow cytometry. NHDFs were induced to senescence using doxorubicin and insulin-like growth factor-1. The senolytic effect of SENOMUNE was evaluated by measuring senescence-associated β-galactosidase activity, gene and protein expression, and the apoptosis rate. SENOMUNE reduced the viability of senescent cells in a dose-dependent manner, with a more pronounced effect in senescent cells than in control cells. It was also associated with caspase-independent programmed cell death involving apoptosis-inducing factor and lysosomal membrane permeabilization in senescent cells. Moreover, SENOMUNE reduced the production of SASP factors, increased the expression of skin barrier-associated markers, and attenuated pigmentation by modulating the secretion of inflammatory cytokines. These effects were evaluated using conditioned media derived from senescent fibroblasts and validated through ex vivo skin biopsy experiments. Our results suggest that SENOMUNE exhibits senolytic properties and thus is a promising anti-aging phytopharmaceutical ingredient for managing skin-related disorders.

secondary.title: The neuropathy-causing GARS1∆ETAQ mutation drives pathology in subsets of motor and sensory neurons in mice.
secondary.abstract: Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease type 2D (CMT2D) results from gain-of-function mutations in GARS1, which encodes glycyl-tRNA synthetase (GlyRS), the enzyme responsible for charging transfer RNA (tRNA) with glycine. There are several CMT2D mouse models, but Gars∆ETAQ/+ is the only one that bears a patient-sourced mutation. Created using CRISPR/Cas9 to model a 12-nucleotide de novo GARS1 deletion identified in an unusually severe CMT2D patient, Gars∆ETAQ/+ mice have previously been shown to display several neuromuscular phenotypes: motor axon loss, denervated neuromuscular junctions (NMJs) and reduced muscle function. Here, we extend these analyses to provide a more comprehensive understanding of both motor and sensory nerve deficits across hind- and fore-limbs. At 3 months, Gars∆ETAQ/+ mice possess sex-independent alterations in the levels of neuropathy biomarkers - including decreased NfL and increased periaxin - alongside reduced muscle endurance and strength, and impairments in the sensory modalities of mechanosensation, proprioception and nociception. Underpinning these dysfunctions, we identified site-specific defects comprising altered sensory neuron populations, muscle spindle loss, reduced motor neuron size, disrupted NMJ innervation and maturation, and reduced axonal transport of signalling endosomes in vivo. Together, these experiments show that Gars∆ETAQ/+ mice display robust and selective peripheral nerve pathology that manifests in a general length-dependent fashion, priming this CMT2D allele for testing treatments and evaluating mechanisms underlying peripheral nerve vulnerability.
