secondary.title: Competing Colloidal Interactions Govern Polymer Encapsulation of Hydrophobic Iron Oxide Nanoparticles.
secondary.abstract: Control over synthesis conditions is necessary to ensure high loading in polymer-encapsulated iron oxide nanoparticles (P-IONPs) and enable biomedical applications. While flash nanoprecipitation (FNP) is a robust method to fabricate P-IONPs, very little is known regarding the response of hydrophobic IONPs to the change in solvent quality during FNP and its effect on the nature of encapsulation. In this work, we first probe the sizes of oleic acid (OA)-coated IONPs at varying compositions of water (ϕw) in a tetrahydrofuran (THF)-water mixture through time-based dynamic light scattering (DLS) and cryo-electron microscopy. It was found that OA-IONPs existed as large (micron)-sized clusters in THF, which broke into smaller clusters as ϕw in the solvent mixture increased. A free energy model of clustering is presented to describe the competing repulsive and attractive interparticle interactions driving the equilibrium cluster sizes (d*) as a function of ϕw. This effect was further pronounced when an aqueous Tween 80 solution was added to the dispersion, resulting in individually dispersed IONPs at high ϕw. The d* directly influenced the nature of P-IONPs produced using FNP at varying aqueous-to-organic flow rate ratios. Finally, a systematic study was performed to investigate the effects of the concentration of polymer and IONPs, and OA surface coverage on IONPs, on the extent and nature of encapsulation. The findings suggest the key role of competing colloidal interactions in governing the fate of synthesized P-IONPs via FNP. The understanding from this study would enable the rational design of P-IONPs with high, uniform loading for desired applications.

secondary.title: Investigating Structural Heterogeneities of Amyloid Aggregates with Spatially Resolved Infrared Spectroscopy.
secondary.abstract: The aggregation of proteins into fibrillar amyloids is central to the pathology of neurodegenerative disorders. However, the relationship between the structure of amyloid aggregates and disease progression remains incompletely understood, in part because amyloid systems are intrinsically heterogeneous: structurally distinct species coexist at every stage of aggregation, and conventional ensemble-averaged methods cannot always resolve them. This Account describes how infrared spectroscopy can be coupled to different imaging modalities to resolve this heterogeneity at multiple length scales: from single-aggregate level to amyloid species in diseased brain tissues. Our findings demonstrate that (i) early stage tau fibrils exhibit pronounced structural polymorphism without morphological differences, converging to a single dominant conformation upon maturation that unexpectedly includes antiparallel β-sheet structure; (ii) Aβ42 oligomeric heterogeneity propagates through protofibrils into fibrils, where structurally distinct domains coexist along a single fibril, demonstrating that amyloid fibrils can deviate significantly from the canonical parallel cross-β architecture; (iii) Aβ(16-22) fibrils undergo a parallel-to-antiparallel β-sheet transition during maturation through disordered intermediates without morphological change, providing direct evidence of spontaneous structural reorganization in fibrillar species. Beyond single-protein systems, (iv) Aβ42 forms structurally distinct mixed polymorphs when aggregated with sequentially or structurally heterotypic seeds and when coaggregated with α-synuclein, establishing heterotypic interactions as an underappreciated source of aberrant aggregate structures; (v) coaggregation of Aβ with the islet amyloid polypeptide (IAPP) from the monomeric state produces a unique heterotypic polymorph in which both peptides adopt non-native structures, whereas cross-seeding with preformed IAPP fibrils yields predominantly homotypic Aβ aggregates, demonstrating that conformational flexibility at the monomeric stage is required for heterotypic fibril formation. These molecular-level findings are complemented by tissue-scale evidence: (vi) discrete frequency IR imaging reveals that amyloid plaques in AD brain exhibit chemical and structural heterogeneities not reflected in morphology, consistent with in vitro observations; and (vii) optical photothermal infrared (O-PTIR) spectroscopic imaging of vascular amyloid deposits in cerebral amyloid angiopathy (CAA) reveals a disease-stage-dependent increase in antiparallel β-sheet content that correlates specifically with colocalized lipids, recapitulated in vitro by coaggregating Aβ40 with lipid extracts. Collectively, these findings support the view that structural heterogeneity is not merely an artifact of in vitro conditions but a property that can persist in human brain tissues and illustrate how spatially resolved IR spectroscopy can complement cryogenic electron microscopy (cryo-EM) and solid-state NMR in the study of amyloid pathology.

secondary.title: A case of STING-associated vasculopathy with onset in infancy highlighting the pathogenetic role of interferon regulatory factor 5.
secondary.abstract: OBJECTIVES: To elucidate the pathophysiology of stimulator of interferon genes (STING)-associated vasculopathy with onset in infancy (SAVI), we evaluated interferon-stimulated gene (ISG) expression and nuclear translocation of interferon regulatory factors 3 and 5 (IRF3 and IRF5) in patient-derived cells before and after Janus kinase (JAK) inhibitor treatment. METHODS: A 3-year-old girl presenting with refractory eczema, polyarthritis, and interstitial lung disease (ILD) was confirmed to have SAVI. Baricitinib, a JAK1/2 inhibitor, was initiated for refractory ILD, and peripheral blood samples were analysed before and 4 months after baricitinib initiation. Expression of representative ISGs (IFI27, MX1, and OAS1) was quantified by reverse-transcription quantitative polymerase chain reaction. Nuclear localization of IRF3 and IRF5 was examined in sorted monocytes and B cells using confocal microscopy after intracellular staining. Activation was quantified by the nuclear-to-cytoplasmic mean fluorescence intensity ratio. RESULTS: ISG expression was markedly elevated at baseline and decreased to levels comparable to those in a healthy control subject after 4 months of treatment. IRF3 localization remained unchanged, whereas IRF5 showed pronounced nuclear enrichment in monocytes at baseline, an effect that diminished after treatment. This reduction paralleled clinical improvement, including resolution of lung involvement and rash, and seroreversion of autoantibodies. CONCLUSION: IRF5 activation may sustain chronic inflammation in SAVI independently of IRF3. The observed reduction in IRF5 nuclear translocation paralleled the improvement in disease activity, suggesting that targeting IRF5 may help suppress inflammatory processes not adequately controlled by existing treatments.

secondary.title: Piezo1 knockdown alleviates high‑altitude cerebral edema by improving brain microvascular endothelial cell tight junctions via blocking the calcium influx‑mediated Calpain‑1 activity.
secondary.abstract: High‑altitude cerebral edema (HACE) is a life‑threatening complication of acute high‑altitude exposure, but effective treatment strategies remain limited. The influence of Piezo1 on the tight junctions of brain microvascular endothelial cells in HACE was examined to identify novel therapeutic interventions against HACE. A mouse model of HACE was established through exposure to a simulated high‑altitude hypobaric hypoxia environment. Brain water content, Evans Blue staining, magnetic resonance imaging, hematoxylin and eosin staining, FITC‑Dextran leakage assay and transmission electron microscopy were utilized to evaluate the impact of Piezo1 on HACE. A cell model of HACE was created by subjecting bEnd.3 cells to high fluid shear stress (HFSS) and hypoxic conditions. The effects of Piezo1 and Calpain‑1 on tight junction protein expression were assessed via western blot analysis. Mice with HACE exhibited increased brain water content, disrupted blood‑brain barrier integrity, enhanced microvascular permeability, hippocampal and cortical damage and reduced expression of VE‑cadherin, occludin, claudin‑5 and ZO‑1 proteins, alongside elevated Piezo1 and Calpain‑1 activity in brain microvascular endothelial cells. Silencing of Piezo1 alleviated these HACE symptoms. bEnd.3 cells subjected to HFSS and hypoxia showed increased intracellular Ca2+, along with heightened Calpain‑1 protein expression and activity, while levels of VE‑cadherin, occludin, claudin‑5 and ZO‑1 proteins were diminished. Both Piezo1 silencing and Calpain‑1 inhibition reversed these in vitro changes. Notably, Piezo1 silencing reduced Calpain‑1 activity without significantly altering Calpain‑1 protein levels. Piezo1 silencing may ameliorate HACE by enhancing tight junctions in brain microvascular endothelial cells through the suppression of calcium influx‑mediated Calpain‑1 activity. Thus, targeting Piezo1 expression may represent a promising therapeutic approach for HACE.

secondary.title: Engineering sticky microbes: A framework for appraisal of microbial cell-cell adhesion.
secondary.abstract: Engineering bacterial consortia is key in biotechnological applications where specific spatial interactions among their components determine system performance. Genetic tools for programming cell-cell binding such as the nanobody-antigen (Nb-Ag; relying on non-covalent binding) and SpyCatcher-SpyTag (Spy; based on covalent linkage) systems are increasingly adopted as assets for enabling specific interactions of interest among otherwise detached members of a given combination of strains or species. Yet, despite the potential of these technologies, a robust metrology to quantify and compare the efficacy, stability, and specificity of inter-cell binding in a consortium is lacking. This work introduces a conceptual and experimental framework to systematically evaluate synthetic binding systems by combining aggregation assays, flow cytometry, and microscopy. Together, these techniques provide detailed insights into the structure and composition of engineered bacterial aggregates. This methodology was benchmarked with two Escherichia coli strains tagged with different fluorescent markers and engineered to surface-display matching adhesins. Under the test conditions, results showed that the Spy system outperformed the Nb-Ag system in terms of aggregation speed and stability. We also applied the same metrics for assessing the efficacy of the Spy system to mediate synthetic consortia of the pathogenic bacterium Enterobacter cloacae. The robustness of the results suggests the proposed framework to become a valuable tool for quantitative studies on designer bacterial consortia.

secondary.title: Hydrogen Bonding is Required for Continuous Polyvinylpyrrolidone Adhesive Films.
secondary.abstract: The versatility of polyvinylpyrrolidone (PVP) as a dispersing and adhesive agent lies in its amphiphilicity and hydrogen bonding capability. In this study, silicon wafers (SiO2) were silanized with N-(2-aminoethyl)-3-aminopropyltriethoxysilane (AEAPTES), (N,N-dimethylamino)trimethylsilane (TMS), and n-octyldimethylchlorosilane (C8) to construct four substrates with varying fractions of hydrogen bonding sites and hydrophobic groups. PVP thin films were fabricated on the substrates using both static adsorption and spin coating methods. PVP spontaneously adsorbs to and results in 1 nm-thick films on all the substrates, demonstrating the polymer's capability as a universal adhesive. The continuity of the dried PVP films at the nanoscopic and micron scales was imaged using atomic force and optical microscopy, respectively. The film stability was correlated to the fraction of substrate hydrogen bonding sites. The films are stable on SiO2 with 100% hydrogen bonding sites, unstable on TMS with 100% hydrophobic groups, and metastable on AEAPTES and C8 with a mixture of hydrogen bonding sites and hydrophobic groups.

secondary.title: Genetically Encoded APEX2 Enables Metal-Enhanced X-ray Contrast for Energy-Selective Imaging in Complex Tissues.
secondary.abstract: X-ray microscopy offers deep tissue penetration and high spatial resolution, but its application to genetically targeted imaging remains limited by the lack of probes capable of generating sufficient and selective X-ray contrast in complex biological tissues. Here we report a genetically encoded X-ray contrast generation strategy that combines AAV-mediated expression of engineered peroxidase APEX2, enzymatic signal amplification through diaminobenzidine (DAB) deposition, and energy-selective synchrotron X-ray imaging. Optimization of Cre-dependent AAV expression and tissue fixation enabled efficient conversion of gene expression into localized X-ray-absorbing deposits. We further identified tissue-background absorption as a major factor limiting the analytical performance of conventional DAB-based X-ray imaging in dense brain regions. To address this challenge, nickel-enhanced DAB (EDAB) was introduced to generate metal-containing reaction products with characteristic absorption properties. Imaging near the Ni L-edge substantially improved signal discrimination between reporter-labeled neurons and surrounding tissue, overcoming the contrast limitations observed with conventional DAB imaging. This work establishes a genetically encoded and energy-selective X-ray contrast-generation platform that integrates reporter engineering, signal amplification, and absorption-edge-guided detection, providing a general analytical framework for targeted X-ray imaging in complex biological systems.

secondary.title: A WSI-Independent Inference Framework for Cervical and Urinary Cytology Using Hierarchical Labels.
secondary.abstract: BACKGROUND: Cytology artificial intelligence (AI) systems often depend on whole-slide images (WSIs) or high-magnification cell images and are commonly optimized for a single specimen type. We developed CYTOLONE-v2, a contrastive language-image pretraining (CLIP)-based hierarchical classification framework for cervical and urinary cytology that is designed for individual-field inference without WSI input. METHODS: CYTOLONE-v1.1, previously trained for cervical cytology, was further trained by low-rank adaptation using WSI-derived urinary cytology fields equivalent to ×10 magnification. The 90-case source cohort was divided at the case level into training (72 cases; 360 fields) and validation (18 cases; 90 fields) subsets. Five diagnosis-representative fields were manually selected from each case. Field-level performance was evaluated in an independent urinary test cohort of 40 cases (20 Reactive change and 20 Urothelial carcinoma; 200 fields), and retention was assessed using an independent cervical cytology test set. RESULTS: In urinary cytology, CYTOLONE-v2 achieved field-level accuracies of 64.0% for Anomaly and Malignancy and 72.5% for Diagnosis. At the Diagnosis level, sensitivity for urothelial carcinoma was 99.0% (95% confidence interval [CI], 96.7%-100%), whereas specificity against Reactive change was 46.0% (95% CI, 30.0%-62.0%). Cervical cytology accuracy was retained at the Anomaly level (94.8% vs. 94.7% with CYTOLONE-v1.1), decreased modestly at the Malignancy level (91.2% vs. 93.5%), and decreased more at the Bethesda and Diagnosis levels. CONCLUSIONS: CYTOLONE-v2 demonstrates the technical feasibility of extending a hierarchical cytology classification framework from cervical to urinary cytology. The findings are limited to selected WSI-derived fields and a Reactive change-versus-Urothelial carcinoma test cohort; external, case-level, direct-microscopy and prospective workflow validation is required before clinical utility can be established.

secondary.title: Silver sodium nitroprusside nano-aggregates for ultrasound-activated immunomodulatory therapy of MRSA pneumonia.
secondary.abstract: The clinical management of methicillin-resistantS. aureus(MRSA) pneumonia is hindered by biofilm infections and cytokine storms. A key challenge is the lack of real-time monitoring tools for the inflammatory microenvironment during treatment. In this study, we developed a theranostic platform (CS@EAgNP) using TPP-modified chitosan to load silver sodium nitroprusside nano-aggregates (AgNP) and epigallocatechin gallate (EGCG). This system combines ultrasound (US) imaging with US-activated therapy. The CS@EAgNP nano-aggregates can act as an excellent US contrast enhancer.In vivoUS imaging indicated that AgNP generated significantly enhanced echo signals at the infection site, providing real-time and high-contrast visualization of the inflammatory foci that was unattainable with normal lung tissue. Moreover, these nano-aggregates release NO, silver and EGCG under US. The NO and silver penetrate biofilms to kill MRSA, while EGCG scavenges reactive oxygen species and modulates inflammation. This reduces pro-inflammatory cytokines like IL-6 and TNF-α, mitigating the cytokine storm.In vivoresults further confirm that this image-guided strategy achieves significant bacterial clearance and promotes lung tissue regeneration without detectable toxicity to major organs. This integrated approach bridges diagnosis and treatment, offering a promising solution for managing MRSA pneumonia.

secondary.title: Increasing urogenital and oropharyngeal gonorrhoea positivity in women attending a sexual health service in Melbourne, Australia, 2015-2024.
secondary.abstract: BACKGROUND: Gonorrhoea notifications among women have increased, but the determinants of this trend are unclear. We aimed to examine temporal trends in gonorrhoea positivity and associated clinical characteristics among women attending a major sexual health clinic in Melbourne, Australia between 2015 and 2024. METHOD: We conducted a retrospective analysis of women diagnosed with gonorrhoea between 2015 and 2024. Demographic, behavioural and clinical data were extracted from routine clinical records, including sexual practices, sex work status and condom use. A chart review of a subset of positive cases was performed to obtain symptom characteristics and microscopy findings. RESULTS: Over the study period, we included a total of 91,332 consultations (47,013 women), with a gonorrhoea test performed on the day. Overall, the gonorrhoea positivity was 1.9% (1693/91,332), and it increased from 1.3% (61/4711) in 2015 to 2.3% (243/10,497) in 2024 (Ptrend < 0.001), representing a 78.9% relative increase. Oropharyngeal gonorrhoea increased from 4.4% (21/482) to 5.8% (96/1653; Ptrend < 0.001), and urogenital gonorrhoea increased from 1.0% (49/4673) to 1.7% (181/10,435; Ptrend < 0.001), whereas anorectal gonorrhoea remained stable. Of the 1693 women who were diagnosed with gonorrhoea, most were born overseas (52.9%, n = 896), and resided in high socioeconomic areas (76.1%, n = 1289). Co-infection with bacterial vaginosis (14.9%) and chlamydia (13.6%) was frequent. Among symptomatic women who underwent chart review, vaginal discharge was the most common symptom (59.5%), but only 8.7% reported a 'typical' yellow, green or pus-like discharge. CONCLUSION: Gonorrhoea positivity among women increased over the past decade, particularly at the oropharyngeal site, suggesting broader transmission within the general population. As many women did not present with a typical gonorrhoea discharge, general practitioners and other healthcare providers should consider gonorrhoea in women presenting with genital symptoms and offer testing, including at extragenital sites where clinically indicated.

secondary.title: Youth Mental Health-Related Emergency Department Visits After Hurricane Helene: A Difference-in-Differences Analysis.
secondary.abstract: PURPOSE: Extreme weather can disrupt social supports, schooling, and access to behavioral health services, potentially affecting youth mental health. This study examined changes in youth mental health-related emergency department (ED) visits following Hurricane Helene (2024). METHODS: ED surveillance data from North Carolina (2022-2024) were used to assess mental health-related visits among youth aged 5-26. A difference-in-difference (DID) design compared FEMA-designated disaster counties with nondeclared counties before and after the storm. Multilevel intersectional analyses evaluated risk by sex, race/ethnicity, age, and insurance. RESULTS: Anxiety-related ED visits increased in disaster-exposed counties post-Helene (DIDRR = 1.14, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.01-1.29), with larger increases among females than males (DIDRR = 1.18, 95% CI: 1.03-1.35). Depression also showed greater relative increases among females (difference-in-difference-in-differencesRR = 1.28, 95% CI: 1.09-1.51). Self-harm visits declined overall (DIDRR = 0.70, 95% CI: 0.52-0.94). DISCUSSION: Hurricane Helene was associated with shifts in youth mental health-related ED use, demonstrating the need to strengthen adolescent and young adult behavioral health services in disaster-prone rural communities.

secondary.title: Organization of myosin H in the apical complex of Toxoplasma gondii revealed by 3D single-molecule super-resolution microscopy.
secondary.abstract: Toxoplasma gondii is a single-celled eukaryotic parasite with prolific invasion capability. The parasite uses an apical complex comprising proteinaceous structures and secretory organelles to efficiently enter host cells. As a result, the apical complex remains a vital structure of interest, with many studies dedicated to understanding its protein organization. One such protein is the motor myosin H (MyoH), which is indispensable for parasite motility and host-cell invasion. Given the small size of the complex, roughly a diffraction-limited volume in the visible, high-resolution techniques are required to make precise determinations of protein organization. In this work, we use 3D single-molecule localization microscopy in both traditionally fixed and gel-expanded parasites to localize the indispensable motor MyoH within the apical complex. Labeling of the N and C termini of MyoH in fixed parasites resolved the orientation of the motor protein in the apical complex, showing the motor head radially exterior to the tail. Two-color imaging of MyoH with tubulin in fixed parasites allowed for localization of the MyoH termini relative to the conoid, a barrel of tubulin-based fibrils in the apical complex, and showed the MyoH tail toward the interior face of the conoid and the head at the conoid exterior. Gel expansion showed improved labeling density for both tubulin and MyoH but altered MyoH localization, highlighting the nuanced effects of gel expansion on protein organization.

secondary.title: Integrated SEM, TEM and CLSM workflow for tegumental analysis of adult Schistosoma mansoni.
secondary.abstract: The tegument of Schistosoma mansoni is a key host-parasite interface and a major target for drug and vaccine development. Although ultrastructural studies of the tegument date back decades, methodological inconsistencies often complicate comparisons across studies. Here, we present a standardized, easy-to-use framework for investigating tegumental architecture using three complementary techniques: scanning electron microscopy (SEM), transmission electron microscopy (TEM), and confocal laser scanning microscopy (CLSM). We provide step-by-step protocols, highlight strengths and limitations of each method, and illustrate their outputs using adult male worms. We also outline a scheme for unbiased quantitative analysis of the resulting images and indicate how the protocols can be adapted to female worms, to other developmental stages and schistosome species, and to immunolocalization at the ultrastructural level. This integrative pipeline enables reproducible morphological characterization and facilitates downstream applications in pharmacology, immunology, and parasite biology.

secondary.title: Real-time tracking of vaccinia virus entry using a split luciferase complementation assay.
secondary.abstract: UNLABELLED: A recombinant vaccinia virus (vA4-HiBiT) was constructed with a short, split luciferase HiBiT tag at the C-terminus of the A4 core protein open reading frame. When HeLa or A549 cells stably expressing LgBiT were infected with vA4-HiBiT, the interaction of the split luciferase fragments reconstituted NanoLuc enzyme activity. Upon addition of a membrane-permeable luciferase substrate, a strong luminescence signal indicated core entry into the cytoplasm within 5 min after infection and was proportional to virus multiplicity within the range of 0.5-80 PFU/cell. This direct entry assay was dependent on a functional virus entry-fusion complex, was inhibited by a neutralizing antibody, and was unaffected by an inhibitor of protein synthesis. Entry was enhanced by brief pH 5 treatment of cell-bound virus relative to pH 7 and prevented by pH 3 treatment. Bafilomycin A1, an inhibitor of endosomal acidification, exhibited greater inhibition of entry in A549-LgBiT cells compared to HeLa-LgBiT cells, as did treatment with ammonium chloride, suggesting variations in entry pathways or cell metabolism. Inhibition of entry by latrunculin A and cytochalasin D indicated a role for actin polymerization in both cell lines. Despite the discovery of a conserved furin cleavage consensus sequence in the A16 subunit of the entry-fusion complex, a furin inhibitor did not reduce virus entry unlike results obtained with a human papillomavirus control. These data support the use of this NanoBiT assay for studies of vaccinia virus entry, with application to basic research, antivirals, and neutralizing antibodies. IMPORTANCE: Assays to measure virus entry into cells mostly rely on post-entry events such as gene expression, cytopathic effects, or virus yields. Although fluorescence and electron microscopy can provide direct analyses, such methods are labor intensive and semiquantitative. Here we describe a rapid and quantitative real-time direct entry assay for vaccinia virus with application to basic research, antivirals, and neutralizing antibodies.

secondary.title: Orientation mapping via dictionary indexing of AC-STEM Kikuchi patterns using open-source software.
secondary.abstract: The properties of polycrystalline materials are strongly influenced by the spatial arrangement and orientations of individual grains within the microstructure, making nanoscale characterization of grain orientation essential. This is also often the case for small grains in the nm regime explored using scanning transmission electron microscopy (STEM). Automated crystal orientation mapping (ACOM) is traditionally performed using spot-like diffraction patterns. In contrast, orientation mapping based on transmission Kikuchi diffraction (TKD) using an aberration-corrected (AC) convergent STEM probe remains relatively underexplored, despite its superior orientation sensitivity and higher spatial resolution. In this work, we present an open-source software-based template-matching approach for orientation mapping using AC-STEM TKD. A master pattern (a simulated angular distribution of Kikuchi band intensities on the unit sphere) is first generated through a dynamical simulation implemented in open-source software. This resulting pattern is subsequently imported into another open-source package for geometric simulations and orientation indexing. We demonstrate the capability of the proposed method by applying it to orientation mapping in BaZr0.4Ce0.4Y0.1Yb0.1O3-δ (BZCYYb4411) fuel-cell material and LiNiO2 (LNO) lithium-ion battery cathode material. The best-matched simulated patterns exhibit strong agreement with experimental data, even under the challenging conditions with limited diffraction space available for matching.

secondary.title: Development of a europium-thiosemicarbazide-based nano-optical biosensor for early detection of HE4 in ovarian cancer.
secondary.abstract: Early diagnosis of ovarian cancer remains a major clinical challenge. Human epididymis protein 4 (HE4) has emerged as a promising biomarker for early OC detection. To address limitations of existing HE4 quantification methods, we developed a nano-optical biosensor based on a luminescent europium-thiosemicarbazide (Eu-TSC) complex immobilized within a modified epoxy-cellulose thin-film matrix. The Eu-TSC thin film exhibited characteristic europium excitation and emission bands at 395 nm and 617 nm. Following functionalization with a monoclonal anti-HE4 antibody, the biosensor displayed a concentration-dependent fluorescence quenching response upon HE4 binding. A linear analytical response was obtained over 0.05-0.37 ng mL-1, with LOD of 0.108 ng mL-1. However, the LOQ (0.327 ng mL-1) lies close to the upper limit of the linear range, the practical validated quantification interval is extremely narrow (approximately 0.327-0.37 ng mL-1). This interval is far too narrow to cover the clinical HE4 range, and the present sensor should therefore be regarded as a preliminary proof-of-concept platform rather than a clinically suitable quantitative assay. Time-resolved luminescence measurements are consistent with a quenching-based sensing response, but the present experiments do not distinguish between FRET, PET, or other quenching pathways. Molecular docking and 50 ns molecular dynamics simulations provide a computational rationale for ligand selection and suggest possible surface binding of thiosemicarbazide-based ligands to HE4. Selectivity studies against twelve potential interferents revealed relative responses below 5% for all tested analytes when tested individually at clinically relevant concentrations (n = 3 per interferent; one-way ANOVA with Dunnett's test). However, because interferents were tested individually rather than as pooled mixtures, and because cross-reactivity with structurally related proteins cannot be fully excluded, these selectivity results are preliminary and do not establish excellent selectivity in complex serum. The biosensor was further evaluated using 21 human serum samples (11 OC patients, 10 healthy controls), demonstrating agreement with a commercial HE4 ELISA assay (R2 > 0.98). Recovery values were re-verified for all samples; several values fall outside the commonly accepted 85-115% range and are flagged in Tables 1A and B. Therefore, the analytical accuracy of the present method is preliminary and not satisfactory for clinical quantification. ROC analysis yielded an AUC of 1.000, with 90.9% sensitivity and 100% specificity. These findings are based on a limited case-control cohort (n = 21) and must be interpreted as a preliminary proof-of-concept analytical and clinical evaluation, not as a clinically validated diagnostic platform. Larger prospective, multi-center studies including patients with benign gynecological conditions are required before clinical implementation can be considered.

secondary.title: A highly sensitive fluorescent nickel-based coordination polymer for Nitrofuran antibiotics detection in real water samples.
secondary.abstract: Nitrofuran antibiotics (NFAs) residues in aquatic environments pose significant threats to both ecosystems and public health. Therefore, it is of paramount importance to develop an accurate and effective technology to detect these specific pollutants. Herein, a novel Ni-CP, [Ni(H2edda)(H2O)2(Tripp)2]n (XYNU-3), has been rationally designed and constructed from 5,5'-(ethane-1,2-diylbis(oxy)) diisophthalic acid (H4edda), 2,4,6-tris(4-pyridyl)pyridine (Tripp) and NiSO4·6H2O, using hydrothermal method under a mixed-ligand strategy. Structural analysis indicates that XYNU-3 features a three-dimensional supramolecular architecture stabilized by hydrogen bonding interactions. Moreover, XYNU-3 exhibits exceptional chemical stability in different pH solutions and impressive thermal stability. Interestingly, fluorescence sensing experiments demonstrate that XYNU-3 could function as a fluorescent sensor toward nitrofurantoin (NFT) and nitrofurazone (NFZ) with high selectivity and sensitivity. Meanwhile, the well-maintained excellent sensing performance in Shihe River water renders its potential practical application in real water samples. Furthermore, detailed mechanism investigations, integrating experimental studies with density functional theory (DFT) calculations, suggest that the fluorescent quenching response of XYNU-3 toward NFAs could be attributed to a synergistic effect involving inner filter effect (IFE), fluorescence resonance energy transfer (FRET) and photoinduced electron transfer (PET). Importantly, this research might shed light on the advancement of designing luminescent coordination polymer (LCP)-based fluorescent platforms, enabling convenient and efficient environmental antibiotic pollution monitoring.

secondary.title: AI-powered dynamic scattering liquid crystal biosensor for label-free detection of ovarian cancer biomarker CA125.
secondary.abstract: Conventional static liquid crystal (LC) biosensors are frequently constrained by limited optical contrast and insufficient sensitivity for trace biomarker detection. Here, we report a label-free biosensing platform based on dual-frequency liquid crystals (DFLCs) operated in the dynamic scattering mode (DSM). By driving the DFLC system at the crossover frequency of 22.2 kHz and an optimized voltage of 22.5 V, it entered an electrohydrodynamically unstable state, where minute interfacial perturbations induced by biomolecular recognition were amplified into high-contrast macroscopic scattering responses. Using haze as a quantitative readout, the DSM optical response stabilized within 3 s of electric-field application, and the platform achieved a limit of detection (LOD) of 0.11 ng/mL for bovine serum albumin, 0.82 and 4.86 ng/mL for cancer antigen 125 (CA125) in deionized water and human serum, respectively, demonstrating high sensitivity and robust resistance to matrix interference. To enable automated quantitative analysis and concentration prediction from the highly complex DSM optical textures, we implemented a ResNet-34-based convolutional neural network (CNN), which utilizes a residual backbone for hierarchical feature extraction from polarized optical microscopy images, integrated with a custom regression head. The deep learning model achieved a cross-validation coefficient of determination R2 of 0.84, and 82% of the independent blind-evaluation samples were correctly assigned to their experimentally prepared concentration groups. The integration of DSM-based signal amplification with AI-driven quantitative analysis positions the DFLC biosensor as a rapid, sensitive, and automated analytical platform with strong potential for next-generation in vitro diagnostics.

secondary.title: Accelerated and memory-efficient clutter filtering toward online-compatible ultrasound localization microscopy via compressed-matrix randomized QRD.
secondary.abstract: Ultrasound localization microscopy (ULM) enables super-resolution visualization of cerebral microvasculature; however, its clinical translation is hindered by the substantial computational burden of singular value decomposition (SVD)-based clutter filtering. To address this issue, we propose Compressed-Matrix Randomized QR Decomposition (CM-rQRD) as an accelerated and memory-efficient filtering framework. By integrating a Compressed-Matrix strategy into rQRD-based methods, the computational complexity of the decomposition step is substantially reduced. Specifically, the proposed methods achieve the lowest theoretical complexity, providing a 7.7-fold acceleration over conventional SVD while reducing memory usage to 50-65% of baseline levels. Although Power Doppler (PD) imaging exhibits a marginal 1-2 dB reduction in SNR and CNR, ULM reconstructions preserved spatial resolution and flow-related information comparable to SVDcov, with supplementary structural similarity values above 0.95. Furthermore, on an 800-frame in vivo dataset, CM-rQRDs complete clutter filtering in 72 ms on a CPU and in 7.7 ms on a GPU, underscoring their potential as online-compatible clutter-filtering modules for scalable ULM processing.

secondary.title: QuRad: Radiomics Feature Extraction for QuPath.
secondary.abstract: Radiomic features provide a quantitative description of tissue organization in histopathology images. QuPath, a widely used open-source platform for whole-slide image analysis, offers morphology, intensity, and Haralick texture measurements but no standardized radiomic feature set such as that of PyRadiomics. Researchers must therefore export data to external Python pipelines, interrupting their QuPath workflow. QuRad extracts radiomic features from cell detections and annotation regions directly inside QuPath. The extension and equivalent Groovy script implement 119 features: 103 two-dimensional features enabled by default and 16 optional legacy shape descriptors. We compared QuRad 0.4 with PyRadiomics 3.0.1 on identical grayscale images and pixel masks. All 103 default features met a 10-9 absolute-or-relative agreement tolerance on a breast-cancer benchmark tile (410 cells). On 20 melanoma tiles (8,644 nuclei), 97 of 103 features met this tolerance and 6 polygon-derived shape features differed from PyRadiomics' raster-derived mesh (minimum concordance correlation coefficient 0.942). The 22 synthetic regions accepted by PyRadiomics reproduced the expected intensity and texture values. A single-threaded server benchmark reached about 1,900 nuclei per second, and processing the 184,242 cells of a whole-slide image took 2.7 min on a laptop. A random forest distinguished tumor cells from lymphocytes in melanoma (pooled macro-F1 0.853) and classified 197 tissue regions of 6 breast-cancer slides into 3 compartments (0.696). QuRad exports the features with object coordinates and extraction settings for use in QuPath or downstream analyses.

secondary.title: RSReason: Remote Sensing Reasoning Segmentation via Rotation-aware Large Vision-Language Model.
secondary.abstract: Remote Sensing Referring Expression Segmentation (RSRES) has laid the groundwork for mapping natural language instructions to pixel-level segmentation in remote sensing imagery, where objects frequently occur at diverse scales, dense spatial distributions, and arbitrary orientations. However, existing approaches predominantly rely on explicit, category-driven queries, thereby limiting their ability to reason over spatial relationships, geometric properties, and both commonsense and domain-specific knowledge. To address these challenges, we introduce Remote Sensing Reasoning Segmentation (RSReasonSeg), a new task requiring models to perform segmentation and interpretation based on implicit, reasoning-centric, commonsense-rich language instructions. To support this, we present the RSReason benchmark, a large-scale dataset comprising 5,138 samples with reasoning-centric queries, expert-annotated masks, and explanatory answers. We further propose the RSReason-Net, a large vision-language model equipped with a Rotation Awareness Optimization (RAO) module. RAO models irregular masks as 2D Gaussians to align predictions with geometric and orientational cues derived from language. Extensive experiments demonstrate that RSReasonNet achieves superior performance over the classical LISA baseline on RSReasonSeg. Moreover, RAO consistently improves the recent state-of-the-art RSRefSeg 2 model, establishing a new state-of-the-art result. On RRSIS-D, RAO enhances RSRefSeg 2 across all evaluation metrics on both the validation and test sets, without introducing additional inference-time overhead.

secondary.title: A low-resource tracking workflow improves documentation and localizes the latent tuberculosis infection care gap in college student health.
secondary.abstract: OBJECTIVE: To assess a low-resource tracking workflow for improved documentation of latent tuberculosis infection (LTBI) treatment status and describe identified follow-up gaps in a Student Health clinic. PARTICIPANTS: Students with confirmed LTBI before (2018-2023; n = 82) and after (2024-2025; n = 147) implementation. METHODS: Retrospective before-after chart review. In 2024, the clinic added a tracking spreadsheet, nurse-initiated follow-up offering tuberculosis preventive treatment (TPT), 1-month dispensing, and standardized documentation. Outcomes were summarized descriptively. RESULTS: Among students prescribed TPT at Student Health, documented completion rose from 45.8 to 71.4% and known status from 58.3 to 89.3%; documented completion among students managed outside Student Health rose from 23.1 to 56.1%. Undocumented final status was essentially unchanged (35.4-34.0%), but 46/50 (92%) unresolved post-intervention cases had no response after two messages. CONCLUSIONS: The workflow improved documentation among engaged students and identified nonresponse after TPT was offered as the main actionable gap.

secondary.title: Niche Divergence-Based Identification of Microbial Indicators Tracking Cyanobacterial Bloom Succession: A Metagenomic and Machine Learning Framework.
secondary.abstract: Cyanobacterial harmful algal blooms (CyanoHABs) pose significant environmental and public health risks through toxin production, antibiotic resistance gene dissemination, and the disruption of biogeochemical cycles. Although extensive metagenomic investigations have explored microbial interactions between Cyanobacteria and coexisting members, the potential of incorporating functional indicators into early CyanoHAB monitoring systems remains underexplored. In this study, we employed metagenomic binning combined with machine learning approaches to analyze seasonal cyanobacterial succession and coexisting microbial communities across 19 sites in Erhai Lake across four seasons. We documented distinct niche shifts driven by the spatiotemporal heterogeneity in seasonal cyanobacterial succession alongside the formation of unique niches triggered by this asynchrony. Specialized microbial members (SN-MAGs) were identified as candidate bioindicators associated with early-stage cyanobacterial proliferation. Functional profiling showed r/K selection and metabolic adaptations in these SN-MAGs, including stress resistance and altered carbon metabolism, linked to cyanobacterial dynamics. Machine learning models leveraging these features were constructed and retrospectively evaluated. Cross-lake validation using an independent Lake Taihu dataset confirmed associations among these features and microbial community shifts preceding Microcystis proliferation. Our findings highlight the potential value of the dynamics of specific bacteria as a sensitive indicator of cyanobacterial dynamics. Moreover, we propose that these identified functional markers could potentially be developed into targeted molecular assays (e.g., qPCR assays), offering possible utility in predicting Microcystis population expansion.

secondary.title: Imaging-Enhanced Prediction of Upper Limb Motor Function After Stroke Using Automated Segmentation and Cluster Analysis.
secondary.abstract: BACKGROUND: Stroke is a leading cause of long-term disability, and early prediction of motor outcomes is critical for guiding individualized rehabilitation strategies. Although neuroimaging offers prognostic insights, its clinical integration remains limited. This study aimed to evaluate whether explainable imaging-derived features can improve the prediction of upper limb motor impairment and to identify distinct recovery profiles through cluster analysis. METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 242 patients with acute ischemic stroke who underwent brain magnetic resonance imaging and motor function assessment. Clinical and imaging variables-including infarct volume, motor tract involvement, and subtype classification-were extracted using automated software. Predictive models for Fugl-Meyer Assessment upper extremity (FMA-UE) scores were developed using hierarchical regression, and K-means clustering was applied to standardized baseline data. Cluster characteristics were compared, and recovery profiles were visualized. RESULTS: Incorporating imaging variables improved prediction of FMA-UE scores (adjusted R²: 0.595), with motor tract lesion volume emerging as a key predictor. Cluster analysis revealed three distinct patient subgroups: Cluster 1 (mild impairments, younger age), Cluster 2 (older patients with multiple comorbidities), and Cluster 3 (severe neurological deficits, large infarcts). Functional outcomes differed significantly across clusters, with Cluster 3 showing the greatest disability (76% with follow-up modified Rankin Scale 4-6, P < 0.001). CONCLUSION: Imaging-derived features from early magnetic resonance imaging improve the prediction of upper limb motor outcomes after stroke. Cluster-based stratification identifies clinically meaningful subgroups, supporting precision rehabilitation through personalized care planning and targeted secondary prevention.

secondary.title: A practical one-electrode electrochemical methodology for tracking catalyst reconstruction in NiFe-Prussian blue analogues for the oxygen evolution reaction.
secondary.abstract: Efficient and durable alkaline oxygen evolution reaction (OER) catalysts are essential for large-scale water electrolysis, yet the dynamic reconstruction of precatalysts into their true active phases remains difficult to track with simple, broadly accessible tools. Here, we use NiFe Prussian blue analogues (NiFe-PBA) grown on nickel foam (NF) as a model system to develop a practical, fully sequential one-electrode workflow that correlates structural evolution with electrochemical kinetics during the OER. NiFe-PBA/NF electrodes with varying Ni : Fe stoichiometries are synthesized hydrothermally and optimized for OER performance, identifying NiFe-PBA 1 : 1/NF as the best-performing composition. A continuous one-electrode protocol is then applied to the same physical electrode, enabling us to monitor reconstruction and kinetic stabilization under realistic operating conditions. Post-OER analysis reveals substantial disruption of the NiFe-PBA framework, amorphization, and increased Ni3+/Fe3+ and oxyhydroxide species, consistent with the formation of a NiFeOOH-like active phase. By directly linking these structural and surface-chemical changes to the observed kinetic improvements, this study clarifies the role of NiFe-PBA as an electrochemically transformable precursor to NiFeOOH and demonstrates a simple, accessible one-electrode approach for tracking catalyst reconstruction and active-phase evolution in alkaline OER.

secondary.title: Automated Multi-class Segmentation of Mandibular Odontogenic Cysts and the Mandibular Canal on CBCT Images Using a Hybrid Deep Learning Framework.
secondary.abstract: Mandibular odontogenic cysts can complicate surgical planning if located near the mandibular canal. Accurate delineation of both structures is therefore clinically important. This study presents a deep learning-based method for simultaneously segmenting mandibular odontogenic cysts and the mandibular canal in cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT) images. The developed method relies on a hybrid deep learning architecture integrating a ConvNeXt-Base encoder, a Dilated Context Block, a U-Net-based decoder, and a Deep Supervision mechanism. This framework simultaneously segments the mandibular canal and odontogenic cyst regions within the same architecture, promoting multi-scale contextual feature learning. We evaluated the performance of the proposed method using fivefold cross-validation experiments on a real-world clinical CBCT dataset comprising 103 patient images. We assessed segmentation performance using overlap-based metrics together with boundary-aware HD95 and ASSD metrics. The experimental results demonstrated that the model achieved a mean intersection over union (mIoU) of 76.28% ± 1.83%. Excluding the background class yielded macro IoU and macro F1-score values of 64.46% ± 2.74% and 77.00% ± 1.89%, respectively. Meanwhile, the weighted IoU and weighted F1-score values were 78.71% ± 4.25% and 87.63% ± 2.63%, respectively. In boundary-based evaluations, the mandibular canal had an HD95 of 2.44 ± 2.98 mm and an ASSD of 0.45 ± 0.30 mm. The corresponding values for odontogenic cysts were 5.59 ± 3.65 mm and 1.43 ± 0.88 mm, respectively. These results suggest that the mandibular canal is more consistently delineated, while cyst segmentation remains more challenging, particularly at irregular and low-contrast boundaries. The proposed framework allows for the simultaneous and objective segmentation of mandibular odontogenic cysts and the mandibular canal within a unified, multi-class CBCT analysis framework. By providing reproducible delineation of both structures, this method could serve as a technical foundation for future quantitative analyses of lesion-canal relationships. However, further validation using larger, multicenter, volumetric CBCT datasets is required before clinical translation.

secondary.title: Annotation-Efficient Individual Muscle Segmentation from Dixon MRI: A Multi-Dataset Benchmark of Pretraining and Fat-Fraction Guidance.
secondary.abstract: Measuring individual muscles and their fatty infiltration on Dixon MRI can support sarcopenia assessment, but manual annotation is time-consuming and annotated datasets are often small. This study investigated accurate individual-muscle segmentation with limited labelled data. Three datasets were used: an abdominal CT dataset of 300 subjects with adipose-tissue labels, a lower-limb Dixon MRI dataset of 25 subjects with 13 thigh and 9 calf muscles, and an independent cohort of 66 subjects for external testing. Network architecture, encoder pretraining, a Dixon-derived fat-fraction input, and a shared CT-MRI encoder were compared. A 2.5D model, subject-level cross-validation, zero-shot transfer, label-free domain adaptation, and few-shot adaptation were also evaluated. The best models reached Dice 0.947 ± 0.017  for CT adipose tissue and 0.925 ± 0.010  for thigh muscle; the best 2.5D model reached 0.928, while a reported 3D Attention-Res-V-Net reached 0.857 under a different protocol. Encoder pretraining helped most at the smallest budgets, with ImageNet performing best and comparably to CT-based pretraining at eight subjects. A shared CT-MRI encoder retained accuracy with 44 %  fewer parameters, and thigh-muscle volumes agreed closely with reference measurements (ICC ( 2 , 1 ) = 0.998  ). On the external cohort, fine-tuning raised Dice from 0.11 zero-shot to 0.61, 0.76, and 0.88 with four, eight, and 46 labelled target subjects. The fat-fraction input improved segmentation only when very few subjects (two or four) were labelled. Encoder pretraining and efficient model sharing help when annotated MRI data are scarce. A small amount of target-domain annotation substantially improves cross-cohort transfer, and repeated subject-level validation is important for reliable evaluation.

secondary.title: Combined eye tracking and electroencephalography during referential selection in dyadic interaction.
secondary.abstract: Understanding language in real-world interaction requires methods that integrate auditory, visual, and neural signals. We present a proof-of-concept study combining mobile electroencephalography (EEG) and eye tracking to investigate referential selection during dyadic communication. Using a simplified version of the director task, pairs of participants engaged in naturalistic object-movement instructions while EEG and gaze data were recorded and synchronized via LabStreamingLayer, allowing us to calculate overlap-corrected, regression-based event-related potentials (rERPs) time-locked to spoken nouns and to participants' fixations, focusing on the N400/P300 (300-500 ms) and later (500-800 ms) time windows. Our results show that gaze behavior and fixation-related potentials provide crucial information for interpreting language-related ERPs: Targets competing with occluded referents elicited a stronger posterior positivity consistent with greater attentional demands. Fixation timing systematically modulated neural responses. Contrary to predictions, competitors received little visual attention, indicating that participants prioritized task-relevant information. These findings highlight the potential of multimodal data integration for understanding attentional and predictive mechanisms in real-world communication. Importantly, we show that established analytic techniques, such as artifact subspace reconstruction, independent component analysis, and linear deconvolution for ERP calculation, apply to noisy, naturalistic datasets. In addition, we provide a subsampling sensitivity approach to test the stability of the effects across different sample sizes. This study provides a methodological framework linking gaze and neural activity during interactive language processing. All preprocessing and analysis scripts, along with example datasets, are openly available on OSF ( https://osf.io/5ds4z ; a modified and optimized Python implementation is also available on GitHub: https://github.com/XlinCLab/DGAME ).

secondary.title: Along-tract statistical mapping of white matter abnormalities in children with SeLECTS.
secondary.abstract: BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: Emerging evidence suggests that self-limited epilepsy with centrotemporal spikes (SeLECTS) may reflect atypical neurodevelopment. As WM maturation extends from the second trimester through adolescence, this study aimed to identify regions of delayed or aberrant white matter (WM) development in children with SeLECTS using along-tract statistical mapping for precise localization of microstructural alterations. MATERIALS AND METHODS: 38 children with SeLECTS and 31 healthy controls underwent diffusion-weighted MRI scan. Fractional anisotropy (FA), mean diffusivity (MD), and radial diffusivity (RD) were derived from the diffusion tensor model. Whole-brain tractography was performed using deterministic EuDX tracking and registered to a standardized bundle atlas in MNI space. Thirty WM tracts per subject were extracted. Linear mixed models within the BUAN tractometry framework were used to assess segment wise group differences, while partial correlations were performed to evaluate associations between diffusion metrics and cognitive performance. FDR correction was applied per bundle for all comparisons. RESULTS: After FDR correction, children with SeLECTS showed increased MD in the forceps minor, midbody of the corpus callosum, right corticospinal tract, right extreme capsule, and bilateral uncinate fasciculi. MD values in the affected WM segments showed negative correlations with performance and full-scale IQ, and the segments showing significant correlations overlapped with those showing significant group differences. CONCLUSIONS: SeLECTS is associated with MD-based microstructural alterations in superficial frontal, temporal, and parietal pathways, potentially indicating delayed white matter maturation.

secondary.title: ASFNR Clinical State of Practice Statement on Imaging of Chronic Subdural Hematoma.
secondary.abstract: BACKGROUND: The efficacy of middle meningeal artery embolization (MMAE) for chronic subdural hematoma (cSDH) has heightened interest in imaging biomarkers that may reflect neomembrane activity, predict recurrence, and identify patients most likely to benefit from treatment. Characterization of hematoma internal architecture, referred to as the imaging phenotype, may provide indirect information regarding the biological activity and maturation of the neomembrane. However, imaging phenotype has not been incorporated into randomized trials or validated treatment-selection algorithms, and standardized definitions and reporting remain lacking. METHODS: The American Society of Functional Neuroradiology Clinical Practice Committee developed this State of Practice statement through expert consensus and review of the available literature. KEY MESSAGE: Noncontrast CT (NCCT) remains the primary imaging modality for cSDH assessment. Hematoma burden should be characterized by maximum thickness measured perpendicular to the inner table, midline shift, and, when appropriate, volume. Volume may be estimated using the ABC/2 formula, whereas segmentation is more accurate for irregular, crescentic, or multiloculated collections when available. Internal architecture should be described using the Nakaguchi framework of homogeneous, laminar, separated, and trabecular phenotypes, with mixed or transitional features explicitly reported. Advanced techniques, including dual-energy CT, photon-counting CT, MRI, and arterial spin labeling, may provide information regarding membrane activity but are supported by limited, largely single-center evidence and currently have a problem-solving rather than routine role. Standardized reporting and prospective validation are needed before imaging phenotype or advanced-imaging biomarkers can guide treatment selection.

secondary.title: A Cloud-Enabled LIMS-QMS Platform With Large Language Model-Assisted Standard Operating Procedure Generation for GLP/GMP-Aligned Theranostics Laboratory Operations.
secondary.abstract: Theranostic development centers operate under stringent good laboratory practice (GLP) and good manufacturing practice (GMP) requirements that fragmented, paper-based workflows cannot adequately support. This paper presents the design, regulatory compliance mapping, and pilot deployment of the Laboratory Tracking Software (LTS) platform, a cloud-ready, web-based system that unifies laboratory information management system (LIMS) and quality management system (QMS) functions under a risk-based Computer Software Assurance (CSA) framework aligned with U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) 21 CFR Part 11 and ISO/IEC 17025. The platform operationalizes a 6×6 deterministic request-and-service lifecycle across nine governance modules and embeds a large language model (LLM)-assisted module that, from a single service-name input, generates structured standard operating procedures (SOPs), identifies required consumables and instruments, performs operational risk assessment, and proposes an executable workflow. Pilot deployment across 187 laboratory requests is reported descriptively (23-day mean turnaround time, 1,456 quality-control checkpoints, and 43 deviation-handling episodes); because no comparable pre-deployment dataset could be reconstructed, these values are not interpreted as efficiency or error-reduction gains. A 21 CFR Part 11-aligned control matrix and a CSA-based verification package document authenticated electronic approvals, activity records, two-factor authentication (2FA), and role-based access control (RBAC); a consolidated high-risk user-acceptance campaign executed 31 of 31 scripted scenarios successfully, with independent reviewer and approver sign-off still pending. Beyond the original single BRAF droplet digital PCR (ddPCR) illustrative case, a document-level evaluation was performed across a locked corpus of 20 laboratory services (10 analysis and 10 synthesis workflows). All 280 mandatory template elements were present (100.0% template adherence), and none of the 80 predefined automated document-control checks was flagged (0.0%). Expert-adjudicated error rate, human edit distance, and time saving were not measured and are deferred to a prospective follow-up study. Comparative analysis against QT9 ERP/QMS, RAMS®, and SENAITE LIMS positions the platform as a governance-first, theranostic-specific informatics system with native LLM-assisted documentation generation, a capability absent from existing commercial and open-source alternatives. The results indicate that integrating LLM-assisted document generation into a regulated laboratory informatics platform is technically feasible; however, given the hallucination risk documented in the medical LLM literature, systematic human-in-the-loop validation of generated content remains a prerequisite for unsupervised deployment in GLP/GMP settings. The revised design description additionally specifies a template-constrained prompting strategy, a generation-record schema supporting prompt and output reconstruction, a model-change-control procedure, an explicit LLM data-privacy boundary, and alignment with the January 2026 FDA/EMA guiding principles of good artificial intelligence (AI) practice in drug development.

secondary.title: Improving Data Quality, Model Transparency and Performance in Lung Histopathology with Explainable AI.
secondary.abstract: Convolutional neural networks (CNNs) have shown strong capabilities for image analysis. However, deploying these models in medical settings is complicated by their limited transparency. Over recent years, many approaches have been developed to overcome the so-called "black box" problem of deep neural networks. Here, we show how such explainable AI (XAI) approaches can be applied to not only improve transparency but also training data quality and model performance, with classification of lung damage in histopathology images as use case. First, we conducted a thorough exploratory data analysis and visually compared the compressed multi-dimensional representations of the histology images from the last CNN layers with labels given by pathologists to reveal flaws in the training data. Second, we used Gradient-based Class Activation Mapping (Grad-CAM) as well as SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) values to identify image regions that significantly contributed to the model decisions. To overcome identified shortcomings, we then finetuned additional top layers of the CNNs and introduced model architectures with attention which improved model performance. In summary, we developed a practical workflow that uses interpretability analyses to examine model perception, assess label consistency, and guide model refinement on the example of lung histopathology scoring, demonstrating how XAI approaches can increase both transparency and model performance. The code for this paper is shared at https://github.com/Aitslab/Histology_XAI.git.

secondary.title: Integrative genetic analyses for drug repurposing identify emodin as a candidate modulator of STAT3 signaling in abdominal aortic aneurysm.
secondary.abstract: Abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA) is a life-threatening vascular disease lacking effective pharmacological therapies. To identify potential therapeutic targets and candidate compounds, we performed integrative genetic analyses for drug repurposing by combining Mendelian randomization (MR), summary-data-based Mendelian randomization (SMR), and Bayesian colocalization. This framework prioritized multiple druggable candidates, among which STAT3 emerged as a key regulatory node. Subsequent functional studies demonstrated that emodin suppressed vascular smooth muscle cell proliferation, migration, phenotypic switching, and inflammatory responses. These effects were accompanied by reduced STAT3 phosphorylation and nuclear localization. Molecular docking suggested a potential binding mode of emodin within the STAT3 SH2 domain, while cellular thermal shift assays demonstrated thermal stabilization of STAT3 by emodin in intact cells, consistent with target engagement. Notably, emodin and the selective STAT3 inhibitor STAT3-IN-13 produced comparable effects, and co-treatment did not yield additive efficacy, suggesting overlapping mechanisms. In vivo, emodin attenuated aneurysm development and reduced vascular inflammation in experimental models. Collectively, these findings identify emodin as a candidate modulator of AAA progression acting through suppression of STAT3-associated signaling pathways, and demonstrate the potential of genetic evidence-guided drug repurposing strategies in complex vascular diseases.

secondary.title: Artificial intelligence in personalized internal dosimetry for radiopharmaceutical therapy: a narrative mini-review.
secondary.abstract: Personalized internal radiation dosimetry supports individualized radiopharmaceutical therapy but remains difficult to implement because workflows require repeated quantitative imaging, segmentation, registration, kinetic modeling, and absorbed-dose calculation. This mini-review summarizes current evidence on artificial intelligence across the personalized dosimetry workflow and considers clinical readiness. A narrative PubMed search was completed in early 2026 and covered peer-reviewed studies published from 2015 to early 2026. Studies addressing artificial intelligence, machine learning, or deep learning in quantitative image reconstruction, segmentation, registration, time-activity curve estimation, absorbed-dose calculation, or clinical decision support were considered. Studies reporting quantitative performance or validation results were prioritized. Deep learning reduced yttrium-90 single-photon emission computed tomography reconstruction error from 149.5% ± 31.2% to 9.2% ± 1.7%; lesion dose-rate error was 8.6% ± 5.7% in virtual-patient testing. Learning-based registration reduced computation time from about 50 s to under 6 s. Single-time-point approaches can simplify imaging, and recent machine learning work has explored prediction of organ effective half-life. Automated segmentation methods show improving reproducibility, whereas evidence for artificial intelligence-based clinical decision support remains mainly retrospective and single-center. Artificial intelligence applications in reconstruction and segmentation appear closer to clinical readiness, while decision-support applications still require prospective, multicenter validation.

secondary.title: Computerized fine motor assessment in Parkinson's Disease: Task-specific measures provide complementary clinical information.
secondary.abstract: BACKGROUND: Fine motor impairment is a common feature of Parkinson's disease (PD) and contributes substantially to functional disability. Although the Movement Disorder Society-Unified Parkinson's Disease Rating Scale (MDS-UPDRS Part III) remains the standard clinical tool for motor evaluation, quantitative computerized assessments may provide complementary task-specific information. OBJECTIVES: This cross-sectional case-control study compared fine motor performance measured using the Motorische Leistungs-Serie (MLS) between 19 patients with idiopathic PD and 20 healthy controls and examined associations between MLS-derived parameters and clinical motor severity. METHODS: Motor performance was evaluated using five MLS subtests covering aiming behavior, hand steadiness, precision arm-hand coordination, speed arm-hand, and speed wrist-finger tasks. RESULTS: After adjustment for age, sex, and educational level, patients with PD showed significantly poorer overall fine motor performance, as reflected by the Composite Motor Performance Score, together with significant impairments in selected task-specific measures of aiming performance and visuomotor tracking. Several MLS-derived parameters, particularly aiming duration and hand steadiness, were significantly associated with MDS-UPDRS Part III scores. CONCLUSION: These findings suggest that MLS-derived task-specific measures provide objective quantitative information that complements conventional clinical motor assessment in Parkinson's disease. Analysis of individual task-specific parameters may provide complementary clinically relevant information beyond a single global composite score. However, larger prospective studies are required to determine the clinical utility of task-specific computerized fine motor assessment for monitoring disease progression and treatment response.

secondary.title: A contactless approach for accurate sleep stage detection using the Sleepal AI Lamp.
secondary.abstract: Objective.To validate the accuracy and clinical feasibility of a noncontact radar system (Sleepal AI Lamp) for assessing sleep architecture and staging. Although noncontact radar sensors can capture respiratory and motor mechanics without physical attachment, robust validation in large-scale, pathologically diverse cohorts remains scarce.Approach.Nocturnal respiratory and body movement signals were assessed in 1022 adults using simultaneous measurements from a frequency-modulated continuous-wave bedside radar and gold-standard Polysomnography. The cohort included individuals with normal sleep profiles and patients with varying severities of obstructive sleep apnea. A frequency-augmented deep learning architecture interpreted these respiratory and movement signals.Main results.In the independent validation set, binary sleep-wake classification achieved 92.7% accuracy, a Cohen's kappa of 0.792, 96.4% sleep sensitivity, 80.8% sleep specificity, and a macro-averagedF1 score of 0.896. Four-stage classification (Wake, Light, Deep, and rapid eye movement (REM) sleep) achieved 77.2% accuracy, a Cohen's kappa of 0.677, a macro-averagedF1 score of 0.768, and balanced accuracy/macro-recall of 77.4%, with stage-specificF1 scores of 0.839, 0.740, 0.691, and 0.802 for Wake, Light, Deep, and REM, respectively.Significance.The findings support the validity of the 60 GHz radar-based system for automated assessment of sleep macrostructure. By capturing stage-specific respiratory and movement phenotypes without physical attachment, this technology may provide an unobtrusive tool for home-based screening, longitudinal recovery tracking, and population-level sleep epidemiology.

secondary.title: Wavelet Scalogram-Based Nystagmus Classification for Automated Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo Subtype Diagnosis.
secondary.abstract: Benign paroxysmal positional vertigo (BPPV) is the most common cause of vestibular vertigo, yet accurate diagnosis remains challenging without specialist expertise. This study aimed to develop and evaluate an artificial intelligence (AI)-based diagnostic algorithm for BPPV using video-nystagmography (VNG) recordings. A total of 1352 VNG recordings were collected from patients with posterior semicircular canal (PSCC) BPPV (n = 234), lateral semicircular canal (LSCC) BPPV (canalolithiasis, n = 188; cupulolithiasis, n = 58), and healthy controls (n = 224) at a single tertiary referral hospital, yielding 1738 signal segments (1312 nystagmus segments annotated by two otolaryngologists and 426 normal segments). Eye trajectory signals were extracted using a deep learning-based VNG eye-tracking algorithm, transformed into two-dimensional (2D) scalogram representations via continuous wavelet transform (CWT), and classified using task-specific backbone architectures selected through systematic comparison under a patient-level data split. Ablation analysis showed that CWT-based 2D representations significantly outperformed raw one-dimensional (1D) time-series baselines. The final models achieved area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) values of 0.974 for horizontal and 0.961 for torsional nystagmus classification. For BPPV subtype diagnosis, recording-level accuracy was 0.935 for the PSCC and 0.938 for the LSCC evaluation; F1-scores exceeded 0.84 for all PSCC classes and ranged from 0.59 to 0.98 for LSCC classes, with canalolithiasis variants outperforming cupulolithiasis variants. These findings suggest the feasibility of AI-assisted BPPV diagnosis from VNG recordings.

secondary.title: A single-particle tracking framework for quantifying intracellular partition free energies.
secondary.abstract: Biomolecular condensates are membrane-less organelles that locally enrich specific molecules at spatial sites. A central challenge is determining the physical parameters of individual condensates, as their dimensions are typically below the diffraction limit of conventional microscopy. Single-particle tracking overcomes this limitation, but robust methods for extracting physical observables from trajectory collections remain scarce. Here, we present a framework for inferring the potential difference between molecules inside a condensate and those in the surrounding environment. We introduce a correction that accounts for condensate motion during acquisition, enabling reliable density estimation even from sparse data. After testing on in silico data, we apply our approach to 5 experimental datasets of proteins active in DNA repair and separate them based on the liquid nature of the focus.

secondary.title: Benchmarking three simple DNA staining-based image metrics for live-cell tracking of chromatin organization.
secondary.abstract: Quantifying chromatin-state dynamics in living cells remains challenging, in part because most methods require fixation or cell lysis. Here, we introduce two simple DNA image-derived metrics - Diffuse Signal Index (DSI)and 1-Gini - and benchmark them against the coefficient of variation (CV) as fixation-free readouts of chromatin reorganization. Leveraging the pronounced compact-to-decompact chromatin transition of NETosis, we show that all three metrics track progressive chromatin reorganization, with DSI providing the strongest trajectory-level discrimination between NETing and non-NETing cells. All three metrics also correlate with ATAC-see-based chromatin accessibility measurement in fixed cells, supporting their biological interpretability. In dividing cells, the metrics capture mitotic chromatin compaction and post-mitotic decompaction, demonstrating applicability in diverse biological processes. Together, these results provide a practical framework for extracting readouts of chromatin reorganization from routine live-cell DNA staining. We also provide NucMetrics, an open-source ImageJ/Fiji macro toolset for easily computing CV, DSI and 1-Gini.

secondary.title: Toward Personalized Surgeons' Cognitive Workload: A Linear Mixed-Effects Model Analysis of EEG Features.
secondary.abstract: Surgical Flow Disruptions in the operating room can increase cognitive workload and the risk of technical errors. While electroencephalography (EEG) provides an objective framework for monitoring mental effort, traditional statistical methods often rely on group-level analysis. This approach potentially ignores the significant degree of inter-subject variability among individuals. This study evaluated the effectiveness of various EEG features in monitoring the impact of SFDs using a Linear Mixed-Effects Model (LMEM) framework to distinguish between group trends and individual-specific responses. EEG data were recorded from nine surgical trainees during a simulated microvascular anastomosis, during which participants were subjected to six predefined SFDs, including auditory alerts and visual distractions. EEG features were analyzed using LMEM with random intercepts and slopes, and a subjectivity index was introduced to quantify the degree of individualization across 36 extracted EEG features. An initial analysis of variance on the fixed effects revealed that, generally, theta and beta power bands were significantly impacted by disruptions across the group. However, the subjectivity index identified several features, such as Gamma Asymmetry, that exhibited high individualization despite the absence of a significant group trend. Features characterized by both significant fixed effects and high subjectivity indices, such as Mean Power Beta, were identified as the most reliable metrics for tracking cognitive load. These results demonstrate that traditional group-averaging methods can mask critical individual physiological responses. By utilizing LMEM and the associated subjectivity index, this research establishes a statistical foundation for developing personalized intraoperative monitoring systems tailored to a surgeon's unique cognitive profile.

secondary.title: Application of digital pathology to assess the effect of hormone treatment on placental histomorphometry in mares with induced ascending placentitis.
secondary.abstract: This study aimed to evaluate the effects of hormonal treatments with altrenogest (ALT) and estradiol cypionate (ECP) on placental histomorphometry in mares with experimentally induced ascending placentitis, using digital pathology as a quantitative tool. Thirty pregnancies from 27 Criollo-type mares were assigned to six groups: healthy controls (n = 5); basic treatment (n = 5), treated with trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole (TSM), and flunixin meglumine (FM); ALT group (n = 5) + basic treatment; ECP group (n = 5) + basic treatment; ALT + ECP group (n = 5) in addition to basic treatment; and an untreated placentitis group (n = 5). Following parturition, chorioallantoic samples were collected from the cervical star, uterine body, and both horns. Digital images were analyzed using NIH ImageJ software to quantify microcotyledonary and capillary areas per field. Gestation length in the ECP group was comparable to that of the healthy controls, while placental weight and expulsion time did not differ significantly among groups. Histomorphometric analysis revealed that mares in the ECP group exhibited significantly increased capillary area and total microcotyledonary area compared to other placentitis groups. These results suggest that ECP enhances placental vascularization and microstructure in mares with ascending placentitis. The findings support the therapeutic potential of ECP in promoting placental recovery and maintaining uterine homeostasis. Additionally, this study highlights the utility of digital pathology in the quantitative assessment of equine placental morphology, providing new perspectives for improving therapeutic strategies in the management of placentitis.

secondary.title: Multi-scale ROI-based SEM image analysis of processing time and magnification effects in lignocellulosic biomass.
secondary.abstract: Quantitative characterization of treatment-induced microstructural evolution in lignocellulosic biomass using scanning electron microscopy (SEM) is challenging because image-derived descriptors are affected by both processing-induced structural changes and imaging magnification, limiting direct comparison of measurements. This study presents an ROI-based multi-scale SEM image analysis methodology for evaluating process-induced microstructural evolution and magnification-dependent descriptor behavior, demonstrated using ball-milled mustard seed husk as a representative case study. GLCM (gray-level co-occurrence matrix) texture features, including entropy (spatial randomness in gray-level relationships) and contrast, and pore characteristics were quantified from SEM images obtained at different milling stages and magnifications. Increasing GLCM entropy, contrast, and pore count, together with decreasing mean pore area, indicated progressive surface fragmentation. Entropy showed relatively low magnification sensitivity, whereas contrast and pore count were strongly scale-dependent. Pore area showed convergence at selected scales, indicating improved measurement consistency. Two-way analysis of variance (ANOVA) showed significant effects of milling time and magnification on all descriptors (p<0.001); the interaction was significant for contrast, entropy, and pore count, but not for pore area (p=0.150). The proposed framework provides a standardized approach for quantitative SEM characterization of heterogeneous lignocellulosic microstructures by considering both processing duration and imaging magnification.
