secondary.title: Tracking biomolecular pathogenesis and recovery in neonatal calf diarrhea via serum infrared spectroscopy.
secondary.abstract: Neonatal calf diarrhea (NCD) is an important health and economic problem in dairy cattle production because of its association with morbidity, mortality, and production losses. Moving beyond basic diagnostic classification, this study aims to track the biomolecular pathogenesis and recovery in NCD by evaluating host-level molecular damage using serum ATR-FTIR spectroscopy. Serum samples obtained from 1 to 20-day-old Holstein calves were analyzed in the mid-infrared spectral range, and the integral areas, bandwidths, and spectrochemical indices of critical bands were calculated. During the active disease phase, profound biomolecular reorganization was observed. Serum lipid acyl-chain order, packing, and mobility were severely disrupted, as evidenced by decreases in the 2922 cm-1 band area, its bandwidth, and the A2922/A2966 and Bw2922/Bw2966 indices. Moreover, the increase in the A1740/A1540 ratio reflect a disease-induced disruption of the serum lipid-protein balance. Furthermore, a pronounced release of RNA and nucleic acid components was detected, indicated by increased PO₂-, RNA ribose, and C-O-C band areas, as well as elevated nucleic acid-to-protein ratios (A1080/A1540 and A(1240+1080)/A(1650+1540)). In the recovered group, these structural and molecular aberrations systematically shifted back toward the healthy profile. ROC analyses showed that the spectrochemical parameters studied have high discriminatory potential for tracking disease activity and resolution. Overall, the findings suggest serum infrared spectroscopy as a robust, non-invasive framework not only for elucidating the molecular footprint of active pathogenesis but also for monitoring structural tissue recovery from sera in NCD.

secondary.title: RV-mixer: Random Fourier and variance-guided global feature learning for medical image segmentation.
secondary.abstract: Hybrid CNN-Transformer architectures have achieved promising performance in medical image segmentation, yet the high computational cost of self-attention limits their application in resource-constrained clinical scenarios. Moreover, medical images exhibit domain-specific challenges, including ultrasound speckle noise, low contrast, and ambiguous lesion boundaries, which require robust feature representation beyond conventional local modeling. To address these issues, we propose RV-Mixer, a lightweight module for efficient global representation learning with medical-domain priors. Instead of explicit attention-based token interaction, RV-Mixer employs Random Fourier Features (RFF) to project local representations into a shared frequency-domain embedding space, providing nonlinear feature enhancement with low computational overhead. Furthermore, Variance-Guided Channel Recalibration (VGCR) introduces global statistical aggregation through channel-wise variance modeling, enabling adaptive emphasis of discriminative pathological textures and lesion boundaries that may be weakened by mean-based feature aggregation. Extensive experiments on five public medical image segmentation datasets, covering ultrasound, endoscopy, dermoscopy, and MRI scenarios, demonstrate that RV-Mixer achieves competitive or superior performance compared with Transformer-, MLP-, and Mamba-based approaches while maintaining fewer parameters and lower computational complexity. These results highlight the effectiveness of domain-informed frequency representation and statistical global aggregation for efficient and robust medical image segmentation.

secondary.title: A novel frequency tracking method based on improved ESC control method for megasonic cleaning system.
secondary.abstract: To address the issue of poor frequency tracking accuracy in conventional frequency tracking algorithms for megasonic cleaning systems under continuous operating conditions, this paper proposes a maximum current tracking method based on an improved ESC (Extremum Seeking Control) algorithm. First, the expression for the dynamic branch current of the megasonic transducer is derived. The relationship between the input current corresponding to the voltage driving pole and the dynamic branch current near the resonant frequency is established. To compensate for the limited sampling rate of ADC (Analog-to-Digital Converter) chips, a smoothing algorithm based on CIC (Cascaded Integrator-Comb) interpolation is proposed, and the effectiveness in peak-seeking is verified through simulation. The control experiments confirm that, in the megahertz frequency domain, the CIC current sampling method demonstrates higher sampling accuracy when compared to the existing sampling methods. Dual - channel sampling experiments verify the effectiveness of the proposed method for extracting dynamic branch currents. Subsequently, an improved ESC frequency tracking method is introduced, which combines peak-seeking techniques with maximum dynamic current tracking. Experimental results demonstrate that the extremum-seeking method proposed in this paper can effectively track the resonance frequency of the megasonic generation system and significantly enhance the driving current of the megasonic transducer. Comparative experiments show that, compared with existing control methods, the frequency tracking method presented in this paper can provide a higher driving current and a greater acoustic pressure output for megasonic transducers, thus significantly improving the cleaning efficiency of megasonic cleaning systems.

secondary.title: Fixed-phase resonance tracking for fast Nonlinear Resonant Ultrasound Spectroscopy.
secondary.abstract: Nonlinear Resonant Ultrasound Spectroscopy (NRUS) experiments that rely on repeated sampling of resonance curves are inherently sensitive to measurement protocol due to evolution of material parameters caused by fast and slow dynamic effects. We introduce a model-assisted discrete-time resonance tracking method that maintains a system at its instantaneous resonance condition without the need to acquire full frequency sweeps. Resonance is defined through a prescribed phase relation between excitation and response, and the excitation frequency is iteratively updated using a linearized frequency-phase model. The procedure allows controlled suppression of transient wave buildup using optional feedforward correction with respect to an external control parameter. The method is demonstrated on NRUS and performing a conditioning-relaxation protocol, both conducted on a sandstone bar, providing estimates of resonance frequency and damping. Comparison with conventional approaches shows that measurement speed and mode stability significantly influence the inferred nonlinear indicators. The proposed framework is not limited to nonlinear acoustics and can be applied to arbitrary resonant systems with slowly evolving parameters.

secondary.title: HFFNet: Hierarchical feature fusion network for lightweight RGB-T semantic segmentation.
secondary.abstract: In recent years, the integration of RGB and thermal infrared (TIR) images has shown great potential in advancing semantic segmentation, particularly under challenging conditions such as low-light environments and cluttered backgrounds. However, existing models often suffer from inefficient multi-modal feature fusion and high computational cost. To address these issues and achieve high segmentation accuracy with low complexity, we propose a hierarchical feature fusion network (i.e., HFFNet) for lightweight RGB-T semantic segmentation. Specifically, HFFNet introduces a multi-scale feature fusion (MFF) module that operates on mid-level and high-level encoder features from both modalities. The MFF module employs a parallel-cascade structure with depthwise separable convolutions of varying dilation rates (dilated DSConv) to extract multi-scale features efficiently. Furthermore, a two-stage fusion strategy is adopted: first to merge RGB and TIR features at each individual scale, and then to combine all scales for enhanced cross-modal representation. To further enhance object localization, we design a hierarchical integration (HI) module to align and aggregate multi-level fused features, thereby combining high-level semantic information with low-level spatial details. Extensive experiments on two public RGB-T datasets clearly demonstrate that our HFFNet not only achieves superior segmentation accuracy compared to state-of-the-art methods but also maintains low computational complexity, making it suitable for real-time GPU inference and resource-constrained RGB-T segmentation scenarios.

secondary.title: FARCLUSS: fuzzy adaptive rebalancing and contrastive uncertainty learning for semi-supervised semantic segmentation.
secondary.abstract: Semi-supervised semantic segmentation (SSSS) faces persistent challenges in effectively leveraging unlabeled data, including ineffective utilization of pseudo-labels, the exacerbation of class imbalance biases, and the neglect of prediction uncertainty. Moreover, current approaches often discard uncertain regions through strict thresholding, thereby favouring dominant classes. To address these limitations, we introduce a holistic framework that transforms uncertainty into a learning asset through four principal components: (1) fuzzy pseudo-labeling, which preserves soft class distributions from top-K predictions to enrich supervision; (2) uncertainty-aware dynamic weighting, that modulates pixel-wise contributions via entropy-based reliability scores; (3) adaptive class rebalancing, which dynamically adjusts the loss to counteract long-tailed class distributions; and (4) lightweight contrastive regularization, that encourages compact and discriminative feature embeddings. Extensive experiments on Pascal VOC and Cityscapes demonstrate that our method outperforms current state-of-the-art approaches, with pronounced gains on under-represented classes and ambiguous boundary regions.

secondary.title: FASFF: Frequency domain information-aided spatial domain feature fusion for RGBT tracking.
secondary.abstract: RGBT object tracking takes advantage of the complementary properties of RGB and thermal infrared (TIR) modalities. However, many existing methods focus on fusion within a single domain, either spatial or frequency, without fully exploiting the complementarity of multiple domains. This limits the interaction between domains and makes trackers less robust under severe conditions. To improve feature representation by leveraging both spatial and frequency information, we propose a Frequency domain information-Aided Spatial domain Feature Fusion framework for RGBT tracking (FASFF), which mainly consists of the Frequency domain Attention Enhancement Module (FAEM) and the Spatial-Frequency feature interaction Fusion Module (SFFM). The FAEM employs the Discrete Cosine Transform Attention block (DCTAttn), which highlights informative frequency components while integrating spatial and frequency domains information, and the Cross-modality Collaborative Attention block (CCAttn), which suppresses noise via cross-modal feature refinement to enhance intra-modality feature representation. The SFFM further harnesses the interaction between the spatial and frequency domains to collaboratively refine feature representation, leveraging complementary information from the frequency domain to enhance spatial domain representations. We evaluate the FASFF on three benchmark datasets: RGBT210, RGBT234, and LasHeR. The experimental results show that the FASFF maintains stable and reliable performance across different tracking scenarios, verifying its effectiveness for RGBT object tracking.

primary.title: cAMP signaling promotes acute lysosome biogenesis through TFEB nuclear import-export dynamics.
primary.abstract: Cyclic adenosine monophosphate (cAMP) signaling is a major stimulus for lipid and glucose catabolism, yet catabolic processes like these can also coordinate with lysosome-dependent degradation. However, the impact of cAMP signaling on lysosomal dynamics remains unclear. Transcription factor EB (TFEB), a master regulator of lysosomal biogenesis, is regulated by stimulus-dependent nuclear-cytoplasmic shuttling through a variety of phosphorylation events. Here, we find that elevating intracellular cAMP with forskolin and IBMX induces rapid nuclear import of TFEB-GFP within 30 minutes and coincides with a transient upregulation of TFEB target lysosome genes. By 8 hours, TFEB returns to the cytoplasm, accompanied by transcriptional downregulation. Inhibition of cAMP-dependent protein kinase A (PKA) using H89 did not block nuclear import but unexpectedly caused sustained nuclear accumulation, indicating that PKA promotes TFEB nuclear export. Consistent with this, phosphoproteomic profiling revealed increased phosphorylation of a PKA-consensus motif (RRxS) during the export phase. These findings suggest that cAMP-PKA signaling plays a novel role in temporally "tuning" lysosomal gene expression by regulating TFEB nuclear-cytoplasmic shuttling.

primary.title: TBK1-mediated phosphorylation of WIPI2 links bacteria recognition to autophagosome formation in xenophagy.
primary.abstract: Xenophagy, a selective autophagy pathway, is a critical innate immune defense mechanism that targets pathogens for lysosomal degradation. However, the molecular mechanisms enabling autophagosomes to specifically recognize and engulf bacteria remain incompletely understood. Here, we identify WIPI2, a core component that drives autophagosome biogenesis, as a novel phosphorylation substrate of TBK1 during Salmonella Typhimurium infection. We demonstrate that TBK1 phosphorylates WIPI2 at Ser96, which enhances its interaction with ATG16L1 and its binding to PtdIns3P. Crucially, the recruitment of WIPI2 to intracellular bacteria is dependent on its interaction with ATG16L1, which is localized to the Salmonella-containing vacuole. Furthermore, TBK1-mediated phosphorylation of WIPI2 is required for efficient bacterial clearance. Collectively, our findings reveal a molecular mechanism whereby TBK1-mediated phosphorylation of WIPI2 directs localized phagophore expansion around invading bacteria, thereby bridging bacterial recognition with autophagosome assembly.Abbreviations: ATG: autophagy related; ATG5: autophagy related 5; ATG16L1: autophagy related 16 like 1; CALCOCO2/NDP52: calcium binding and coiled-coil domain 2; CFU: colony-forming units; GFP: green fluorescent protein; GST: glutathione S-transferase; IL6: interleukin 6; KO: knockout; LPS: lipopolysaccharides; MAP1LC3/LC3: microtubule associated protein 1 light chain 3; OPTN: optineurin; PtdIns: phosphatidylinositol; PtdIns3P: phosphatidylinositol-3-phosphate; RB1CC1/FIP200: RB1 inducible coiled-coil 1; RFP: red fluorescent protein;S. primary.title: Tet1-mediated 5-hydroxymethylcytosine alterations in the olfactory bulb are associated with aberrant neurogenesis and PI3K-Akt signaling in response to CIH.
primary.abstract: Chronic intermittent hypoxia (CIH), a key feature of obstructive sleep apnea, impairs central nervous system function, but its effects on olfactory bulb (OB) and epigenetic mechanisms are unclear. We show that CIH causes olfactory behavioral deficits in mice with structural and molecular OB changes. CIH disrupted adult OB neurogenesis, increasing the immature neuron marker doublecortin (DCX) and reducing mature NeuN expression, and activated microglia. At the molecular level, CIH markedly upregulated the DNA demethylation enzyme Tet1 and global 5-hydroxymethylcytosine (5hmC) levels, which were accompanied by aberrant activation of the PI3K-Akt pathway. Importantly, Tet1 knockdown in the OB partially normalized PI3K-Akt signaling, was associated with improved neurogenesis markers, and alleviated CIH-induced olfactory dysfunction. These results suggest that Tet1-dependent epigenetic remodeling represents an important molecular mechanism linking CIH to OB dysfunction, and that Tet1 may serve as a potential therapeutic target for CIH-related sensory impairment.

primary.title: Astrocytic TRPC6 protects against cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury by inhibiting cGAS-STING pathway.
primary.abstract: OBJECTIVE: Cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury (CIRI) is complicated by BBB breakdown and neuroinflammation, processes partially regulated by astrocytes. This study aimed to investigate the neuroprotective mechanism of astrocyte-specific TRPC6, focusing on elucidating its molecular link to the cGAS-STING pathway and BBB integrity. METHODS: MCAO mouse models were established, with astrocyte-specific TRPC6 overexpression achieved via stereotactic injection of AAV-GFAP-Trpc6. Neurological function, infarct volume, apoptosis, and BBB integrity (including tight junction proteins and AQP4) were systematically assessed. In vitro, OGD/R conditioned medium culture and co-culture were used for mechanistic validation, with the STING agonist ADU-S100 employed for intervention and causality confirmation. RESULTS: Astrocyte TRPC6 overexpression significantly improved neurological function and behavioral outcomes, reduced infarct volume, and inhibited neuronal apoptosis. TRPC6 overexpression also stabilized the BBB, shown by reduced cerebral edema, reversed tight junction protein (ZO-1/Occludin) loss, and decreased AQP4 expression. Mechanistic analysis confirmed that TRPC6 overexpression significantly suppressed CIRI-induced activation of the astrocytic cGAS-STING pathway. The STING agonist ADU-S100 partially reversed the neuroprotective and BBB-stabilizing effects of TRPC6. CONCLUSION: Astrocytic TRPC6 maintains BBB integrity by negatively regulating the cGAS-STING innate immune pathway in the early phase of CIRI. The study identified the "Astrocyte TRPC6-STING-Tight Junction" axis, offering a precise and promising novel therapeutic target for CIRI.

secondary.title: Essential Oils From the Fruit of Amomum villosum Lour. Alleviate LPS-Induced Neuroinflammation by Repressing PI3K-Akt and MAPK Signaling Pathways.
secondary.abstract: Amomum villosum Lour. has been traditionally valued in various cultures for its health benefits. Here, we show that the neuroprotective effects of the essential oils extracted from the fruit of Amomum villosum Lour. (AVEO) and elucidate its underlying mechanisms in lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-induced neuroinflammation. The main compounds of AVEO can cross the blood-brain barrier and significantly improve cognitive and behavioral dysfunction in LPS-induced mice, leading to a 50% enhancement in Morris water maze performance, a 60% and 80% reduction in immobility time in the tail suspension test and forced swimming test, respectively. Moreover, AVEO mitigates neuron loss and suppresses the expression of pro-inflammatory mediators, including TNF-α, IL-1β, and IL-6, while upregulating the anti-inflammatory cytokine IL-10 in brain tissue. RNA-seq and metabonomics analyses reveal that AVEO modulates multiple inflammation-related pathways and restore metabolic homeostasis in brain tissue. Remarkably, AVEO attenuates hyperactivation of the PI3K-Akt and MAPK signaling pathways in LPS-induced microglia and improves neuronal damage in LPS-induced microglia-neuron co-culture system. Altogether, our findings suggest that AVEO alleviates neural dysfunction by modulating PI3K-Akt and MAPK signaling cascades and promoting metabolic reprogramming upon neuroinflammation, thereby revealing the therapeutic potential of AVEO in several neurological disorders.

secondary.title: Targeting the Calcium-mtDNA-cGAS-STING Signaling Nexus: A Novel Redox Mechanism for Nimodipine's Neuroprotection in Traumatic Brain Injury.
secondary.abstract: OBJECTIVE: Traumatic brain injury (TBI) induces severe secondary injury where molecular mechanisms remain unclear. This study investigates the involvement of the cyclic GMP-AMP synthase-stimulator of interferon genes (cGAS-STING) signaling pathway in this process and evaluates the neuroprotective effect of the L-type calcium channel blocker nimodipine, focusing on calcium homeostasis, mitochondrial function, and inflammatory signaling. METHODS: Using primary neuronal and mouse TBI models, we assessed outcomes via fluorescent calcium imaging, JC-1 staining, Western blot, quantitative PCR (qPCR)/reverse transcription-quantitative polymerase chain reaction, enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay, and behavioral tests. Nimodipine was applied to inhibit L-type channels, specifically testing its role in reducing mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) release, blocking cGAS-STING activation, and suppressing neuroinflammation. RESULTS: TBI markedly activated the cGAS-STING pathway, increasing pro-inflammatory factors and apoptosis. In the cellular oxygen-glucose deprivation model, calcium overload was directly observed by Fluo-4 AM staining and was associated with subsequent mitochondrial permeability transition pore opening and mtDNA release, identifying this process as a key upstream event for cGAS-STING activation. Nimodipine inhibited intracellular calcium overload, reduced mitochondrial injury and mtDNA release, and consequently suppressed cGAS-STING pathway activation. Both in vivo and in vitro experiments showed dose-dependent decreases in pro-inflammatory factors, along with improved neurological function and attenuated brain tissue pathology. CONCLUSION: Nimodipine attenuates secondary neuroinflammation and neuronal apoptosis after TBI by inhibiting calcium influx, decreasing mtDNA release, and suppressing cGAS-STING signaling. These results suggest that the Ca2+-mtDNA-cGAS-STING axis contributes to TBI pathology and that nimodipine may serve as a potential multitarget therapy. Antioxid. Redox Signal. 00, 000-000.

secondary.title: Preoperative sleep deprivation prolongs postoperative hyperalgesia by downregulating spinal cord D2R expression via the PP2A/AKT-dependent NMDA receptor phosphorylation.
secondary.abstract: Preoperative sleep deprivation (SD) is known to exacerbate postoperative pain, but the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. Using a male mouse model of 48-hour continuous SD followed by incisional surgery, we found that SD alone induced transient mechanical hyperalgesia, and when combined with surgery (SI group) it significantly aggravated and prolonged postoperative pain recovery until day 10. On postoperative day 7, SI mice showed marked downregulation of spinal dopamine D2 receptor (D2R) expression and decreased spinal dopamine concentration. D2R was predominantly expressed on spinal glutamatergic neurons. Overexpression of D2R on these neurons via intrathecal AAV injection effectively alleviated the prolonged hyperalgesia, normalizing pain sensitivity by day 7. Mechanistically, D2R downregulation led to increased phosphorylation of NMDA receptor subunits (p-NR1 and p-NR2B) without altering total NMDA receptor levels. Co-immunoprecipitation revealed an interaction between D2R and protein phosphatase 2A (PP2A). SI mice exhibited decreased PP2A expression but increased p-AKT, p-GSK3β, and β-catenin, indicating activation of the PP2A/AKT signaling pathway, which were reversed by D2R overexpression. Furthermore, pharmacological activation of PP2A with DT-061 not only downregulated p-AKT, p-GSK3β, β-catenin, p-NR1 and p-NR2B, but also produced significant analgesia in SI mice. Collectively, these results demonstrate that preoperative sleep deprivation prolongs postoperative hyperalgesia by downregulating spinal D2R on glutamatergic neurons, which disinhibits the PP2A/AKT pathway and enhances NMDA receptor phosphorylation. Targeting D2R or its downstream PP2A/AKT signaling may represent a novel therapeutic strategy for managing persistent postoperative pain caused by preoperative sleep deprivation in male mice.

secondary.title: Six3 promoting the migration and neural differentiation of BMSCs via Btg2‑mediated Akt signaling pathway activation: A therapeutic strategy for stroke.
secondary.abstract: Bone marrow‑derived mesenchymal stem cell (BMSC) transplantation holds therapeutic potential for stroke; however, but its effectiveness requires optimization. The transcription factor Sine Oculis Homeobox Homolog 3 (Six3) regulates processes crucial for BMSC therapy, such as neural cell proliferation and differentiation. However, whether Six3‑modified BMSCs exert enhanced therapeutic effects on stroke remains unknown. In the present study, mouse BMSCs were isolated and identified using surface markers. Six3‑overexpressing BMSCs exhibited enhanced proliferative, migratory and neural differentiation capacities. RNA‑sequencing analysis comparing the gene expression profiles of BMSCs with and without Six3 overexpression identified BTG Anti‑Proliferation Factor 2 (Btg2) as an upregulated gene (log2FC=1.45, P<0.05) in Six3‑overexpressing cells. Further investigations revealed that Six3 directly binds to the TGATACTGTCT sequence within the Btg2 promoter and activates its transcription. Btg2 knockdown abolished the effects of Six3 overexpression. Mechanistically, Six3 promoted Akt phosphorylation via Btg2, enhancing BMSC viability and neural differentiation. A mouse model of stroke was established using transient middle cerebral artery occlusion (MCAO, 1.5‑h occlusion and 24‑h reperfusion). BMSCs were administered via tail vein injection at the onset of reperfusion. GFP expression detected in brain tissue at 24 h post‑reperfusion confirmed successful the homing of BMSCs to the brain. The transplantation of Six3‑overexpressing BMSCs ameliorated brain pathology, reducing apoptosis and cerebral infarct volume. Notably, Six3‑modified BMSCs demonstrated a significantly greater therapeutic efficacy than unmodified BMSCs. Collectively, these findings demonstrate that Six3 enhances the therapeutic properties of BMSCs by transcriptionally activating Btg2, which promotes Akt phosphorylation. These findings provide novel mechanistic insight into the optimization of stem cell therapy in stroke.

secondary.title: PDE2A is involved in negative emotional behaviors via the cAMP-PKA signaling pathway in the SPS&S model.
secondary.abstract: BACKGROUND: Post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) is characterized by negative affective symptoms, including anxiety, depression, anhedonia, and fear. The molecular mechanisms underlying these symptoms remain poorly understood. Phosphodiesterase 2A (PDE2A), a regulator of cyclic adenosine monophosphate (cAMP) signaling, has been implicated in neuropsychiatric disorders. OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to investigate the role of the PDE2A-cAMP-protein kinase A (PKA) signaling pathway in negative emotional behaviors induced by traumatic stress. METHODS: Transcriptomic datasets were analyzed to identify differentially expressed genes and enriched pathways. A rat PTSD model was established using single prolonged stress combined with foot shocks (SPS&S). Behavioral tests were performed, and PDE2A-cAMP-PKA signaling alterations in the amygdala were examined. The effects of PDE2A inhibitor Hcyb1 and the PKA inhibitor H89 were evaluated. RESULTS: Bioinformatics analysis identified PDE2A as a hub gene associated with PTSD, with significant enrichment of the cAMP signaling pathway. SPS&S rats exhibited anxiety-, depression-like behaviors, and anhedonia, accompanied by increased PDE2A expression and reduced cAMP and phosphorylated PKA (p-PKA) levels in the amygdala. Hcyb1 treatment alleviated behavioral deficits, decreased PDE2A expression, and restored cAMP and p-PKA signaling. H89 blocked p-PKA activation and partially reversed the behavioral benefits of Hcyb1. CONCLUSION: These findings suggest that amygdala PDE2A-cAMP-PKA signaling is associated with negative emotional behaviors in the SPS&S model. PDE2A inhibition may ameliorate behavioral deficits through PKA-related signaling. However, the peripheral blood transcriptomic data, lack of direct PDE2A activity and cAMP/cGMP measurements, and limited biochemical validation constrain mechanistic interpretation. Further studies using brain-derived datasets and comprehensive biochemical approaches are warranted.

secondary.title: Stigmasterol alleviates central precocious puberty by targeting the IGF-1/PI3K/Akt/mTOR signaling pathway and modulating the Kisspeptin/GnRH axis.
secondary.abstract: BACKGROUND: Central precocious puberty (CPP) results from premature activation of the hypothalamic-pituitary-gonadal axis, causing early sexual development and related health risks. Stigmasterol (ST), a natural phytosterol with diverse pharmacological activities, has not been fully evaluated for CPP. METHODS: This study integrated network pharmacology, molecular docking, and molecular dynamics simulations to identify ST targets in CPP. Experimental validation used an N-Methyl aspartic acid-induced CPP rat model and high-glucose high-fat-stimulated GT1-7 hypothalamic neurons. Techniques included histology, ELISA, qPCR, western blot, and flow cytometry. RESULTS: In silico analyses demonstrated favorable binding of ST to core proteins within the IGF-1/PI3K/Akt/mTOR signaling pathway. In vivo, ST treatment significantly delayed vaginal opening, reduced serum levels of estradiol and testosterone, and ameliorated pathological abnormalities in uterine and ovarian tissues. At the molecular level, ST suppressed the hypothalamic overactivation of the IGF-1/PI3K/Akt/mTOR pathway and attenuated neuronal damage and apoptosis. In vitro, ST inhibited HGHF-induced proliferation, inflammatory cytokine release, and apoptosis in GT1-7 cells, while concurrently modulating the expression of key puberty-related genes and proteins, including those within the Kisspeptin/GnRH axis. Conversely, pharmacological reactivation of PI3K signaling with the agonist 740YP attenuated selected protective effects the protective effects of ST, supporting the functional involvement the PI3K/Akt/mTOR pathway in mediating these benefits. CONCLUSIONS: Stigmasterol exhibits significant therapeutic effects against CPP by concurrently targeting the IGF-1/PI3K/Akt/mTOR and Kisspeptin/GnRH signaling pathways. These findings provide robust preclinical evidence supporting ST as a promising multi-targeted natural candidate for CPP management.

secondary.title: Insulin regulates activity-dependent mitochondrial depolarization and calcium dynamics in dentate granule cells.
secondary.abstract: Systemic insulin resistance is associated with reduced hippocampal energy metabolism and cognitive impairment both in humans and animal models. However, whether insulin rapidly regulates neuronal metabolic stability during activity remains unclear. Here, we examined insulin signaling and queried the corresponding mitochondrial responses in dentate granule cells (DGCs) of adult female mice. This layer of excitatory neurons within the hippocampus plays an essential role in learning and memory. Insulin robustly increased Akt phosphorylation in dentate gyrus tissue when insulin degradation was inhibited, and this response was attenuated by genetic deletion of the insulin receptor in DGCs, consistent with cell-autonomous signaling. We found that insulin did not alter mitochondrial membrane potential at rest, but significantly limited activity-evoked mitochondrial depolarization induced by neuronal stimulation. However, this change had no measurable impact on cytosolic ATP availability and was instead associated with Ca2+ dynamics. Removing Ca2+ ions from the extracellular solution, or disrupting mitochondrial Ca2+ uptake, prevented insulin modulation of the mitochondrial membrane potential. Furthermore, insulin limited cytosolic Ca2+ accumulation through an insulin receptor-dependent mechanism that persisted despite Akt inhibition. Insulin also accelerated the clearance of mitochondrial Ca2+ transients in active neurons, which occurred without changes in either neuronal excitability or pyruvate dehydrogenase phosphorylation. Together, these findings identify endogenous insulin degradation as a key regulator of hippocampal insulin signaling, and reveal a previously unrecognized interaction between insulin and Ca2+ signaling in stimulated DGCs. This work also establishes a direct link between central insulin signaling and the maintenance of mitochondrial electrochemical homeostasis in the adult brain.Significance Statement Insulin signaling is known to influence synaptic plasticity, yet its direct effects on neuronal metabolism remain poorly defined. Here, we show that endogenous insulin degradation limits insulin signaling in adult hippocampal tissue. This finding suggests that inhibitors of the insulin degrading enzyme may hold the potential to improve the efficacy of insulin-based interventions aimed at improving learning and memory. Acute insulin signaling does not modify neuronal excitability, or cytosolic ATP availability. Instead, it stabilizes mitochondrial membrane potential and reduces calcium accumulation in active dentate granule cells. By identifying an insulin-dependent mechanism that regulates the electrochemical homeostasis of mitochondria in active neurons, this work provides insight into how brain insulin resistance may contribute to cognitive dysfunction in aging and neurometabolic disorders.

secondary.title: Molecular Signatures of HIV-Induced Neuroinflammation and Neurodegeneration in Human Cerebral Organoids: Identification of Therapeutic Targets for NeuroHIV.
secondary.abstract: HIV-associated neurological complications remain a major concern in people living with HIV (PWH), even under effective viral suppression with combination antiretroviral therapy (cART), underscoring unresolved mechanisms driving HIV-related neurodegeneration. To address this gap, we used HIV-1-infected human cerebral organoids (hCOs) containing microglia as a physiologically relevant three-dimensional model of the central nervous system (CNS) and validated key findings in the brain region of simian immunodeficiency virus (SIV)-infected, cART-treated rhesus macaque model. Integrated single-nucleus RNA sequencing with ATAC-seq (multi-omics), identifies cell-type-specific alterations in dual innate immune-driven inflammatory signaling pathways across neural and glial populations in hCOs. Microglia were preferentially infected and activated, initiating IL-17A-mediated cascades involving IFN-γ/STAT1, CEBPB, and NF-κB signaling. These pathways converged with cGAS-STING and Notch-NEURL1 signaling, both associated with neuroinflammation and synaptic dysfunction. cART suppressed viral replication, reduced IL-17A-mediated neuroinflammation, improved mitochondrial function, and restored synaptic gene expression. Collectively, these findings identify dysregulation of IL-17A, STAT1, CEBPB, and cGAS-STING signaling as key molecular drivers of HIV-associated neuroinflammation. They also establish a potential mechanistic link between IL-17A signaling and microglial remodeling, providing a translational framework for the development of CNS-targeted therapies in PWH.

secondary.title: YBX3 promotes ischemia-reperfusion injury by enhancing microglial glycolysis via PKM2 stabilization and mTOR-HIF-1α pathway activation.
secondary.abstract: Stroke remains one of the leading causes of death and long-term disability worldwide, with neuroinflammation and metabolic dysfunction playing central roles in its pathogenesis. In this study, we investigated the function of Y-box binding protein 3 (YBX3) in ischemic stroke, with particular focus on its regulation of glycolysis and neuroinflammatory responses. Using a middle cerebral artery occlusion (MCAO) model in C57BL/6 mice and an oxygen-glucose deprivation/reperfusion (OGD/R) model in BV2 microglia, we observed that YBX3 expression was markedly upregulated following ischemia-reperfusion. Overexpression of YBX3 aggravated cerebral infarct size, worsened motor and neurological outcomes, and increased the release of pro-inflammatory cytokines (TNF-α, IL-6, and IL-1β) both in vivo and in vitro. Mechanistically, YBX3 enhanced glycolysis in BV2 cells by stabilizing pyruvate kinase M2 (PKM2) mRNA and promoting its expression, while simultaneously activating glycolysis through the mTOR-HIF-1α signaling pathway. Pharmacological inhibition of mTOR with rapamycin reversed YBX3-induced glycolytic activation, neuroinflammation, and neuronal injury. Collectively, these results identify YBX3 as a key regulator of ischemic brain damage through glycolysis-dependent mechanisms and underscore its potential as a therapeutic target for stroke.

secondary.title: Titanium dioxide nanoparticles induce neurotoxicity through PI3K/Akt-mediated mitochondrial apoptosis.
secondary.abstract: Concerns about chronic exposure to titanium dioxide nanoparticles (TiO2-NPs) have increased because of their widespread use in consumer products and subsequent environmental release. Previous studies have shown that TiO2-NPs exert neurotoxic effects and may contribute to Parkinson's disease (PD)-related neurodegenerative processes. However, the molecular mechanisms underlying TiO2-NPs-induced neurotoxicity remain unclear. We investigated these effects and their potential mechanisms in A53T α-synuclein transgenic mice and SH-SY5Y cells. Repeated oral exposure to TiO2-NPs for two months dose-dependently aggravated motor dysfunction and neuronal degeneration in the substantia nigra pars compacta at 1, 10, and 50 mg/kg body weight. In SH‑SY5Y cells, exposure to TiO2‑NPs for 48 h at 0.01, 0.1, 1, 10, 50, and 100 mg/L reduced cell viability in a concentration-dependent manner, impaired mitochondrial function, increased reactive oxygen species (ROS) production and promoted apoptosis. Western blotting showed that TiO2-NPs inhibited PI3K/Akt signaling and altered mitochondrial apoptosis-related proteins, including Bcl-2, Bax, cytochrome C (Cyt C) and caspase-3. The PI3K agonist insulin-like growth factor-1 (IGF-1) partly attenuated these changes. These findings provide mechanistic evidence for TiO2-NPs-induced neurotoxicity and may support the health risk assessment and safe application of TiO2-NPs.

secondary.title: Investigating the role of norepinephrine in regulating depression by a novel organic near-infrared fluorescent probe.
secondary.abstract: Depression is closely associated with alterations in concentration levels and release dynamics of a specific neurotransmitter, such as norepinephrine (NE), in the brain. Visualizing these dynamic changes is essential for understanding depression-associated neurotransmitter dysregulation. Herein, we developed a novel near-infrared fluorescent probe DIPCl-NE by employing a near-infrared fluorophore DIPCl-OH (Em = 689 nm) as the signal reporter and introducing a carbonothioate group as the recognition unit for selective NE detection. DIPCl-NE exhibits high sensitivity, excellent selectivity, good photostability, and effective tissue penetration capability. Using this probe, we visualized NE release dynamics in normal and CORT-induced depressive-like models and revealed that impaired NE exocytosis is associated with reduced mTOR phosphorylation levels. Pharmacological regulation of mTOR signaling further demonstrated its role in modulating NE release dynamics. Moreover, DIPCl-NE enabled visualization of NE alterations in mouse brains and revealed decreased NE availability in depressive model mice. This work provides a valuable chemical tool for monitoring NE dynamics and offers new insights into the relationship between mTOR signaling and depression-associated neurotransmitter dysfunction.

secondary.title: APOE4-AGE axis is linked to mtDNA release and cGAS-STING-mediated neuroinflammation in the aging brain.
secondary.abstract: Advanced glycation end products (AGEs) accumulate with aging and have been implicated in neurodegeneration, yet their relationship with the APOE4 genotype and downstream inflammatory signaling remains poorly understood. Here, we show that APOE4 is associated with greater age-dependent AGE accumulation and APOE glycation in the aging brain compared with APOE3 in animal models. These changes are accompanied by mitochondrial dysfunction and increased release of mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) into the cytosol, providing a potential trigger for innate immune activation. Consistent with enhanced innate immune signaling, APOE4 brains exhibit increased cGAS expression and phosphorylation of STING, TBK1, and IRF3, together with elevated type I interferon and pro-inflammatory responses. This activation is particularly prominent in microglia, as demonstrated by increased cGAS-DNA interactions and greater colocalization of cGAS signaling with Iba1-positive cells. APOE4 mice further display increased levels of cGAMP and IFN-β, as well as enhanced expression of pro-inflammatory cytokines and interferon-stimulated genes. Mechanistically, exposure of primary microglia to AGEs induces cytosolic mtDNA release and activates cGAS-STING signaling, whereas pharmacological inhibition of the receptor for advanced glycation end products (RAGE) attenuates these responses. Together, these findings identify an association between the APOE4-AGE axis, mitochondrial dysfunction, mtDNA release, and enhanced cGAS-STING-related inflammatory signaling in the aging brain, while the in vitro studies support a functional contribution of AGE-RAGE signaling to these responses in primary microglia.

secondary.title: Activation of mTOR pathway by human cytomegalovirus promoting host ribosomal protein expression by coordinated transcriptional and translational controls.
secondary.abstract: Human cytomegalovirus (HCMV) profoundly reprograms host transcription and RNA metabolism, yet its impact on transcription start site (TSS) regulation of host genes remains poorly understood. Here, we employed NanoCap Analysis of Gene Expression sequencing (NanoCAGE-seq) to investigate HCMV-driven changes in alternative TSS usage across the host transcriptome. We identified widespread TSS switching, with ribosomal protein genes (RPGs) emerging as a highly enriched category. Alternative TSS usage produced isoforms with distinct 5'untranslated regions (UTRs), thereby altering cis-regulatory elements that shape translational efficiency. Integrative transcriptomic and proteomic analyses revealed a paradoxical accumulation of RPG proteins despite transcriptional downregulation during infection. Using 5' Rapid Amplification of cDNA Ends (5'RACE), we characterized four RPGs of RPL4, RPS11, RPS23, and RPS24 that generated 5'UTR variants through alternative TSS usage. Notably, isoforms containing a 5'terminal oligopyrimidine (5'TOP) motif were significantly enriched, correlating with mTOR activation induced by HCMV. Functional assays with bicistronic reporter constructs in HEK293 cells and infection models in human embryonic lung fibroblasts demonstrated that the RPL4 5'TOP isoform exhibited enhanced mTORC1-driven translation compared with non-5'TOP counterparts. Importantly, RPL4 upregulation facilitated viral protein synthesis and boosted production of infectious virions. Together, our findings reveal that dynamic TSS switching of RPGs provides a simple, yet effective, mechanism for fine-tuning mTORC1-responsive translation. By co-opting host transcriptional and translational programs, HCMV enhances ribosome function to optimize the cellular environment for productive viral replication.

secondary.title: Ligilactobacillus salivarius NCU-41 reduces oxidative stress to ameliorate Parkinson's disease by regulating the AKT/Nrf2 signaling pathway.
secondary.abstract: A growing body of evidence suggests that the gut microbiota influences the onset and progression of Parkinson's disease (PD) by regulating oxidative stress pathways. However, existing evidence remains the phenotypic level, and high-quality research is still lacking regarding specific probiotic strains with clearly defined ameliorative functions and their precise underlying molecular mechanisms. In this study, high-throughput sequencing confirmed significant differences in the gut microbiota between PD patients and healthy individuals. Furthermore, fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT) from healthy individuals significantly improved motor dysfunction in PD mice, reduced α-syn aggregation (MP vs. M = 319.61 ng/ML vs. 507.84 ng/ML), alleviated neuroinflammation (reduced GFAP and IBA1 positive areas), protected dopaminergic neurons (increased TH expression), and optimized the structure of the gut microbiota, whereas FMT from PD patients exacerbated PD progression. Additionally, through correlation analysis, culturomics, and tryptophan metabolite analysis, Ligilactobacillus salivarius NCU-41 may improve PD by producing indole-3-lactic acid (ILA). Further validation through animal experiments demonstrating that supplementation with either NCU-41 or ILA alone significantly improved PD symptoms, though not as effectively as FMT from healthy individuals. Mechanistically, NCU-41 might activate the AKT/Nrf2 signaling pathway through its tryptophan metabolite (ILA), thereby enhancing the body's antioxidant capacity and ultimately alleviating PD. In summary, this study revealed that L. salivarius NCU-41 to activate the AKT/Nrf2 signaling pathway, thereby exerting a therapeutic effect on PD. These findings provide a deeper mechanistic basis for the potential application of this strain in the future treatment of PD.

secondary.title: Neuroprotective effects of chitosan nanoparticle-loaded orientin in a 6-OHDA-induced Parkinson's disease experimental model in rats.
secondary.abstract: PURPOSE: The present study investigated the neuroprotective effects of orientin, a natural flavonoid with antioxidant and anti-inflammatory properties, loaded into chitosan nanoparticles (CNPs-Orientin) in a unilateral 6-hydroxydopamine (6-OHDA)-induced rat model of Parkinson's disease. The study further evaluated behavioral performance, histopathological alterations, tyrosine hydroxylase (TH) immunoreactivity, oxidative stress, inflammatory cytokines, and apoptosis- and survival-related signaling proteins. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Seventy-two male Sprague-Dawley rats (220-260 g) were randomly assigned into nine experimental groups (n = 8/group): Control, Orientin, CNPs, CNPs-Orientin, 6-OHDA, 6-OHDA + L-DOPA, 6-OHDA + Orientin, 6-OHDA + CNPs, and 6-OHDA + CNPs-Orientin. Parkinsonism was induced by unilateral stereotaxic injection of 6-OHDA into the substantia nigra pars compacta. Drug treatments were initiated after lesion induction and continued for 14 consecutive days. Behavioral, histopathological, immunohistochemical, biochemical, and Western blot analyses were subsequently performed. RESULTS: 6-OHDA administration caused marked motor impairment, neuronal degeneration, reduced TH immunoreactivity, increased α-synuclein and Beclin-1 immunoreactivity, increased oxidative stress, elevated inflammatory cytokines, increased apoptosis-related protein expression, and suppression of antioxidant defense mechanisms. Treatment with CNPs-Orientin significantly improved behavioral performance, preserved TH-positive neurons, reduced α-synuclein-positive cell density and Beclin-1-positive DAB area, reduced neuronal degeneration, decreased MDA, TNF-α, IL-1β, IFN-γ, NF-κB, and Caspase-3 levels, while restoring SOD, GSH, Bcl-2, PI3K, Akt, and mTOR protein expression. Overall, CNPs-Orientin produced greater neuroprotective effects than free orientin alone. CONCLUSION: Chitosan nanoparticle-mediated delivery substantially enhanced the neuroprotective efficacy of the natural flavonoid orientin against 6-OHDA-induced dopaminergic neurodegeneration. The observed protective effects were associated with reduced oxidative stress, inflammation, apoptosis, and changes in PI3K/Akt/mTOR-related protein expression.

secondary.title: Effects and mechanisms of Stauntonia brachyanthera Hand.-Mazz against Alzheimer's disease through network pharmacology and experimental validation.
secondary.abstract: Stauntonia brachyanthera Hand.-Mazz. (SB), a traditional medicinal plant of the Dong ethnic group with nutraceutical applications, exhibits broad-spectrum pharmacological activity. However, the therapeutic effects and mechanisms of SB on Alzheimer's disease (AD) remain unclear. This study aims to investigate the neuroprotective potential and underlying mechanisms of SB against AD. We utilized network pharmacology and molecular docking to predict the active components, targets, and pathways of SB associated with AD treatment. Gene Ontology (GO) enrichment and Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes (KEGG) pathway analysis were further used to identify potential therapeutic targets and underlying mechanisms of SB in relation to AD. Then, the neuroprotective effects, neuronal differentiation-promoting activity and potential mechanism of key active components of SB on the main therapeutic targets were verified by in vitro experiments. The network pharmacological prediction results showed that the treatment of AD with SB was closely related to MAPK and PI3K/Akt pathways. Further experiments showed that the SB active component kaempferol (KMF) alleviated Aβ1-42-induced injury and promoted neuronal differentiation. Additionally, we found that KMF-mediated promotion of neuronal differentiation in N2a cells was dependent on the PI3K/Akt and MAPK pathways. In this study, we employed a combined computational-experimental approach to elucidate the neuroprotective mechanisms of SB against Alzheimer's disease. We further validated KMF as a key active component of SB that alleviates Aβ1-42-induced injury and promotes neuronal differentiation through the PI3K/Akt and MAPK pathways.

secondary.title: ADCY2 promoter hypomethylation in adolescents with borderline personality disorder: An RRBS study with targeted BSP replication.
secondary.abstract: BACKGROUND: Borderline Personality Disorder (BPD) is characterized by emotional dysregulation, impulsivity, and interpersonal instability. Although genetic and environmental contributions to BPD have been investigated, epigenetic correlates in adolescents remain poorly understood. The cyclic adenosine monophosphate (cAMP) signaling pathway is implicated in stress responsivity and emotion regulation, but its epigenetic variation in adolescent BPD remains understudied. METHODS: DNA methylation profiling was performed using Reduced Representation Bisulfite Sequencing (RRBS) in buccal epithelial DNA from adolescents with BPD (n = 15) and healthy controls (HC; n = 15). Differentially methylated regions (DMRs) were identified using metilene, a computational tool for detecting DMRs from bisulfite sequencing data, and subjected to Gene Ontology (GO) and Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes (KEGG) enrichment analyses. Associations between methylation signals and borderline personality features were examined. Adenylate cyclase 2 (ADCY2) promoter methylation was examined using targeted bisulfite sequencing PCR (BSP) in an independent cohort (BPD n = 5; HC n = 5). RESULTS: RRBS identified 7641 DMRs between BPD and HC, with enrichment in pathways related to neuronal signaling and synaptic organization. A hypomethylated DMR was detected in the ADCY2 promoter, a gene implicated in cAMP signaling. Lower ADCY2 promoter methylation was associated with greater clinical severity, including emotional dysregulation, borderline traits, anxiety symptoms, and self-injury behaviors (r=-0.71 to -0.83; all p < 0.0001). Hypomethylation of the ADCY2 promoter was replicated in the independent cohort. CONCLUSIONS: This exploratory two-stage epigenetic study suggests that ADCY2 promoter hypomethylation in peripheral buccal epithelial DNA is associated with core symptom dimensions of adolescent BPD. These findings support a role for cAMP-related epigenetic variation in BPD and warrant replication in longitudinal studies.

secondary.title: Pharmacological evidence suggesting the involvement of autophagy-related signaling in the cognitive effects of neuropeptide Y in an amyloid-β-induced model of Alzheimer's disease.
secondary.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Neuropeptide Y (NPY) exerts neuroprotective effects; however, its functional relationship with autophagy-related signaling pathways in AD-associated cognitive dysfunction remains insufficiently understood. Using an Aβ-induced rat model of AD, the present study evaluated the effects of NPY on learning and memory. Specifically, we examined whether pharmacological manipulation with 3-methyladenine and MHY1485 modifies the cognitive effects of NPY, providing an indirect behavioral-pharmacological assessment of processes potentially related to autophagy and mTOR signaling. METHODS: This experimental study was conducted on 88 male Wistar rats (200-250 g) randomly divided to 11 groups (n = 8 per group). An intracerebroventricular (ICV) injection of Aβ (2 µg/µl per rat) was used to induce the AD model. NPY (10 ng /µl), MHY1485 (an mTOR activator; 2 µM), and 3-methyladenine (3-MA; an autophagy inhibitor; 300 nmol, 30 nmol, and 3 µmol) were administered via ICV injection. Cognitive performance was assessed using the passive avoidance and Y-maze tasks. RESULTS: NPY administration significantly decreased time spent in the dark compartment (TDC), increased step-through latency (STL) in the passive avoidance task, and enhanced spontaneous alternation behavior in the Y-maze (P < 0.05). Importantly, administration of MHY1485 and 3-MA (300 nM), either alone or in combination, significantly attenuated the cognitive-enhancing effects of NPY (P < 0.05) CONCLUSION: NPY improved cognitive performance in an Aβ-induced rat model of Alzheimer's disease. Our behavioral-pharmacological findings suggest that autophagy-related signaling contributes to the memory-enhancing effects of NPY. Pharmacological modulation with 3-MA and MHY1485 provides functional evidence consistent with the potential involvement of Beclin-1- and mTOR-related signaling, although direct molecular confirmation warrants further investigation.

primary.title: Astrocyte-derived extracellular vesicle phosphorylated TDP-43 as a blood-based biomarker for amyotrophic lateral sclerosis.
primary.abstract: Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) is a fatal neurodegenerative disease characterized by central nervous system (CNS) neuroglial TAR DNA-binding protein 43 (TDP-43) pathology in ∼90-95% of cases. Non-invasive biomarkers are critically needed to reduce diagnostic delay, enable patient stratification, and assess treatment efficacy in clinical trials. Astrocyte-derived extracellular vesicles (ADEVs) represent promising CNS liquid biopsy biomarkers, given astrocyte involvement in ALS pathogenesis and the ability of ADEVs to cross the blood-brain barrier and carry TDP-43. Here, we assessed the diagnostic performance of TDP-43 and its hyperphosphorylated pathological form, phospho-Ser409 (pTDP-43), quantified in ADEVs, for distinguishing ALS cases from matched healthy controls. ADEVs were immunoisolated from whole blood (n = 76) and plasma (n = 86) across three ALS biorepositories/cohorts. ADEV quality and enrichment were validated in accordance with minimal information for studies of extracellular vesicles guidelines, and protein levels were normalized by ratio to tetraspanin cluster of differentiation 81 (CD81). Diagnostic accuracy was evaluated by logistic regression and random forest models with cross-validation, adjusting for age and sex across 100 random seeds. Plasma ADEV pTDP-43/CD81 ratio best predicted ALS case status, with a mean AUC of 0.89 (95% CI: 0.75-0.99) from logistic models, corresponding to a mean sensitivity and specificity of 87% and 89%, respectively, and a mean AUC of 0.86 (95% CI: 0.82-0.90) from random forest models. Although the specificity of ADEV pTDP-43 relative to disease mimics and associations with disease progression require further investigation, these findings support its potential as a biomarker candidate for ALS and for patient stratification in TDP-43-targeted clinical trials.

primary.title: Neuropathological and functional impact of astrocyte-derived extracellular vesicles in an aged model of Alzheimer's disease.
primary.abstract: Extracellular vesicles (EVs) are lipid-bound particles that transfer cargos between cells. While plasma neuronal-derived EVs (NEVs) from individuals with mild cognitive impairment (MCI) and Alzheimer's disease (AD) have been reported to exhibit high pathogenic potential, this study examined the impact of astrocyte-derived EVs (AEVs) in an aged AD mouse model. Plasma AEVs were isolated from cognitively normal control (CNC), MCI, and AD individuals using GLAST-based immunocapture and AEV size, purity, and tetraspanin were validated by flow cytometry, nanoparticle tracking, and super-resolution microscopy. AEVs pooled by clinical cohort were injected into the hippocampus of 6-month-old female PSAPP mice. Behavioral, biochemical, and neuropathological outcomes were assessed 6 months later. Rotarod assessment revealed significant impairment in motor coordination (p < 0.0001) in mice receiving MCI- and AD-AEVs compared with those receiving CNC-AEVs. While Morris water maze (MWM) also demonstrated that CNC-AEVs injected mice exhibited a trend toward increased target quadrant entries and faster escape latencies, these measures did not reach did not reach statistical significance. No overt changes were observed in the staining of amyloid plaque burden (6E10), and astrogliosis (GFAP). Immunoblotting of 82E1 and 22C11 confirmed Aβ/AAP levels remained similar across all injected mice, whereas increased cortical tau accumulation was observed in MCI- and AD-AEV injected mice. Cerebellar synaptic density (SY-38) remained unchanged. These findings suggest that while human-derived AEVs can precipitate early tau-related changes and motor coordination deficits, they do not significantly alter overall amyloidosis or astrocyte-reactivity at this time point. Further investigation is required to determine the viability of AEVs as biomarkers or therapeutic targets given the subtle nature of the observed structural pathology.

secondary.title: Exploring the potential of resveratrol-enriched cord mesenchymal stem cell derived exosomes in an in vitro Parkinson's model.
secondary.abstract: Parkinson's disease (PD) is characterized by the progressive loss of dopaminergic neurons in the substantia nigra and the pathological aggregation of α-synuclein (α-syn) into Lewy bodies and it is known as the second most prevalent neurodegenerative disorder. The pathogenesis of PD involves mitochondrial dysfunction, oxidative stress, impaired protein degradation, and neuroinflammation. Current therapeutic strategies are largely symptomatic and remain limited in their ability to halt disease progression. Resveratrol (Res) has been shown to mitigate oxidative stress, preserve mitochondrial integrity, and reduce α-syn aggregation in PD models due to its antioxidant and neuroprotective properties. Despite its promising therapeutic potential, its poor bioavailability and rapid metabolism hinder the achievement of the desired therapeutic effects, which calls for advanced drug delivery systems. Human umbilical cord-derived mesenchymal stem cell (hUC-MSC) exosomes (Exos) are nanoscale extracellular vesicles with intrinsic neuroprotective, anti-inflammatory, and regenerative properties. They represent a promising carrier system owing to biocompatibility and the ability to cross the blood-brain barrier. Since the isolation technique is a critical parameter affecting both Exos yield and therapeutic efficacy, the study initially focused on optimizing the isolation process through a comparative investigation of ultracentrifugation and commercial isolation kits. Exos obtained with the highest yield and optimal characteristics, were subsequently subjected to Res loading through the probe sonication method. After the physicochemical characterization of Res-loaded exosomes (Exo-Res), their therapeutic potential was evaluated in an in vitro PD model established by rotenone-induced neurotoxicity in SH-SY5Y cells. Cell viability, oxidative stress, mitochondrial function, and whole protein aggregation were comprehensively assessed. Exo-Res isolated with Kit-1 showed a smaller particle size (94.0 nm) with high homogeneity (PDI < 0.3), high yield (3.9 × 1011 particles/mL), and good entrapment efficiency (58.3%). It released Res in a sustained manner over 4 h. Our findings confirmed that Exo-Res significantly reduced whole protein aggregation mitigated oxidative stress, enhanced neuronal survival, and preserved mitochondrial function more effectively than either free Res or unloaded Exos. These results show that Exo-Res is a promising biocompatible nanocarrier-based therapeutic strategy for PD and possibly other neurodegenerative disorders, overcoming the key challenge of Res bioavailability while benefiting from the biocompatibility and therapeutic performance of exosomes.

secondary.title: Hypoxic microglia induce oligodendrocyte injury through lactate associated extracellular vesicles and toll like receptor four signaling.
secondary.abstract: Ischemic white-matter injury involves microglia-oligodendrocyte crosstalk, but the contributions of microglial metabolism and extracellular vesicles remain unclear. Primary rat microglia were exposed to 1% O₂, and conditioned-medium and Transwell models were used to assess their effects on oligodendrocyte-lineage cells. Hypoxia increased microglial ionized calcium-binding adaptor molecule 1 (IBA1) intensity 2.82-fold and extracellular lactate from 27.4 ± 2.3 to 48.5 ± 5.2 µmol/mL. Recipient-cell apoptosis increased from 9.1 ± 0.8% to 39.0 ± 1.3%, whereas myelin basic protein (MBP) fluorescence decreased from 1.00 ± 0.08 to 0.35 ± 0.05. Hypoxia-conditioned small extracellular vesicles (sEVs) were associated with a similar injury phenotype, while donor-cell oxamate treatment partially restored MBP fluorescence from 0.34 ± 0.05 to 0.82 ± 0.07. Hypoxia also increased recipient-cell Toll-like receptor 4 (TLR4) mRNA 5.6-fold and histone H3 lysine 18 lactylation (H3K18la) enrichment at the TLR4 promoter from 0.9 ± 0.1 to 7.1 ± 0.9; both were attenuated by oxamate. TAK-242 reduced apoptosis from 13.9 ± 0.9% to 7.3 ± 0.7% and increased MBP fluorescence to 1.82 ± 0.14. Human transcriptomic datasets showed directionally concordant metabolic, inflammatory, and myelination changes. These findings support a testable framework in which lactate-related microglial metabolism and hypoxia-conditioned sEVs are associated with TLR4-related inflammatory regulation, without establishing a single linear causal pathway.

secondary.title: Sacral Neural Crest-Derived Extracellular Vesicles Promote Pelvic Ganglion Repair Through Anti-Pyroptotic Effects Involving ANXA1-FPR2 Signaling.
secondary.abstract: Pelvic autonomic nerve injury is a major cause of postoperative bowel dysfunction, yet effective strategies for restoring damaged pelvic ganglia remain lacking. Here, we demonstrate that extracellular vesicles derived from human pluripotent stem cell-derived sacral neural crest cells (Sacral NC-EVs) promote pelvic neuroregeneration by suppressing oxidative stress-induced pyroptosis. In a rat model of major pelvic ganglion (MPG) injury, local administration of Sacral NC-EVs improved gastrointestinal motility and partially restored rectal neural innervation and epithelial barrier integrity. Mechanistic analyses showed that MPG injury increased oxidative stress and activated the NLRP3-caspase-1-GSDMD pyroptosis pathway, whereas Sacral NC-EVs attenuated both responses. Comparisons across EV sources showed that Sacral NC-EVs more effectively suppressed oxidative stress and pyroptosis and increased PGP9.5-positive and ChAT-positive neuronal areas than mesenchymal stem cell-derived EVs and vagal neural crest-derived EVs. Proteomic and functional analyses implicated EV-associated annexin A1 (ANXA1) as one contributor to the antioxidant and anti-pyroptotic effects of Sacral NC-EVs through FPR2 signaling. Collectively, our findings support Sacral NC-EVs as a promising cell-free strategy for pelvic neural repair by targeting the oxidative stress-pyroptosis axis.

secondary.title: SIRT5 Attenuates Traumatic Brain Injury by Preserving OPA1-Mediated Mitochondrial Fusion and Limiting Oxidative Stress.
secondary.abstract: AIMS: Mitochondrial dysfunction and oxidative stress are central pathological drivers of disease progression following traumatic brain injury (TBI). Sirtuin 5 (SIRT5), a predominantly mitochondrial NAD+-dependent deacylase, plays critical roles in mitochondrial quality control, redox homeostasis, and metabolic regulation. This study aims to define the upstream regulatory machinery controlling SIRT5 stability and to identify the downstream pathway linking SIRT5 to mitochondrial remodeling after TBI. RESULTS: In this study, we demonstrated that TBI promotes neuronal SIRT5 protein degradation via a synergistic regulatory mechanism involving USP7 and TRIM21. Using neuron-specific Sirt5 conditional knockout mice, we found that SIRT5 deficiency exacerbates TBI-induced mitochondrial dysfunction, oxidative damage, cerebral edema, and neurological deficits. SIRT5 regulates OPA1 expression through a MEF2A-dependent mechanism, thereby preserving mitochondrial structure and function and alleviating oxidative injury. The protective effects of neuronal SIRT5 overexpression were abolished in mice lacking Opa1 specifically in neurons, confirming that OPA1 is a critical downstream effector of SIRT5-mediated neuroprotection. Finally, rabies virus glycoprotein (RVG)-conjugated extracellular vesicles loaded with SIRT5 mRNA demonstrated both efficacy and safety in preclinical TBI models. INNOVATION: This study identifies the USP7/TRIM21-SIRT5-MEF2A-OPA1 axis as a novel regulatory cascade that governs the transition between adaptive and maladaptive mitochondrial remodeling after TBI, a concept with broad implications for acute brain injury and neurodegeneration. CONCLUSION: This study defines the USP7/TRIM21-SIRT5-MEF2A-OPA1 axis as a novel regulatory cascade that controls mitochondrial remodeling after TBI. SIRT5 acts through a MEF2A-dependent mechanism to maintain OPA1 expression and mitochondrial fusion, and its transient restoration via RVG-EV delivery of SIRT5 mRNA is a promising therapeutic strategy. secondary.title: TGF-β Inhibition Attenuates Tau Accumulation and Neurodegeneration in Progressive Supranuclear Palsy Patient-Derived Organoids.
secondary.abstract: BACKGROUND: Progressive supranuclear palsy (PSP) is a devastating 4-repeat tauopathy with no approved disease-modifying treatments. Recent evidence showed increased transforming growth factor-β (TGF-β) levels in PSP patient-derived ventral midbrain organoids (vMOs) and serum neuronally derived exosomes. OBJECTIVE: This study investigated whether TGF-β pharmacological inhibition could mitigate PSP pathology in vMOs. METHODS: Ninety-six vMOs were generated from induced pluripotent stem cells from two PSP-Richardson's syndrome patients and two healthy control donors (HCs). From day 60 to day 90, PSP organoids were (1) exposed to TGF-β receptor I inhibitor (SB431542); (2) exposed to recombinant TGF-β1, TGF-β2, and TGF-β3; or (3) untreated. At day 90, several tau species were assessed by immunoblotting; neurodegeneration was evaluated through TUNEL assay and immunofluorescence (tyrosine hydroxylase [TH], neurofilament light chain [NfL]); astrocytic activation (glial fibrillary acidic protein [GFAP]) marker was evaluated by immunofluorescence, and histopathological hallmarks were evaluated by immunohistochemistry. An HC-derived organoid subgroup was exposed to the treatment conditions to assess potential toxicity. RESULTS: At day 90, untreated PSP-derived vMOs exhibited increased phosphorylated tau levels (Ser396, Thr181, Ser202/Ser205 [AT8]) compared with HC-derived vMOs, dopaminergic neuron loss (reduced TH, increased NfL), and astrocytic reactivity (increased GFAP), along with PSP characteristic tau deposition. Tau hyperphosphorylation, neurodegeneration, and astrocytic reactivity were all markedly reduced in PSP-derived vMOs treated with TGF-β receptor I inhibitor. Conversely, exposure to TGF-β exacerbated these features. No toxic effects were observed in HC vMOs exposed to treatment conditions. CONCLUSIONS: Pharmacological inhibition of TGF-β signaling prevented key PSP molecular alterations in patient-derived organoids. These findings support further research and pave the way for future investigation of TGF-β-targeting strategies in clinical trials in patients with PSP. © 2026 The Author(s). secondary.title: Uropathogenic Escherichia coli escapes autolysosome exocytosis by inhibiting autophagosome-lysosome fusion.
secondary.abstract: UNLABELLED: Urinary tract infections (UTIs), predominantly caused by uropathogenic Escherichia coli (UPEC), represent a massive global health burden. UPEC infects bladder epithelial cells (BECs) via fusiform vesicles and then escapes into the cytosol, either establishing biofilm-like intracellular bacterial communities (IBCs), which protect UPEC from host immune clearance, or is captured by autophagy and expelled in a transient receptor potential cation channel 3-dependent manner from lysosomes. The mechanisms enabling UPEC to evade this exocytosis defense to establish IBCs remain poorly defined. Here, we reveal that UPEC nucleoside-diphosphate kinase (NDK) reduces the lysosomal exocytosis of BECs by inhibiting host cell autophagic flux in vitro and ex vivo. Mechanistically, NDK interacts with the small GTPase Rab7, thereby impairing autophagosome-lysosome fusion. Small interfering RNA interferes with Rab7 in 5637 cells and abrogates lysosomal exocytosis for UPEC. Thus, our results reveal a critical role for NDK in inhibiting autophagic flux, thereby favoring bacterial escape from host lysosomal exocytosis in UPEC. IMPORTANCE: Zhang et al. uncover a novel immune evasion strategy employed by uropathogenic Escherichia coli (UPEC), a leading cause of urinary tract infections. By demonstrating that the bacterial nucleoside-diphosphate kinase (NDK) directly targets the host small GTPase Rab7 to block autophagosome-lysosome fusion, this study reveals how UPEC resists lysosomal exocytosis-a key host defense mechanism that normally expels intracellular pathogens. Importantly, the authors validate that Rab7 interference via small interfering RNA reduces UPEC exocytosis, confirming the mechanistic necessity of this pathway. These insights fundamentally shift the understanding of UPEC pathogenesis from passive survival to active, molecular-level manipulation of host vesicular trafficking. Moreover, by identifying NDK-Rab7 interaction as a critical checkpoint in autophagic flux, this work opens new avenues for host-directed therapies that restore lysosomal exocytosis and enhance bacterial clearance, offering a promising alternative or adjunct to traditional antibiotics that face rising resistance.

secondary.title: Neuron-Derived Vesicular circMagi1 Restrains Vascular Repair After Ischemic Stroke by Promoting TRIM65-Mediated ANXA2 Degradation.
secondary.abstract: Circular RNAs (circRNAs) contribute to stroke pathogenesis, yet their intercellular functions within the ischemic neurovascular unit remain poorly defined. Profiling of plasma extracellular vesicles (EVs) revealed a higher abundance of circMagi1 in patients with acute ischemic stroke compared with healthy controls. This upregulation was recapitulated in the ischemic mouse brain, where cell-type-resolved analyses identified injured neurons as a primary source of circMagi1-containing EVs that accumulate in endothelial cells. Mechanistically, endothelial circMagi1 binds ANXA2 and enhances its engagement with TRIM65, thereby promoting TRIM65-mediated ANXA2 ubiquitination and proteasomal degradation and restraining angiogenesis. To therapeutically target this axis in vivo, treatment with siCircMagi1-RVG-EVs was initiated on post-stroke day 1 and maintained thereafter, while siTrim65-Ang2-EVs were introduced from either day 1 or day 9. Among the schedules tested, adding siTrim65-Ang2-EVs from day 9 was associated with greater neurovascular recovery than sustained circMagi1-targeted treatment alone or co-initiation on day 1. Together, these findings delineate a vesicle-mediated signaling axis linking neuronal injury to impaired vascular repair and support further evaluation of delayed TRIM65 inhibition during sustained circMagi1 suppression.

secondary.title: Extracellular vesicle α-synuclein topology reveals disease-associated conformers in brain and blood.
secondary.abstract: Parkinson's disease (PD), dementia with Lewy bodies (DLB), and multiple system atrophy (MSA) are unified by pathological α-synuclein (αSyn) aggregation, yet diverge in terms of the cellular distribution of pathology and clinical phenotype. Extracellular vesicles (EVs) have emerged as potential mediators or biomarkers of αSyn pathology, but whether their molecular constituents in the brain reflect disease-specific processes or conformations remains unknown. Here, we combined EV isolation, electrochemiluminescence, quantitative mass spectrometry and nanoscale single-vesicle imaging by direct stochastic optical reconstruction microscopy (dSTORM) to map the topology, epitope exposure and cellular origin of αSyn in EVs isolated from post-mortem PD, DLB, MSA, and healthy control (HC) brains and assessed the tractability of these molecular signatures in blood. Proteomics and immunoblotting of EV lysates isolated from human brains confirmed that they were highly purified and derived from neurons and glial cell subtypes. Across diseases, αSyn association with EVs exhibited distinct patterns: In PD and DLB, both total αSyn levels normalised to CD81 and the percentage of neuronal (L1CAM+) EVs with aggregated αSyn as detected by aggregate-preferring antibodies, were increased, whereas in MSA, aggregated αSyn was detected primarily in neuronal and to a lesser extent glial EV subpopulations without an increase in total EV-associated αSyn. Further epitope mapping by dSTORM identified a distinct αSyn conformational arrangement, as detected by antibodies against an epitope spanning αSyn residues 34-45, that was enriched on the surface of L1CAM+ EVs in MSA compared to PD. This N-terminal immunoreactive conformer was tractable in serum and enriched on the surface of L1CAM+ EVs from MSA compared to PD patients or controls. Collectively, our findings suggest that the epitope accessibility and topology of EV-associated αSyn proteoforms, rather than their abundance alone, discriminate synucleinopathy subtypes, offering a framework for a blood-based conformational stratification of these disorders.

secondary.title: Renal stress-associated extracellular vesicle signaling linked to lysosomal cathepsin D and NEK7-NLRP3 neuroinflammation.
secondary.abstract: Systemic exposure to neurotoxins such as 1-methyl-4-phenyl-1,2,3,6-tetrahydropyridine (MPTP) affects both the central nervous system (CNS) and peripheral organs; however, the contribution of peripheral organ stress to neuroinflammation remains incompletely understood. Here, we propose a peripheral-to-central signaling mechanism in which renal stress-associated extracellular vesicles (EVs) are linked to microglial inflammasome activation. Using computational and biochemical approaches, cathepsin D (CTSD) was identified as a molecular target of the MPTP metabolite 1-methyl-4-phenylpyridinium (MPP +). MPP + accumulated in renal tissue and was associated with lysosomal stress and tubular injury, accompanied by increased release of circulating EVs enriched with renal injury markers. Pharmacological inhibition of pepstatin A-sensitive lysosomal protease activity attenuated renal injury and EV release. MPTP exposure was also associated with blood-brain barrier disruption, potentially permitting circulating EV-associated signaling to influence the CNS. Plasma-derived EVs isolated under MPTP-treated conditions were associated with increased microglial activation, whereas pharmacological inhibition of EV biogenesis attenuated this response. Mechanistically, EV exposure was associated with inflammatory responses involving NIMA-related kinase 7 (NEK7)-NOD-like receptor family pyrin domain-containing 3-associated inflammatory signaling and IL-1β maturation. Consistent with these findings, NEK7 deficiency attenuated microglial activation and dopaminergic neuron loss in vivo. Together, these findings suggest that renal stress-associated EVs may be involved in linking peripheral stress to central neuroinflammatory responses. This study provides a tentative but verifiable framework for renal stress-EV-inflammasome communication in toxin-induced neuroinflammation.

secondary.title: Olive leaf-derived exosome-like vesicles attenuate neurotoxicity in an in vitro rotenone model of Parkinson's disease.
secondary.abstract: Parkinson's disease (PD) is a progressive neurodegenerative disease primarily characterized by dopaminergic neuronal loss, oxidative stress, mitochondrial dysfunction, and protein aggregation. Despite extensive research, current therapeutic options remain limited to symptomatic management, underscoring the need for neuroprotective strategies targeting disease pathology. In this study, we investigated the neuroprotective potential of exosome-like vesicles derived from olive (Olea europaea) leaves (Ole-ELVs) in an in vitro PD model induced by rotenone in SH-SY5Y human neuroblastoma cells. To evaluate the protective impact of olive leaf-derived ELVs, oxidative stress, cell viability, mitochondrial function, and protein aggregation were assessed by measuring reactive oxygen species (ROS) levels, 3-(4,5-dimethylthiazol-2-yl)-2,5-diphenyltetrazolium bromide (MTT) assay, JC-1 mitochondrial membrane potential staining, and Thioflavin S staining for α-synuclein aggregation. Our findings indicate that treatment with Ole-ELVs significantly attenuated rotenone-induced ROS production, preserved mitochondrial membrane potential, and reduced protein aggregation. Collectively, these results suggest that Ole-ELVs exert neuroprotective effects through antioxidative, protection against cytotoxicity, and mitochondrial-stabilizing mechanisms, offering a promising natural nanoscale therapeutic candidate for PD.
